KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p503#2/r1.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p503#2/r1.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p503#2/r1.claim: Test orphans’ judgment, dispositions, and property management before puberty; once sound judgment is clear, transfer their assets at puberty without delay.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p503#2/r1.anchor: واختبروا عقولهم وذوقوا احوالهم ومعرفتهم بالتصرف قبل البلوغ حتى اذا تبينتم منهم رشدا

KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p503#2/r2.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p503#2/r2.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p503#2/r2.claim: ‘Reaching marriage’ means puberty, marked by a wet dream, when one is ready for procreation; ānastum means ascertain, by extension from perceiving.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p503#2/r2.anchor: وبلوغ النكاح ان يحتلم لأنه يصلح للنكاح عنده ولطلب ما هو مقصود به

KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p503#2/r3.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p503#2/r3.speaker: أبو حنيفة وأصحابه
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p503#2/r3.claim: Abū Ḥanīfa and companions test by entrusting property for a youth to manage; sound judgment is knowing how to handle transactions.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p503#2/r3.anchor: فالابتلاء عند أبي حنيفة وأصحابه ان يدفع اليه ما يتصرف فيه حتى يستبين حاله

KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p503#2/r4.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p503#2/r4.speaker: ابن عباس
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p503#2/r4.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās defines sound judgment as mental uprightness and protecting property.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p503#2/r4.anchor: وعن ابن عباس الصلاح في العقل والحفظ للمال

KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p503#2/r5.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p503#2/r5.speaker: مالك والشافعي
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p503#2/r5.claim: Mālik and al-Shāfiʿī observe transactions and signs of piety; they define sound judgment as religious rectitude because sin damages property.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p503#2/r5.anchor: وعند مالك والشافعي الابتلاء أن يتتبع أحواله وتصرفه في الأخذ والاعطاء

KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p503#2/r6.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p503#2/r6.speaker: أبو حنيفة
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p503#2/r6.claim: If judgment is absent at puberty, Abū Ḥanīfa waits until age twenty-five: puberty at eighteen plus seven years of human change, then releases the property even without prudence.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p503#2/r6.anchor: ينتظر إلى خمس وعشرين سنة لأن مدة بلوغ الذكر عنده بالسن ثماني عشرة سنة

KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p503#2/r7.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p503#2/r7.speaker: أصحابه
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p503#2/r7.claim: Abū Ḥanīfa’s companions never release the property unless sound judgment appears.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p503#2/r7.anchor: وعند أصحابه لا يدفع اليه ابدا الا بإيناس الرشد

KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p503#2/r8.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p503#2/r8.speaker: النبي عليه الصلاة والسلام
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p503#2/r8.claim: The cited report says to command children to pray at seven, supporting the seven-year period.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p503#2/r8.anchor: لقوله عليه الصلاة والسلام 257 ( مروهم بالصلاة لسبع )

KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p503#2/r9.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p503#2/r9.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p503#2/r9.claim: The indefinite wording permits any demonstrated aptitude in commerce rather than requiring complete maturity.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p503#2/r9.anchor: معناه نوعا من الرشد وهو الرشد في التصرف والتجارة أو طرفا من الرشد

KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p505/r1.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p505/r1.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p505/r1.claim: The until-clause sets the limit of testing; puberty begins a conditional sequence, and transfer follows only if sound judgment is observed.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p505/r1.anchor: جعل غاية للإبتلاء وهي ( حتى ) التي تقع بعدها الجمل

KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p505/r2.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p505/r2.speaker: ابن مسعود
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p505/r2.claim: Ibn Masʿūd reads aḥsastum (‘perceived’) instead of ānastum.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p505/r2.anchor: وقرا ابن مسعود ( فإن أحسيتم ) بمعنى أحسستم

KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p505/r3.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p505/r3.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p505/r3.claim: The word for sound judgment is read with fatḥa or ḍamma on both syllables.

KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p505/r4.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p505/r4.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p505/r4.claim: The prohibition targets guardians spending lavishly or hastening to consume assets before orphans grow up and reclaim them.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p505/r4.anchor: مسرفين ومبادرين كبرهم أو لإسرافكم ومبادرتكم كبرهم تفرطون في إنفاقها

KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p505/r5.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p505/r5.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p505/r5.claim: A wealthy guardian abstains; a poor guardian may take a measured allowance as wages or a loan, a matter of disagreement.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p505/r5.anchor: والفقير ياكل قوتا مقدرا محتاطا في تقديره على وجه الاجرة أو استقراضا على ما في ذلك من الاختلاف

KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p505/r6.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p505/r6.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p505/r6.claim: Asked about an orphan in his care, the Prophet permits customary food without accumulating wealth or protecting one’s property with the orphan’s, and says discipline as one would a child.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p505/r6.anchor: وعن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم 258 ان رجلا قال له ان في حجري يتيما

KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p505/r7.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p505/r7.speaker: ابن عباس
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p505/r7.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās allows drinking an orphan’s camel milk if the guardian tends, waters, and treats the animals without harming offspring or overmilking.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p505/r7.anchor: وعن ابن عباس أن ولي اليتيم قال له أفأشرب من لبن ابله قال ان كنت تبغي ضالتها

KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p505/r8.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p505/r8.speaker: ابن عباس
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p505/r8.claim: Another report allows eating proportionately while working with the orphans and wearing only modest clothing.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p505/r8.anchor: وعنه يضرب بيده مع أيديهم فليأكل بالمعروف ولا يلبس عمامة فما فوقها

KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p505/r9.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p505/r9.speaker: إبراهيم
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p505/r9.claim: Ibrāhīm forbids linen and fine clothes, allowing only food that satisfies hunger and clothing that covers nakedness.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p505/r9.anchor: وعن إبراهيم لا يلبس الكتان والحلل ولكن ما سد الجوعة ووارى العورة

KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p506/r1.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p506/r1.speaker: محمد بن كعب
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p506/r1.claim: Muḥammad b. Kaʿb says the guardian eats sparingly, like an animal grazing, and treats himself as a hired worker taking only what is necessary.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p506/r1.anchor: وعن محمد بن كعب يتقرم تقرم البهيمة وينزل نفسه منزلة الأجير فيما لا بد منه

KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p506/r2.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p506/r2.speaker: الشعبي
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p506/r2.claim: Al-Shaʿbī allows food in proportion to work; another report compares it to carrion, permitting only necessity with repayment later.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p506/r2.anchor: وعن الشعبي يأكل من ماله بقدر ما يعين فيه وعنه كالميتة يتناول عند الضرورة ويقضي

KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p506/r3.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p506/r3.speaker: مجاهد
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p506/r3.claim: Mujāhid says take a loan from the orphan’s property and repay when able.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p506/r3.anchor: وعن مجاهد يستسلف فاذا أيسر أدى

KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p506/r4.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p506/r4.speaker: سعيد بن جبير
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p506/r4.claim: Saʿīd b. Jubayr allows surplus milk, riding, covering clothes, and food within limits; repay if able, and an insolvent guardian is excused.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p506/r4.anchor: وعن سعيد بن جبير إن شاء شرب فضل اللبن وركب الظهر ولبس ما يستره من الثياب

KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p506/r5.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p506/r5.speaker: عمر بن الخطاب
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p506/r5.claim: ʿUmar compares public funds to an orphan’s property: abstain if wealthy, eat moderately if poor, and repay when able; istaʿiff implies added abstention.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p506/r5.anchor: وعن عمر بن الخطاب رضي الله عنه إني انزلت نفسي من مال الله منزلة والي اليتيم

KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p506/r6.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p506/r6.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p506/r6.claim: Witness transfer to establish receipt, discharge the guardian’s liability, and prevent later dispute or denial.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p506/r6.anchor: ﴿ فأشهدوا عليهم ﴾ بانهم تسلموها وقبضوها وبرئت عنها ذممكم

KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p506/r7.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p506/r7.speaker: أبو حنيفة وأصحابه
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p506/r7.claim: Without witnesses, Abū Ḥanīfa’s school accepts the guardian’s claim on oath; Mālik and al-Shāfiʿī require proof, making witnesses protection from suspicion and liability.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p506/r7.anchor: ألا ترى انه اذا لم يشهد فادعى عليه صدق مع اليمين عند أبي حنيفة وأصحابه

KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p507/r1.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p507/r1.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p507/r1.claim: God suffices as witness to delivery and receipt, or as accountant; guardians should be honest and avoid falsehood.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p507/r1.anchor: أي كافيا في الشهادة عليكم بالدفع والقبض أو محاسبا فعليكم بالتصادق واياكم والتكاذب

MAWARDI-FULL:v1p452/r12.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v1p452/r12.speaker: author
MAWARDI-FULL:v1p452/r12.claim: Guardians should test orphans' minds, discernment, and religion before giving them their property.
MAWARDI-FULL:v1p452/r12.anchor: أي اختبروهم في عقولهم وتمييزهم وأديانهم

MAWARDI-FULL:v1p452/r13.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v1p452/r13.speaker: author
MAWARDI-FULL:v1p452/r13.claim: Reaching marriageable age means puberty, by consensus.

MAWARDI-FULL:v1p452/r14.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v1p452/r14.speaker: مجاهد والشعبي
MAWARDI-FULL:v1p452/r14.anchor: أن الرشد العقل , وهو قول مجاهد , والشعبي

MAWARDI-FULL:v1p452/r15.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v1p452/r15.speaker: السدي
MAWARDI-FULL:v1p452/r15.claim: Righteous maturity means reason and religious uprightness.
MAWARDI-FULL:v1p452/r15.anchor: أنه العقل والصلاح في الدين , وهو قول السدي

MAWARDI-FULL:v1p452/r16.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v1p452/r16.speaker: ابن عباس والحسن والشافعي
MAWARDI-FULL:v1p452/r16.claim: Righteous maturity requires religious uprightness and proper financial management.
MAWARDI-FULL:v1p452/r16.anchor: أنه صلاح في الدين وإصلاح في المال , وهو قول ابن عباس , والحسن , والشافعي

MAWARDI-FULL:v1p452/r17.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v1p452/r17.speaker: ابن جريج
MAWARDI-FULL:v1p452/r17.claim: Righteous maturity means uprightness and knowledge of what benefits the ward.
MAWARDI-FULL:v1p452/r17.anchor: أنه الصلاح والعلم بما يصلحه , وهو قول ابن جريج

MAWARDI-FULL:v1p452/r18.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v1p452/r18.speaker: author
MAWARDI-FULL:v1p452/r18.claim: Once maturity is established, guardians must hand over the property held for the orphans.
MAWARDI-FULL:v1p452/r18.anchor: يعني التي تحت أيديكم أيها الأولياء عليهم

MAWARDI-FULL:v1p452/r19.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v1p452/r19.speaker: author
MAWARDI-FULL:v1p452/r19.claim: Guardians must not consume the property extravagantly or hastily before the orphans grow up; excess means exceeding what is lawful.
MAWARDI-FULL:v1p452/r19.anchor: لا تأخذوها إسرافا على غير ما أباح الله لكم , وأصل الإسراف تجاوز الحد المباح

MAWARDI-FULL:v1p452/r20.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v1p452/r20.speaker: ابن عباس
MAWARDI-FULL:v1p452/r20.claim: Acting hastily means consuming an orphan's property before the ward grows up and can take control of it.
MAWARDI-FULL:v1p452/r20.anchor: وهو أن تأكل مال اليتيم تبادر أن يكبر , فيحول بينك وبين ماله

MAWARDI-FULL:v1p452/r21.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v1p452/r21.speaker: author
MAWARDI-FULL:v1p452/r21.claim: A wealthy guardian should abstain from using the orphan's property.

MAWARDI-FULL:v1p452/r22.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v1p452/r22.speaker: عمر وابن عباس وجمهور التابعين
MAWARDI-FULL:v1p452/r22.claim: A poor guardian may borrow from the orphan and repay it once able.
MAWARDI-FULL:v1p452/r22.anchor: أنه القرض يستقرض إذا احتاج ثم يرده إذا وجد

MAWARDI-FULL:v1p452/r23.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v1p452/r23.speaker: الحسن وإبراهيم ومكحول وقتادة
MAWARDI-FULL:v1p452/r23.claim: A poor guardian may take only enough food to satisfy hunger and clothing to cover the body, with no repayment.
MAWARDI-FULL:v1p452/r23.anchor: أنه يأكل ما يسد الجوعة , ويلبس ما يواري العورة , ولا قضاء

MAWARDI-FULL:v1p452/r24.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v1p452/r24.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
MAWARDI-FULL:v1p452/r24.claim: When Thābit ibn Rifāʿa's uncle asked what he could take from his ward, the Prophet permitted customary consumption without shielding his own property or hoarding the ward's wealth.
MAWARDI-FULL:v1p452/r24.anchor: قال : ( أن تأكل بالمعروف من غير أن تقي مالك بماله ولا تتخذ من ماله وقرا

MAWARDI-FULL:v1p452/r25.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v1p452/r25.speaker: أبو العالية والشعبي
MAWARDI-FULL:v1p452/r25.claim: A poor guardian may eat the orphan's produce and drink livestock milk, but should not take other property such as gold or silver.
MAWARDI-FULL:v1p452/r25.anchor: أن يأكل من ثمره , ويشرب من رسل ماشيته من غير تعرض لما سوى ذلك من فضة أو ذهب

MAWARDI-FULL:v1p452/r26.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v1p452/r26.speaker: ابن عباس
MAWARDI-FULL:v1p452/r26.claim: A guardian tending orphan camels may drink their milk after caring for strays, sick animals, troughs, and watering, without harming offspring or overmilking.
MAWARDI-FULL:v1p452/r26.anchor: فاشرب من ألبانها غير مضر بنسل , ولا بأهل في الحلب

MAWARDI-FULL:v1p452/r27.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v1p452/r27.speaker: عطاء
MAWARDI-FULL:v1p452/r27.claim: A poor guardian may take a fixed wage proportionate to the service provided.
MAWARDI-FULL:v1p452/r27.anchor: أن يأخذ إذا كان محتاجا أجرة معلومة على قدر خدمته , وهو قول عطاء

MAWARDI-FULL:v1p452/r28.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v1p452/r28.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
MAWARDI-FULL:v1p452/r28.claim: In a report about a man with no wealth who cared for an orphan, the Prophet permitted nonwasteful use without shielding one's own property with the ward's.
MAWARDI-FULL:v1p452/r28.anchor: فقال : ( كل من مال يتيمك غير مسرف ولا واق مالك بماله

MAWARDI-FULL:v1p452/r29.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v1p452/r29.speaker: author
MAWARDI-FULL:v1p452/r29.claim: Witness the transfer of the orphans' property so there is evidence that it was handed over.
MAWARDI-FULL:v1p452/r29.anchor: ليكون بينة في دفع أموالهم إليهم

MAWARDI-FULL:v1p452/r30.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v1p452/r30.speaker: author
MAWARDI-FULL:v1p452/r30.claim: God is sufficient as a witness or as the one who makes witnesses unnecessary.
MAWARDI-FULL:v1p452/r30.anchor: يعني شهيدا . والثاني : كافيا من الشهود

MUJAHID:v1p145/r1.author: Mujāhid b. Jabr
MUJAHID:v1p145/r1.speaker: مجاهد
MUJAHID:v1p145/r1.claim: Testing orphans means testing their understanding.
MUJAHID:v1p145/r1.anchor: عن مجاهد ﴿ وابتلوا اليتامى ﴾ يقول ابتلوا عقولهم

MUJAHID:v1p145/r2.author: Mujāhid b. Jabr
MUJAHID:v1p145/r2.speaker: مجاهد
MUJAHID:v1p145/r2.anchor: مجاهد ﴿ وابتلوا اليتامى ﴾ يقول ابتلوا عقولهم ﴿ حتى إذا بلغوا النكاح ﴾ يقول إذا بلغوا الحلم

MUJAHID:v1p145/r3.author: Mujāhid b. Jabr
MUJAHID:v1p145/r3.speaker: ابن عباس
MUJAHID:v1p145/r3.claim: A needy guardian may take enough food and clothing, drink surplus milk, and ride a surplus mount from the orphan's property; repay if later solvent, but there is no liability if unable.
MUJAHID:v1p145/r3.anchor: يأكل والي اليتيم من مال اليتيم قوته ويلبس منه ما يستره ويشرب فضل اللبن ويركب فضل الظهر

MUJAHID:v1p145/r4.author: Mujāhid b. Jabr
MUJAHID:v1p145/r4.speaker: مجاهد
MUJAHID:v1p145/r4.claim: He understands customary consumption as a loan from the orphan's property.
MUJAHID:v1p145/r4.anchor: مجاهد قال ﴿ فليأكل بالمعروف ﴾ يعنى سلفا من مال يتيمه

MUJAHID:v1p145/r5.author: Mujāhid b. Jabr
MUJAHID:v1p145/r5.speaker: ابن أبي رباح
MUJAHID:v1p145/r5.claim: The guardian may eat with the orphans in proportion to the service and work he provides.
MUJAHID:v1p145/r5.anchor: يضع يده مع أيديهم فيأكل معهم بقدر خدمته وقدر عمله

MUQATIL:4:6/r1.author: Muqātil b. Sulaymān
MUQATIL:4:6/r1.speaker: author
MUQATIL:4:6/r1.claim: Guardians should test orphans’ understanding until puberty and return their assets when they show religious uprightness and sound financial judgment; they must not consume assets wastefully or hasten to take them before maturity.
MUQATIL:4:6/r1.anchor: { وابتلوا اليتامى } ، يقول: اختبروا عقولهم، { حتى إذا بلغوا النكاح } ، يعنى الحلم،

MUQATIL:4:6/r2.author: Muqātil b. Sulaymān
MUQATIL:4:6/r2.speaker: author
MUQATIL:4:6/r2.claim: A wealthy guardian must abstain; a poor one may borrow reasonably and repay if able. Witness the transfer at maturity; God is the best witness. The verse concerns Thabit b. Rifaʿa, whose uncle held his inheritance.
MUQATIL:4:6/r2.anchor: نزلت فى ثابت ابن رفاعة وعمه، وذلك أن رفاعة توفى وترك ابنه ثابت،

NASAFI-FULL:v1p204#2/r1.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v1p204#2/r1.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v1p204#2/r1.claim: Test orphans' understanding and ability to manage property before puberty by letting them handle it; this supports a discerning child's permission to trade.
NASAFI-FULL:v1p204#2/r1.anchor: واختبروا عقولهم وذوقوا أحوالهم ومعرفتهم بالتصرف قبل البلوغ فالابتلاء عندنا أن يدفع إليه ما يتصرف فيه

NASAFI-FULL:v1p204#2/r2.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v1p204#2/r2.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v1p204#2/r2.claim: Reaching marriage means puberty, when a person becomes fit for marriage and its purpose of procreation.
NASAFI-FULL:v1p204#2/r2.anchor: أى الحلم لأنه يصلح للنكاح عند ولطلب ما هو مقصود به

NASAFI-FULL:v1p204#2/r3.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v1p204#2/r3.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v1p204#2/r3.claim: Anīsū means they have discerned sound judgment in handling business and transactions.
NASAFI-FULL:v1p204#2/r3.anchor: ﴿ فإن آنستم منهم ﴾ تبينتم ﴿ رشدا ﴾ هداية فى التصرفات وصلاحا فى المعاملات

NASAFI-FULL:v1p204#2/r4.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v1p204#2/r4.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v1p204#2/r4.claim: Once puberty and discernible judgment are present, deliver their property without delay; the syntax makes release conditional on judgment after puberty.
NASAFI-FULL:v1p204#2/r4.anchor: من غير تأخير عن حد البلوغ ونظم هذا الكلام

NASAFI-FULL:v1p204#2/r5.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v1p204#2/r5.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v1p204#2/r5.claim: The indefinite رشد either specifies commercial judgment or signals that even a little sound judgment suffices; this supports Abū Ḥanīfa's release of property at age twenty-five.
NASAFI-FULL:v1p204#2/r5.anchor: وتنكير الرشد يفيد أن المراد رشد مخصوص وهو الرشد فى التصرف والتجارة أو يفيد التقليل

NASAFI-FULL:v1p204#2/r6.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v1p204#2/r6.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v1p204#2/r6.claim: Do not consume the property wastefully or rush to spend it before the orphans grow up and reclaim it; the verbal nouns are circumstantial or purposive.
NASAFI-FULL:v1p204#2/r6.anchor: ولا تأكلوها مسرفين ومبادرين كبرهم فاسرافا وبدارا مصدران فى موضع الحال

NASAFI-FULL:v1p204#2/r7.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v1p204#2/r7.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v1p204#2/r7.claim: A rich guardian must refrain from the orphan's property; a poor guardian may take a carefully measured customary amount.
NASAFI-FULL:v1p204#2/r7.anchor: قسم الأمر بين أن يكون الوصى غنيا وبين أن يكون فقيرا فالغنى يستعفف

NASAFI-FULL:v1p204#2/r8.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v1p204#2/r8.speaker: إبراهيم
NASAFI-FULL:v1p204#2/r8.claim: Ibrāhīm defines a poor guardian's customary share as enough to fill hunger and cover nakedness.
NASAFI-FULL:v1p204#2/r8.anchor: عن إبراهيم ما سد الجوعة ووارى العورة

NASAFI-FULL:v1p204#2/r9.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v1p204#2/r9.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v1p204#2/r9.claim: When returning the property, obtain witnesses to prove receipt and avoid denial or a disputed oath.
NASAFI-FULL:v1p204#2/r9.anchor: بأنهم تسلموها وقبضوها دفعا للتجاحد وتفاديا عن توجه اليمين

NASAFI-FULL:v1p204#2/r10.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v1p204#2/r10.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v1p204#2/r10.claim: Ḥasīb means one who audits and reckons; alternatively, it warns the guardian taking a customary share not to exceed it because God will account for it.

SAMIN-DURR:4:6/r1.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:4:6/r1.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:4:6/r1.claim: Most grammarians make ḥattā a conjunction marking the endpoint of testing: test orphans until puberty, then give them their wealth if they show maturity.
SAMIN-DURR:4:6/r1.anchor: أشهرهما: أنها حرف غاية دخلت على الجملة الشرطية وجوابها، والمعنى: وابتلوا اليتامى إلى وقت بلوغهم واستحقاقهم دفع أموالهم بشرط إيناس الرشد،

SAMIN-DURR:4:6/r2.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:4:6/r2.speaker: الزجاج وابن درستويه
SAMIN-DURR:4:6/r2.claim: Al-Zajjaj, Ibn Darastawayh, and others instead make ḥattā a preposition, leaving idhā purely temporal rather than conditional.
SAMIN-DURR:4:6/r2.anchor: والثاني: وهو قول جماعة منهم الزجاج وابن درستويه أنها حرف جر، وما بعدها مجرور بها، وعلى هذا ف " إذا " تتمحض للظرفية،

SAMIN-DURR:4:6/r3.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:4:6/r3.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:4:6/r3.claim: On the majority analysis, idhā is governed by the sense of its answer: when they reach marriageable age mature, hand over their property.
SAMIN-DURR:4:6/r3.anchor: وعلى القول الأول يكون العامل في " إذا " ما تخلص من معنى جوابها تقديره: إذا بلغوا النكاح راشدين فادفعوا.

SAMIN-DURR:4:6/r4.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:4:6/r4.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:4:6/r4.claim: Some deny that idhā is conditional because its event is expected to occur; Sibawayh allows it to govern a condition in poetry, while al-Khalil argues from ‘when the dates ripen’ versus ‘if they ripen.’
SAMIN-DURR:4:6/r4.anchor: وأجاز سيبويه أن يجازى بها في الشعر، وقال: " فعلوا ذلك مضطرين "

SAMIN-DURR:4:6/r5.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:4:6/r5.speaker: الشيخ
SAMIN-DURR:4:6/r5.claim: The Shaykh explains that grammarians agree idhā usually carries conditional meaning; denials mean only that it does not govern jussive verbs.
SAMIN-DURR:4:6/r5.anchor: قال الشيخ: " وكلامه يدل على أنها تكون ظرفا مجردا ليس فيها معنى الشرط، وهو مخالف للنحويين

SAMIN-DURR:4:6/r6.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:4:6/r6.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:4:6/r6.claim: The author says there is no need to insert ‘the age’ or ‘the time’ of marriage: the wording means they become fit for marriage.
SAMIN-DURR:4:6/r6.anchor: والظاهر أنه لا يحتاج إليه، إذ المعنى: صلحوا للنكاح.

SAMIN-DURR:4:6/r7.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:4:6/r7.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:4:6/r7.claim: The fāʾ in ‘if you perceive’ answers idhā, and the fāʾ in ‘then hand over’ answers in.
SAMIN-DURR:4:6/r7.anchor: والفاء في قوله: { فإن آنستم } جواب " إذا " ، وفي قوله " فادفعوا " جواب " إن ".

SAMIN-DURR:4:6/r8.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:4:6/r8.speaker: ابن مسعود
SAMIN-DURR:4:6/r8.claim: Ibn Masud reads aḥastum, with one of the two identical sīn letters deleted from aḥsastum; the deletion is irregular, though some report it as a productive Sulaymi dialect rule.
SAMIN-DURR:4:6/r8.anchor: وقرأ ابن مسعود: " فإن أحستم " والأصل: أحسستم فحذف إحدى السينين،

SAMIN-DURR:4:6/r9.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:4:6/r9.speaker: أبو زبيد
SAMIN-DURR:4:6/r9.claim: Abu Zubayd’s poem supplies a parallel for deleting one sīn from a doubled verb.
SAMIN-DURR:4:6/r9.anchor: ويحتمل أن تكون العين أو اللام، ومثله قول أبي زبيد:

SAMIN-DURR:4:6#2/r1.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:4:6#2/r1.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:4:6#2/r1.claim: The indefinite rushdan indicates variety: any kind of maturity is sufficient.
SAMIN-DURR:4:6#2/r1.anchor: ونكر " رشدا " دلالة على التنويع، والمعنى: أي نوع حصل من الرشد كان كافيا.

SAMIN-DURR:4:6#2/r2.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:4:6#2/r2.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:4:6#2/r2.claim: Most read rushdan with ḍamma and sukūn; Ibn Masud and al-Sulami read fatḥa on both consonants, and some read two ḍammas.
SAMIN-DURR:4:6#2/r2.anchor: وقرأ الجمهور: " رشدا " بضمة وسكون، وابن مسعود والسلمي بفتحتين، وبعضهم بضمتين.

SAMIN-DURR:4:6#2/r3.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:4:6#2/r3.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:4:6#2/r3.claim: Ānasa means to sense or perceive; al-Farraʾ also glosses it as ‘find,’ and another view is ‘see.’

SAMIN-DURR:4:6#2/r4.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:4:6#2/r4.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:4:6#2/r4.claim: ‘Wastefully and hastily’ may be two objects of purpose, describing why guardians consume the property.
SAMIN-DURR:4:6#2/r4.anchor: قوله: { إسرافا وبدارا } فيه وجهان، أحدهما: أنهما منصوبان على المفعول من أجله أي: لأجل الإسراف والبدار.

SAMIN-DURR:4:6#2/r5.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:4:6#2/r5.speaker: ابن عباس
SAMIN-DURR:4:6#2/r5.claim: Ibn Abbas says guardians hurried to consume orphans’ wealth before the child grew up and took the property back.
SAMIN-DURR:4:6#2/r5.anchor: ونقل عن ابن عباس أنه قال: " كان الأولياء يستغنمون أكل مال اليتيم، لئلا يكبر، فينتزع المال منهم ".

SAMIN-DURR:4:6#2/r6.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:4:6#2/r6.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:4:6#2/r6.claim: Alternatively, both accusatives are circumstantial: the guardian acts wastefully and in haste.
SAMIN-DURR:4:6#2/r6.anchor: والثاني: أنهما مصدران في موضع الحال أي: مسرفين ومبادرين.

SAMIN-DURR:4:6#2/r7.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:4:6#2/r7.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:4:6#2/r7.claim: Badāran is the verbal noun of bādara; it may describe mutual haste by guardian and orphan, or a one-sided action with form III meaning form I.
SAMIN-DURR:4:6#2/r7.anchor: و " بدارا " مصدر بادر، والمفاعلة هنا يجوز أن تكون من اثنين على بابها،

SAMIN-DURR:4:6#3/r1.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:4:6#3/r1.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:4:6#3/r1.claim: ‘That they grow up’ may be the object of badār, as a verbal noun governs its object; the cited ‘feeding an orphan’ verse is parallel, though this government is disputed.
SAMIN-DURR:4:6#3/r1.anchor: أحدهما: أنه مفعول بالمصدر أي: وبدارا كبرهم، كقوله:

SAMIN-DURR:4:6#3/r2.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:4:6#3/r2.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:4:6#3/r2.claim: Alternatively, an implied ‘fearing’ makes the clause a purpose, with the object of badār omitted.
SAMIN-DURR:4:6#3/r2.anchor: والثاني: أنه مفعول من أجله على حذف، أي: مخافة أن يكبروا، وعلى هذا فمفعول " بدارا " محذوف.

SAMIN-DURR:4:6#3/r3.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:4:6#3/r3.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:4:6#3/r3.claim: The prohibition begins an independent sentence; coordinating it with the conditional answer is rejected because it would make the warning precede the event it depends on.
SAMIN-DURR:4:6#3/r3.anchor: وهذه الجملة النهيية فيها وجهان، أصحهما: أنها استئنافية، وليست معطوفة على ما قبلها.

SAMIN-DURR:4:6#3/r4.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:4:6#3/r4.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:4:6#3/r4.claim: The alternative coordination would make ‘do not consume’ follow the conditional result, contradicting ‘in haste lest they grow up.’
SAMIN-DURR:4:6#3/r4.anchor: لأن الشرط وجوابه مترتبان على بلوغ النكاح، وهو معارض لقوله { وبدارا أن يكبروا } فيلزم منه سبقه على ما ترتب عليه

SAMIN-DURR:4:6#3/r5.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:4:6#3/r5.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:4:6#3/r5.claim: Kafā is a verb, not a noun-like particle; its subject is the noun governed by the extra bāʾ.
SAMIN-DURR:4:6#3/r5.anchor: أحدهما وهو الصحيح أنه المجرور بالباء، والباء زائدة فيه وفي فاعل مضارعه

SAMIN-DURR:4:6#3/r6.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:4:6#3/r6.speaker: أبو البقاء
SAMIN-DURR:4:6#3/r6.claim: Abu al-Baqa says the extra bāʾ signals the imperative sense ‘be content with God.’
SAMIN-DURR:4:6#3/r6.anchor: قال أبو البقاء: " زيدت لتدل على معنى الأمر إذ التقدير: اكتف بالله ".

SAMIN-DURR:4:6#3/r7.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:4:6#3/r7.speaker: ابن السراج
SAMIN-DURR:4:6#3/r7.claim: Ibn al-Sarraj instead posits an implicit verbal-noun subject, ‘sufficiency,’ with bi-Allah as its semantic object; the author notes Basrans allow this only in poetic necessity.
SAMIN-DURR:4:6#3/r7.anchor: والثاني: أنه مضمر، والتقدير: كفى الاكتفاء، و " بالله " على هذا في موضع نصب لأنه مفعول به في المعنى،

SAMIN-DURR:4:6#3/r8.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:4:6#3/r8.speaker: الشيخ
SAMIN-DURR:4:6#3/r8.claim: The Shaykh rejects the hidden verbal-noun analysis because it leaves an omitted subject and makes an omitted noun govern its complement.
SAMIN-DURR:4:6#3/r8.anchor: لا يجوز عندهم إعمال المصدر مضمرا وإن عنى بالإضمار الحذف امتنع عندهم أيضا لوجهين

SAMIN-DURR:4:6#3/r9.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:4:6#3/r9.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:4:6#3/r9.claim: The author responds that if the subject is implicit, bi-Allah need not attach to that subject; it can attach to the verb, as Makki and al-Zajjaj suggest.
SAMIN-DURR:4:6#3/r9.anchor: بل نعلقه بنفس الفعل كما تقدم، وهذا القول سبقه إليه مكي والزجاج

SAMIN-DURR:4:6#3/r10.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:4:6#3/r10.speaker: الزجاج
SAMIN-DURR:4:6#3/r10.claim: Al-Zajjaj says the bāʾ enters the subject because the utterance conveys a command, but the author finds this contradictory about whether bāʾ is extra and who the subject is.
SAMIN-DURR:4:6#3/r10.anchor: دخلت الباء في الفاعل، لأن معنى الكلام الأمر، أي: اكتفوا بالله

SAMIN-DURR:4:6#4/r1.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:4:6#4/r1.speaker: ابن عطية
SAMIN-DURR:4:6#4/r1.claim: Ibn Atiyya says bi-Allah is nominative after an extra preposition and that the preposition gives a statement the force of a command; the author sees this as answering al-Zajjaj by making the bāʾ extra.
SAMIN-DURR:4:6#4/r1.anchor: وفي كلام ابن عطية " نحو من قوله أيضا، فإنه قال: " بالله " في موضع رفع بتقدير زيادة الخافض

SAMIN-DURR:4:6#4/r2.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:4:6#4/r2.speaker: ابن عيسى
SAMIN-DURR:4:6#4/r2.claim: Ibn ʿIsa says bāʾ joins the phrase as both subject-like and genitive attachment, reflecting that divine sufficiency exceeds ordinary sufficiency; the author says this needs thought.
SAMIN-DURR:4:6#4/r2.anchor: وقال ابن عيسى: " إنما دخلت الباء في " كفى بالله " لأنه كان يتصل اتصال الفاعل، وبدخول الباء اتصل اتصال المضاف واتصال الفاعل

SAMIN-DURR:4:6#4/r3.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:4:6#4/r3.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:4:6#4/r3.claim: Ḥasīban is most likely an accusative of specification, shown by its ability to take min; the alternative is a circumstantial accusative.
SAMIN-DURR:4:6#4/r3.anchor: فيه وجهان، أصحهما: أنه تمييز يدل على ذلك صلاحية دخول " من " عليه، وهي علامة التمييز.

SAMIN-DURR:4:6#4/r4.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:4:6#4/r4.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:4:6#4/r4.claim: Here kafā takes one object, omitted as ‘God suffices you.’
SAMIN-DURR:4:6#4/r4.anchor: و " كفى " هنا متعدية لواحد، وهو محذوف تقديره: وكفاكم الله "

SAMIN-DURR:4:6#4/r5.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:4:6#4/r5.speaker: أبو البقاء
SAMIN-DURR:4:6#4/r5.claim: Abu al-Baqa treats kafā as taking two omitted objects, ‘God suffices you against them,’ citing 2:137; the author says that is a different sense and questions the analysis.
SAMIN-DURR:4:6#4/r5.anchor: وقال أبو البقاء: " وكفى " تتعدى إلى مفعولين حذفا هنا تقديره: كفاك الله شرهم بدليل قوله:

QURTUBI-FULL:2:283#11/r4.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:2:283#11/r4.speaker: أبو الفرج الجوزي
QURTUBI-FULL:2:283#11/r4.claim: Al-Jawzi answers that God dignified wealth as human sustenance, prohibited entrusting it to the foolish, and ordered its return when orphans attain sound judgment.
QURTUBI-FULL:2:283#11/r4.anchor: وقد شرفه الله وعظم قدره وأمر بحفظه، إذ جعله قواما للآدمي وما جعل قواما للآدمي الشريف فهو شريف

QURTUBI-FULL:4:6/r1.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:4:6/r1.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
QURTUBI-FULL:4:6/r1.claim: The Prophet told Hind to take enough customary support for herself and her child; another report about a son asking to be fed indicates this applies to one unable to earn.

QURTUBI-FULL:4:6/r2.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:4:6/r2.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:4:6/r2.claim: Someone who has reached puberty is expected to seek a livelihood, since the verse sets reaching marriageable age as a threshold.
QURTUBI-FULL:4:6/r2.anchor: ومن بلغ سن الحلم فلا يقول ذلك لأنه قد بلغ حد السعي على نفسه والكسب لها

QURTUBI-FULL:4:6/r3.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:4:6/r3.speaker: عطاء والزهري
QURTUBI-FULL:4:6/r3.claim: Ata, al-Zuhri, and Kufan jurists say a wife cannot seek separation for her husband's poverty and should await payment as a court debt; they cite the respite for an insolvent debtor and the encouragement to marry the poor.
QURTUBI-FULL:4:6/r3.anchor:
هذا قول عطاء والزهري. وإليه ذهب الكوفيون متمسكين بقوله تعالى:
وإن كان ذو عسرة فنظرة إلى ميسرة

QURTUBI-FULL:4:6/r4.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:4:6/r4.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:4:6/r4.claim: Al-Qurtubi says the cited verses do not prove that position, while the report about the wife demanding support or divorce directly addresses the dispute.
QURTUBI-FULL:4:6/r4.anchor: ولا حجة لهم في هذه الآية على ما يأتي بيانه في موضعها. والحديث نص في موضع الخلاف

QURTUBI-FULL:4:6/r5.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:4:6/r5.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:4:6/r5.claim: An alternative takes the address as directed to the orphan's guardian, who should spend according to the child's means and needs; if the child has no property, the state and then closest Muslims, especially the mother, must care for him without reimbursement.
QURTUBI-FULL:4:6/r5.anchor: فالوصي ينفق على اليتيم على قدر ماله وحاله

QURTUBI-FULL:4:6/r6.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:4:6/r6.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:4:6/r6.claim: Speaking kindly means gentle address and reassuring promises; interpretations include prayers for the child and promising delivery of the estate once he is prudent.

QURTUBI-FULL:4:6#2/r1.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:4:6#2/r1.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:4:6#2/r1.claim: The command to test orphans addresses everyone and explains how their property is to be delivered; one occasion reported is the uncle of the orphaned Thabit ibn Rifa'a asking the Prophet what he may use and when to return the child's assets.
QURTUBI-FULL:4:6#2/r1.anchor: وقيل: إنها نزلت في ثابت بن رفاعة وفي عمه. وذلك أن رفاعة توفي وترك ابنه وهو صغير

QURTUBI-FULL:4:6#2/r2.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:4:6#2/r2.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:4:6#2/r2.claim: Testing means assessing character, judgment, and ability to manage property; a promising child may receive a small trial amount, with the full estate delivered if managed well and retained if mismanaged.
QURTUBI-FULL:4:6#2/r2.anchor: فإذا توسم الخير قال علماؤنا وغيرهم: لا بأس أن يدفع إليه شيئا من ماله يبيح له التصرف فيه

QURTUBI-FULL:4:6#2/r3.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:4:6#2/r3.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:4:6#2/r3.claim: Passing a test alone does not end guardianship: the verse also requires reaching marriageable age before the estate is released.
QURTUBI-FULL:4:6#2/r3.anchor: وليس في العلماء من يقول: إنه إذا اختبر الصبي فوجده رشيدا ترتفع الولاية عنه

QURTUBI-FULL:4:6#2/r4.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:4:6#2/r4.speaker: جماعة من الفقهاء
QURTUBI-FULL:4:6#2/r4.claim: Some jurists test a boy by letting him manage household expenses for a month or a small sum under supervision; if he shows sound judgment, the guardian hands over the estate and witnesses it.
QURTUBI-FULL:4:6#2/r4.anchor: وقال جماعة من الفقهاء: الصغير لا يخلو من أحد أمرين إما أن يكون غلاما أو جارية

QURTUBI-FULL:4:6#2/r5.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:4:6#2/r5.speaker: جماعة من الفقهاء
QURTUBI-FULL:4:6#2/r5.claim: For a girl, some jurists test household management, such as supervising cotton workers and judging the yarn; if prudent, her estate is delivered with witnesses, otherwise guardianship continues.
QURTUBI-FULL:4:6#2/r5.anchor: وإن كانت جارية رد إليها ما يرد إلى ربة البيت من تدبير بيتها والنظر فيه

QURTUBI-FULL:4:6#2/r6.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:4:6#2/r6.speaker: الحسن ومجاهد وغيرهما
QURTUBI-FULL:4:6#2/r6.claim: Hasan, Mujahid, and others say orphans should be tested in intellect, religion, and the growth of their assets.
QURTUBI-FULL:4:6#2/r6.anchor: وقال الحسن ومجاهد وغيرهما: اختبروهم في عقولهم وأديانهم وتنمية أموالهم

QURTUBI-FULL:4:6#3/r1.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:4:6#3/r1.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:4:6#3/r1.claim: Reaching marriageable age means puberty, as shown by the Quran's parallel phrase about children reaching puberty; puberty can be established by five signs, three shared by both sexes and menstruation and pregnancy specific to women.

QURTUBI-FULL:4:6#3/r2.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:4:6#3/r2.speaker: العلماء
QURTUBI-FULL:4:6#3/r2.claim: Scholars agree menstruation and pregnancy establish female puberty and trigger legal duties and rulings.
QURTUBI-FULL:4:6#3/r2.anchor: فأما الحيض والحبل فلم يختلف العلماء في أنه بلوغ، وأن الفرائض والأحكام تجب بهما

QURTUBI-FULL:4:6#3/r3.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:4:6#3/r3.speaker: الأوزاعي والشافعي وابن حنبل
QURTUBI-FULL:4:6#3/r3.claim: Al-Awza'i, al-Shafi'i, and Ibn Hanbal, with several Medinese authorities, set puberty at fifteen for someone without a wet dream; legal duties and penalties then apply, and Ibn al-Arabi prefers this limit.
QURTUBI-FULL:4:6#3/r3.anchor: قال الأوزاعي والشافعي وابن حنبل: خمس عشرة سنة بلوغ لمن لم يحتلم

QURTUBI-FULL:4:6#3/r4.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:4:6#3/r4.speaker: أصبغ بن الفرج
QURTUBI-FULL:4:6#3/r4.claim: Asbagh says fifteen is the best legal threshold because it is also the age at which a boy receives a share in military service and is allowed into battle.
QURTUBI-FULL:4:6#3/r4.anchor: إن حد البلوغ الذي تلزم به الفرائض والحدود خمس عشرة سنة

QURTUBI-FULL:4:6#4/r1.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:4:6#4/r1.speaker: ابن عمر
QURTUBI-FULL:4:6#4/r1.claim: Ibn Umar's report supports fifteen as an age threshold: the Prophet accepted him for the Trench at fifteen but had rejected him at Uhud at fourteen.
QURTUBI-FULL:4:6#4/r1.anchor: إذ عرض يوم الخندق وهو ابن خمس عشرة سنة فأجيز، ولم يجز يوم أحد لأنه كان ابن أربع عشرة سنة

QURTUBI-FULL:4:6#4/r2.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:4:6#4/r2.speaker: أبو عمر بن عبد البر
QURTUBI-FULL:4:6#4/r2.claim: For people whose birth dates are unknown, Ibn Abd al-Barr reports Umar's instruction to assess puberty by the appearance of pubic hair; Uthman used a similar sign when judging a boy who stole.
QURTUBI-FULL:4:6#4/r2.anchor: هذا فيمن عرف مولده، وأما من جهل مولده وعدة سنه أو جحده فالعمل فيه بما روى نافع عن أسلم عن عمر

QURTUBI-FULL:4:6#4/r3.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:4:6#4/r3.speaker: عطية القرظي
QURTUBI-FULL:4:6#4/r3.claim: Atiyya al-Qurazi says the Prophet inspected Banu Qurayza after Sa'd ibn Mu'adh's ruling, killing those who had grown pubic hair and sparing those who had not; he was spared.
QURTUBI-FULL:4:6#4/r3.anchor: عرض رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم بني قريظة فكل من أنبت منهم قتله بحكم سعد بن معاذ

QURTUBI-FULL:4:6#4/r4.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:4:6#4/r4.speaker: مالك وأبو حنيفة وغيرهما
QURTUBI-FULL:4:6#4/r4.claim: Malik, Abu Hanifa, and others set maturity by puberty rather than age; the text gives seventeen years, while Malik also cited a deepened voice and altered nostrils, and Abu Hanifa's best-known view is nineteen for boys and seventeen for girls.
QURTUBI-FULL:4:6#4/r4.anchor: وقال مالك وأبو حنيفة وغيرهما: لا يحكم لمن لم يحتلم حتى يبلغ ما لم يبلغه أحد إلا احتلم، وذلك سبع عشرة سنة

QURTUBI-FULL:4:6#4/r5.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:4:6#4/r5.speaker: داود
QURTUBI-FULL:4:6#4/r5.claim: Dawud says age never establishes puberty without a wet dream, even if someone reaches forty.
QURTUBI-FULL:4:6#4/r5.anchor: وقال داود: لا يبلغ بالسن ما لم يحتلم ولو بلغ أربعين سنة

QURTUBI-FULL:4:6#4/r6.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:4:6#4/r6.speaker: ابن القاسم وسالم
QURTUBI-FULL:4:6#4/r6.claim: Ibn al-Qasim, Salim, and several jurists treat pubic hair as a sign of puberty; another Shafi'i view uses that sign specifically in the Banu Qurayza ruling, while green stubble is not enough.
QURTUBI-FULL:4:6#4/r6.anchor: فأما الإنبات فمنهم من قال: يستدل به على البلوغ روي عن ابن القاسم وسالم

QURTUBI-FULL:4:6#4/r7.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:4:6#4/r7.speaker: مالك
QURTUBI-FULL:4:6#4/r7.claim: Malik says his operative practice follows Umar's report: someone on whom the razor passes is legally mature for punishment.
QURTUBI-FULL:4:6#4/r7.anchor: وقال ابن القاسم: سمعت مالكا يقول: العمل عندي على حديث عمربن الخطاب

QURTUBI-FULL:4:6#4/r8.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:4:6#4/r8.speaker: أصبغ
QURTUBI-FULL:4:6#4/r8.claim: Asbagh prefers imposing a penalty only when both pubic hair and puberty are established.
QURTUBI-FULL:4:6#4/r8.anchor: وأحب إلي ألا يقام عليه الحد إلا باجتماع الإنبات والبلوغ

QURTUBI-FULL:4:6#4/r9.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:4:6#4/r9.speaker: أبو حنيفة
QURTUBI-FULL:4:6#4/r9.claim: Abu Hanifa rejects pubic hair as either proof or indication of puberty.
QURTUBI-FULL:4:6#4/r9.anchor: وقال أبو حنيفة: لا يثبت بالإنبات حكم، وليس هو ببلوغ ولا دلالة على البلوغ

QURTUBI-FULL:4:6#4/r10.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:4:6#4/r10.speaker: الزهري وعطاء
QURTUBI-FULL:4:6#4/r10.claim: Al-Zuhri, Ata, al-Shafi'i, and some Malikis say no penalty applies before a wet dream, apparently assigning no legal force to age or pubic hair.
QURTUBI-FULL:4:6#4/r10.anchor: وقال الزهري وعطاء: لا حد على من لم يحتلم وهو قول الشافعي

QURTUBI-FULL:4:6#4/r11.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:4:6#4/r11.speaker: ابن العربي
QURTUBI-FULL:4:6#4/r11.claim: Ibn al-Arabi argues that if the Prophet's fifteen-year ruling is not evidence, other proposed ages are unsupported; jurists should use both age and pubic hair, which the Prophet explicitly recognized.
QURTUBI-FULL:4:6#4/r11.anchor: إذا لم يكن حديث ابن عمر دليلا في السن فكل عدد يذكرونه من السنين فإنه دعوى

QURTUBI-FULL:4:6#5/r1.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:4:6#5/r1.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:4:6#5/r1.claim: Al-Qurtubi notes that Ibn al-Arabi took the opposite position in al-Anfal, reading Ibn Umar's report as distinguishing those able to fight and receive spoils from dependants; Umar ibn Abd al-Aziz understood it similarly.
QURTUBI-FULL:4:6#5/r1.anchor: هذا قوله هنا، وقال في سورة الأنفال عكسه إذ لم يعرج على حديث ابن عمر هناك

QURTUBI-FULL:4:6#5/r2.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:4:6#5/r2.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:4:6#5/r2.claim: Anistu means perceived or saw, as in Moses seeing a fire; al-Azhari explains the idiom as looking to see whether anyone is there, and al-Nabigha's wild bull poem illustrates watchful looking.
QURTUBI-FULL:4:6#5/r2.anchor:
أي أبصرتم ورأيتم ومنه قوله تعالى
آنس من جانب الطور نارا

QURTUBI-FULL:4:6#5/r3.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:4:6#5/r3.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:4:6#5/r3.claim: The verb can also mean sensed, found, or knew; its underlying sense is seeing.
QURTUBI-FULL:4:6#5/r3.anchor: وقيل: آنست وأحسست ووجدت بمعنى واحد ومنه قوله تعالى: { فإن آنستم منهم رشدا } أي علمتم

QURTUBI-FULL:4:6#5/r4.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:4:6#5/r4.speaker: السلمي وعيسى والثقفي وابن مسعود
QURTUBI-FULL:4:6#5/r4.claim: The common reading has rushdan with a damma on ra and silent shin; al-Sulami, Isa, al-Thaqafi, and Ibn Masud read it with both vowels open, two dialectal forms and possible verbal nouns.
QURTUBI-FULL:4:6#5/r4.anchor: وقراءة العامة «رشدا» بضم الراء وسكون الشين. وقرأ السلمي وعيسى والثقفي وابن مسعود رضي الله عنهم «رشدا» بفتح الراء والشين

QURTUBI-FULL:4:6#5/r5.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:4:6#5/r5.speaker: الحسن وقتادة وغيرهما
QURTUBI-FULL:4:6#5/r5.claim: Hasan, Qatada, and others interpret rushd as soundness of intellect and religion.
QURTUBI-FULL:4:6#5/r5.anchor: فقال الحسن وقتادة وغيرهما: صلاحا في العقل والدين

QURTUBI-FULL:4:6#5/r6.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:4:6#5/r6.speaker: ابن عباس والسدي والثوري
QURTUBI-FULL:4:6#5/r6.claim: Ibn Abbas, al-Suddi, and al-Thawri define sound judgment as competence of mind and preservation of wealth.
QURTUBI-FULL:4:6#5/r6.anchor: وقال ابن عباس والسدي والثوري: صلاحا في العقل وحفظ المال

QURTUBI-FULL:4:6#5/r7.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:4:6#5/r7.speaker: سعيد بن جبير والشعبي
QURTUBI-FULL:4:6#5/r7.claim: Sa'id ibn Jubayr and al-Sha'bi say even an old person should not receive an orphan's estate until prudence is observed; al-Dahhak likewise withholds it even at a hundred absent sound management.
QURTUBI-FULL:4:6#5/r7.anchor: قال سعيد بن جبير والشعبي: إن الرجل ليأخذ بلحيته وما بلغ رشده فلا يدفع إلى اليتيم ماله

QURTUBI-FULL:4:6#5/r8.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:4:6#5/r8.speaker: مجاهد
QURTUBI-FULL:4:6#5/r8.claim: Mujahid says rushd refers specifically to intellect.
QURTUBI-FULL:4:6#5/r8.anchor: وقال مجاهد: «رشدا» يعني في العقل خاصة

QURTUBI-FULL:4:6#5/r9.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:4:6#5/r9.speaker: أكثر العلماء
QURTUBI-FULL:4:6#5/r9.claim: Most scholars, including Malik, say sound judgment follows puberty; a person who remains imprudent stays under guardianship even when old.
QURTUBI-FULL:4:6#5/r9.anchor: وأكثر العلماء على أن الرشد لا يكون إلا بعد البلوغ

QURTUBI-FULL:4:6#5/r10.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:4:6#5/r10.speaker: أبو حنيفة وزفر بن الهذيل والنخعي
QURTUBI-FULL:4:6#5/r10.claim: Abu Hanifa, Zufar, and al-Nakha'i say a free adult cannot be placed under guardianship once he reaches manhood, even if profligate, so long as he is rational.
QURTUBI-FULL:4:6#5/r10.anchor: لا يحجر على الحر البالغ إذا بلغ مبلغ الرجال، ولو كان أفسق الناس وأشدهم تبذيرا

QURTUBI-FULL:4:6#6/r1.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:4:6#6/r1.speaker: قتادة
QURTUBI-FULL:4:6#6/r1.claim: Qatada transmits the case of Habban ibn Munqidh, whose weak commercial judgment prompted a request for interdiction; the Prophet instead told him to state that there was no fraud and that he had three days to withdraw.
QURTUBI-FULL:4:6#6/r1.anchor: أن حبان بن منقذ كان يبتاع وفي عقدته ضعف، فقيل: يا رسول الله احجر عليه

QURTUBI-FULL:4:6#6/r2.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:4:6#6/r2.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:4:6#6/r2.claim: The case does not prove that guardianship is forbidden, because it was specific to Habban, as al-Qurtubi explained under al-Baqara.
QURTUBI-FULL:4:6#6/r2.anchor: وهذا لا حجة لهم فيه لأنه مخصوص بذلك على ما بيناه في البقرة

QURTUBI-FULL:4:6#7/r1.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:4:6#7/r1.speaker: الشافعي
QURTUBI-FULL:4:6#7/r1.claim: Al-Shafi'i interdicts someone who corrupts both wealth and religion or wealth alone; if religion is corrupt but wealth managed, one view interdicts him and another does not.
QURTUBI-FULL:4:6#7/r1.anchor: إن كان مفسدا لماله ودينه، أو كان مفسدا لماله دون دينه حجر عليه

QURTUBI-FULL:4:6#7/r2.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:4:6#7/r2.speaker: أبو العباس بن شريح
QURTUBI-FULL:4:6#7/r2.claim: Ibn Shurayh chooses the Shafi'i view that a person who misuses religion but manages wealth should still be interdicted.
QURTUBI-FULL:4:6#7/r2.anchor: أحدهما يحجر عليه وهو اختيار أبي العباس بن شريح

QURTUBI-FULL:4:6#7/r3.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:4:6#7/r3.speaker: أبو إسحاق المروزي
QURTUBI-FULL:4:6#7/r3.claim: Al-Maruzi chooses not to interdict someone who is religiously corrupt but manages wealth; al-Qurtubi calls this the apparent Shafi'i position.
QURTUBI-FULL:4:6#7/r3.anchor: والثاني لا حجر عليه وهو اختيار أبي إسحاق المروزي، والأظهر من مذهب الشافعي

QURTUBI-FULL:4:6#7/r4.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:4:6#7/r4.speaker: الثعلبي
QURTUBI-FULL:4:6#7/r4.claim: Al-Tha'labi attributes the permissibility of interdicting a spendthrift to Uthman, Ali, al-Zubayr, Aisha, Ibn Abbas, Abd Allah ibn Ja'far, Shurayh, and many jurists, and reports a claim of consensus.
QURTUBI-FULL:4:6#7/r4.anchor: وهذا الذي ذكرناه من الحجر على السفيه قول عثمان وعلي والزبير وعائشة وابن عباس

QURTUBI-FULL:4:6#7/r5.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:4:6#7/r5.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:4:6#7/r5.claim: Property is delivered only when both sound judgment and puberty are present; most jurists agree, while Abu Hanifa, Zufar, and al-Nakha'i release a person at twenty-five without requiring sound judgment.
QURTUBI-FULL:4:6#7/r5.anchor:
دفع المال يكون بشرطين: إيناس الرشد
 والبلوغ، فإن وجد أحدهما دون الآخر لم يجز تسليم المال

QURTUBI-FULL:4:6#7/r6.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:4:6#7/r6.speaker: علماؤنا
QURTUBI-FULL:4:6#7/r6.claim: Maliki scholars require a girl to have consummated marriage after puberty before testing her judgment, reasoning that seclusion limits her experience; men encounter public dealings from childhood.
QURTUBI-FULL:4:6#7/r6.anchor: إلا أن علماءنا شرطوا في الجارية دخول الزوج بها مع البلوغ

QURTUBI-FULL:4:6#7/r7.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:4:6#7/r7.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:4:6#7/r7.claim: Al-Qurtubi prefers al-Shafi'i's view that intercourse itself adds nothing to a woman's judgment if she already understands affairs and manages her wealth.
QURTUBI-FULL:4:6#7/r7.anchor: وما قاله الشافعي أصوب فإن نفس الوطء بإدخال الحشفة لا يزيدها في رشدها

QURTUBI-FULL:4:6#7/r8.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:4:6#7/r8.speaker: ابن العربي
QURTUBI-FULL:4:6#7/r8.claim: Ibn al-Arabi reports Maliki waiting periods of five to seven years for a girl with a father and one year for an orphan, but says these limits lack evidence and are difficult to define; the Quranic criterion is demonstrated judgment suited to each person.
QURTUBI-FULL:4:6#7/r8.anchor: وليس في هذا كله دليل، وتحديد الأعوام في ذات الأب عسير وأعسر منه تحديد العام في اليتيمة

QURTUBI-FULL:4:6#7/r9.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:4:6#7/r9.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:4:6#7/r9.claim: Al-Qurtubi criticizes Abu Hanifa's grandfather rationale and Abu Bakr al-Razi's argument from two verses: unrestricted wording must, by agreement among legal theorists, be read with the qualified wording.
QURTUBI-FULL:4:6#7/r9.anchor: فإن هذا من باب المطلق والمقيد، والمطلق يرد إلى المقيد باتفاق أهل الأصول

QURTUBI-FULL:4:6#8/r1.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:4:6#8/r1.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:4:6#8/r1.claim: Once a girl is prudent, contracts made during the waiting period are treated either as void until then or as valid only when sound judgment is shown; after it, they are accepted unless folly appears.
QURTUBI-FULL:4:6#8/r1.anchor: واختلفوا فيما فعلته ذات الأب في تلك المدة فقيل: هو محمول على الرد لبقاء الحجر

QURTUBI-FULL:4:6#8/r2.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:4:6#8/r2.speaker: ابن عطية
QURTUBI-FULL:4:6#8/r2.claim: Views differ on whether a guardian must obtain a judge's confirmation before release; Ibn Atiyya says guardians today should, given collusion and false declarations of a ward's prudence.
QURTUBI-FULL:4:6#8/r2.anchor: والصواب في أوصياء زماننا ألا يستغني عن رفعه إلى السلطان وثبوت الرشد عنده

QURTUBI-FULL:4:6#8/r3.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:4:6#8/r3.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:4:6#8/r3.claim: Malik and one Shafi'i view restore guardianship if a released person becomes wasteful; Abu Hanifa says it cannot return, but al-Qurtubi cites the Quran's protection of wealth and its provision for a guardian when a debtor becomes foolish or weak.
QURTUBI-FULL:4:6#8/r3.anchor: ثم عاد إلى السفه بظهور تبذير وقلة تدبير عاد إليه الحجر عندنا

QURTUBI-FULL:4:6#8/r4.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:4:6#8/r4.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:4:6#8/r4.claim: A guardian may manage an orphan's estate as a father would: trade, pay zakat and obligations, cover damages and parents' support, arrange marriage, pay a dowry, acquire a concubine, and settle claims in the ward's interest.
QURTUBI-FULL:4:6#8/r4.anchor: ويجوز للوصي أن يصنع في مال اليتيم ما كان للأب أن يصنعه من تجارة وإبضاع وشراء وبيع

QURTUBI-FULL:4:6#8/r5.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:4:6#8/r5.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:4:6#8/r5.claim: A guardian who pays some creditors from an estate is not liable if funds sufficient for the remaining debts are later lost; if he knowingly distributes the whole estate despite other debts, he must make up the other creditors' shares.
QURTUBI-FULL:4:6#8/r5.anchor: فإن كان عالما بالدين الباقي أو كان الميت معروفا بالدين الباقي ضمن الوصي لهؤلاء الغرماء

QURTUBI-FULL:4:6#8/r6.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:4:6#8/r6.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:4:6#8/r6.claim: A guardian who pays a deceased person's debt without witnesses is liable; if payment was witnessed but the witnesses later die after a long time, he is not liable.
QURTUBI-FULL:4:6#8/r6.anchor: وإذا دفع الوصي دين الميت بغير إشهاد ضمن

QURTUBI-FULL:4:6#9/r1.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:4:6#9/r1.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:4:6#9/r1.claim: Al-Qurtubi points back to al-Baqara 2:220 for fuller rulings on guardians' spending and other fiduciary duties.
QURTUBI-FULL:4:6#9/r1.anchor: من أحكام الوصي في الإنفاق وغيره ما فيه كفاية

QURTUBI-FULL:4:6#9/r2.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:4:6#9/r2.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:4:6#9/r2.claim: The prohibition does not imply that non-extravagant consumption is allowed; it forbids consuming the orphan's property except what is specifically permitted. Israf means excess or transgression.
QURTUBI-FULL:4:6#9/r2.anchor: ليس يريد أن أكل ما لهم من غير إسراف جائز، فيكون له دليل خطاب

QURTUBI-FULL:4:6#9/r3.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:4:6#9/r3.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:4:6#9/r3.claim: The Arabic word israf is explained as excess, crossing a limit, erroneous spending, waste, or heedlessness; poems illustrate the word's usage.
QURTUBI-FULL:4:6#9/r3.anchor: والإسراف في اللغة الإفراط ومجاوزة الحد

QURTUBI-FULL:4:6#9/r4.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:4:6#9/r4.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:4:6#9/r4.claim: Badaran means rushing to consume before an orphan reaches maturity; grammatically it is coordinated with israfan, and an yakbaru is governed by badaran.
QURTUBI-FULL:4:6#9/r4.anchor: وهو معطوف على «إسرافا» و { أن يكبروا } في موضع نصب ب «بدارا»

QURTUBI-FULL:4:6#9/r5.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:4:6#9/r5.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:4:6#9/r5.claim: A wealthy guardian must refrain from the orphan's funds, while a poor guardian may consume customary support; isti'faf means abstaining, as in the command to unmarried people.
QURTUBI-FULL:4:6#9/r5.anchor:
والاستعفاف عن الشيء تركه. ومنه قوله تعالى:
وليستعفف الذين لا يجدون نكاحا

QURTUBI-FULL:4:6#9/r6.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:4:6#9/r6.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
QURTUBI-FULL:4:6#9/r6.claim: A poor guardian who has an orphan may consume from the child's assets only without excess, waste, or accumulating principal.
QURTUBI-FULL:4:6#9/r6.anchor: كل من مال يتيمك غير مسرف ولا مباذر ولا متأثل

QURTUBI-FULL:4:6#9/r7.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:4:6#9/r7.speaker: عائشة
QURTUBI-FULL:4:6#9/r7.claim: Aisha says the allowance applies to a needy guardian who cares for and improves the orphan's affairs; one narration limits it proportionately to the estate.
QURTUBI-FULL:4:6#9/r7.anchor: نزلت في ولي اليتيم الذي يقوم عليه ويصلحه إذا كان محتاجا جاز أن يأكل منه

QURTUBI-FULL:4:6#9/r8.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:4:6#9/r8.speaker: ربيعة ويحيى بن سعيد
QURTUBI-FULL:4:6#9/r8.claim: Rabi'a and Yahya ibn Sa'id instead take the verse to mean that the orphan receives support according to whether his own assets are ample or limited; al-Qurtubi says the majority view is correct because the child cannot manage his money.
QURTUBI-FULL:4:6#9/r8.anchor: وقال بعضهم: المراد اليتيم إن كان غنيا وسع عليه وأعف عن ماله، وإن كان فقيرا أنفق عليه بقدره

QURTUBI-FULL:4:6#9/r9.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:4:6#9/r9.speaker: عمر بن الخطاب وابن عباس وعبيدة وابن جبير والشعبي ومجاهد وأبو العالية
QURTUBI-FULL:4:6#9/r9.claim: One view lets an impoverished guardian borrow customary support and repay it when solvent; Umar compared his use of public funds to a guardian's use of an orphan's property.
QURTUBI-FULL:4:6#9/r9.anchor: فقال قوم: هو القرض إذا احتاج ويقضي إذا أيسر، قاله عمربن الخطاب

QURTUBI-FULL:4:6#10/r1.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:4:6#10/r1.speaker: أبو العالية
QURTUBI-FULL:4:6#10/r1.claim: Abu al-Aliya explicitly interprets customary consumption as a loan, citing the command to witness the return of the assets.
QURTUBI-FULL:4:6#10/r1.anchor: ومن كان فقيرا فليأكل بالمعروف } قال: قرضا ثم تلا { فإذا دفعتم إليهم أموالهم فأشهدوا عليهم

QURTUBI-FULL:4:6#10/r2.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:4:6#10/r2.speaker: إبراهيم وعطاء والحسن البصري والنخعي وقتادة
QURTUBI-FULL:4:6#10/r2.claim: A second view says a poor guardian owes no repayment because modest food and clothing are compensation from God for responsible care; luxury clothing is excluded, and the jurists support it by analogy to an imam's stipend.
QURTUBI-FULL:4:6#10/r2.anchor: لا قضاء على الوصي الفقير فيما يأكل بالمعروف لأن ذلك حق النظر

QURTUBI-FULL:4:6#10/r3.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:4:6#10/r3.speaker: ابن عباس وأبو العالية والشعبي
QURTUBI-FULL:4:6#10/r3.claim: Another explanation allows use of an orphan's livestock milk, servants, or animals so long as the estate is not harmed; jurists compare this to fair wages, with any excess forbidden.
QURTUBI-FULL:4:6#10/r3.anchor: عن ابن عباس وأبي العالية والشعبي أن الأكل بالمعروف هو كالانتفاع بألبان المواشي، واستخدام العبيد، وركوب الدواب

QURTUBI-FULL:4:6#10/r4.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:4:6#10/r4.speaker: الحسن بن صالح بن حي
QURTUBI-FULL:4:6#10/r4.claim: Hasan ibn Salih distinguishes the father's appointed guardian, who may take customary support, from a judge's guardian, who may take nothing.
QURTUBI-FULL:4:6#10/r4.anchor: فرق الحسن بن صالح بن حي ويقال ابن حيان بين وصي الأب والحاكم

QURTUBI-FULL:4:6#10/r5.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:4:6#10/r5.speaker: مجاهد
QURTUBI-FULL:4:6#10/r5.claim: Mujahid says the allowance is abrogated by the prohibition on consuming wealth without trade by mutual consent, because guardianship is not a sale.
QURTUBI-FULL:4:6#10/r5.anchor: روى عن مجاهد قال: ليس له أن يأخذ قرضا ولا غيره

QURTUBI-FULL:4:6#10/r6.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:4:6#10/r6.speaker: زيد بن أسلم
QURTUBI-FULL:4:6#10/r6.claim: Zayd ibn Aslam says the allowance is abrogated by the warning against consuming orphan property unjustly.
QURTUBI-FULL:4:6#10/r6.anchor:
وقال زيد بن أسلم: إن الرخصة في هذه الآية منسوخة بقوله تعالى:
إن الذين يأكلون أموال اليتامى ظلما

QURTUBI-FULL:4:6#10/r7.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:4:6#10/r7.speaker: أبو يوسف
QURTUBI-FULL:4:6#10/r7.claim: Abu Yusuf says he is unsure whether the allowance was abrogated by the prohibition on consuming wealth without consensual trade.
QURTUBI-FULL:4:6#10/r7.anchor: وحكى بشر بن الوليد عن أبي يوسف قال: لا أدري، لعل هذه الآية منسوخة

QURTUBI-FULL:4:6#10/r8.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:4:6#10/r8.speaker: أبو حنيفة وأبو يوسف ومحمد
QURTUBI-FULL:4:6#10/r8.claim: A fifth view bars taking from the orphan's principal while the guardian remains at home, but permits necessary expenses when traveling for the orphan, without acquiring property.
QURTUBI-FULL:4:6#10/r8.anchor: وقول خامس وهو الفرق بين الحضر والسفر فيمنع إذا كان مقيما معه في المصر

QURTUBI-FULL:4:6#10/r9.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:4:6#10/r9.speaker: أبو قلابة
QURTUBI-FULL:4:6#10/r9.claim: Abu Qilaba permits consuming from the orphan's profits but not taking liquid capital as a loan or otherwise.
QURTUBI-FULL:4:6#10/r9.anchor: فليأكل بالمعروف مما يجني من الغلة فأما المال الناض فليس له أن يأخذ منه شيئا

QURTUBI-FULL:4:6#10/r10.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:4:6#10/r10.speaker: عكرمة عن ابن عباس
QURTUBI-FULL:4:6#10/r10.claim: A report from Ibn Abbas through Ikrima limits the allowance to a guardian who is in need and desperate.
QURTUBI-FULL:4:6#10/r10.anchor: روى عكرمة عن ابن عباس { ومن كان فقيرا فليأكل بالمعروف } قال: إذا احتاج واضطر

QURTUBI-FULL:4:6#11/r1.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:4:6#11/r1.speaker: الشعبي
QURTUBI-FULL:4:6#11/r1.claim: Al-Sha'bi compares the guardian's need to necessity for carrion or pork, permitting a limited taking and repayment if able; al-Nahhas says actual necessity already allows taking enough from any available source.
QURTUBI-FULL:4:6#11/r1.anchor: وقال الشعبي: كذلك إذا كان منه بمنزلة الدم ولحم الخنزير أخذ منه فإن وجد أوفى

QURTUBI-FULL:4:6#11/r2.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:4:6#11/r2.speaker: ابن عباس والنخعي
QURTUBI-FULL:4:6#11/r2.claim: Another Ibn Abbas and al-Nakha'i interpretation tells guardians to live modestly from their own funds so they will not need the orphan's money; al-Nahhas calls this the strongest report because others' property is inviolable without clear proof.
QURTUBI-FULL:4:6#11/r2.anchor: المراد أن يأكل الوصي بالمعروف من مال نفسه حتى لا يحتاج إلى مال اليتيم

QURTUBI-FULL:4:6#11/r3.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:4:6#11/r3.speaker: الكيا الطبري
QURTUBI-FULL:4:6#11/r3.claim: Al-Kiya al-Tabari agrees that the verse requires subsistence from one's own property, not the child's; he harmonizes its ambiguity with clear prohibitions on consuming another's wealth without consent, especially an orphan's.
QURTUBI-FULL:4:6#11/r3.anchor: توهم متوهمون من السلف بحكم الآية أن للوصي أن يأكل من مال الصبي

QURTUBI-FULL:4:6#11/r4.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:4:6#11/r4.speaker: الكيا الطبري
QURTUBI-FULL:4:6#11/r4.claim: Al-Kiya answers that judges' salaries come from unowned public funds, whereas a guardian would take from a specific owner without consent for undefined work and an undefined wage.
QURTUBI-FULL:4:6#11/r4.anchor: والوصي إنما يأخذ بعمله مال شخص معين من غير رضاه وعمله مجهول وأجرته مجهولة

QURTUBI-FULL:4:6#11/r5.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:4:6#11/r5.speaker: أبو العباس
QURTUBI-FULL:4:6#11/r5.claim: Abu al-Abbas allows fair compensation when a large estate demands substantial work; for a trivial estate he permits only customary small quantities of milk, food, or ghee without harm or excess.
QURTUBI-FULL:4:6#11/r5.anchor: إن كان مال اليتيم كثيرا يحتاج إلى كبير قيام عليه بحيث يشغل الولي عن حاجاته ومهماته

QURTUBI-FULL:4:6#12/r1.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:4:6#12/r1.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:4:6#12/r1.claim: Al-Qurtubi says abstaining from compensation is better; he condemns fees taken by partition judges and their agents as unlawful and within the threat against consuming orphan property.
QURTUBI-FULL:4:6#12/r1.anchor: قلت: والاحتراز عنه أفضل، إن شاء الله. وأما ما يأخذه قاضي القسمة ويسميه رسما ونهب أتباعه فلا أدري له وجها ولا حلا

QURTUBI-FULL:4:6#12/r2.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:4:6#12/r2.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:4:6#12/r2.claim: Witnessing the handover is commanded to secure the assets and clear suspicion; scholars differ whether it is recommended, since a guardian is trusted, or obligatory, since he cannot testify in his own favor against heirs.
QURTUBI-FULL:4:6#12/r2.anchor: أمر الله تعالى بالإشهاد تنبيها على التحصين وزوالا للتهم

QURTUBI-FULL:4:6#12/r3.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:4:6#12/r3.speaker: عمر بن الخطاب وابن جبير
QURTUBI-FULL:4:6#12/r3.claim: Umar and Ibn Jubayr understand the witnesses to document repayment by a poor guardian of a loan from the orphan's assets.
QURTUBI-FULL:4:6#12/r3.anchor: ورأى عمر بن الخطاب رضي الله عنه وابن جبير أن هذا الإشهاد إنما هو على دفع الوصي

QURTUBI-FULL:4:6#12/r4.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:4:6#12/r4.speaker: عبيدة
QURTUBI-FULL:4:6#12/r4.claim: Ubayda says the verse proves that a guardian who borrowed or consumed the orphan's assets must witness repayment once solvent.
QURTUBI-FULL:4:6#12/r4.anchor: قال عبيدة هذه الآية دليل على وجوب القضاء على من أكل المعنى

QURTUBI-FULL:4:6#12/r5.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:4:6#12/r5.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:4:6#12/r5.claim: Al-Qurtubi says the wording covers both repayment and any spending for a ward; witnessing is the apparent command, and a witnessed entrustment is discharged only by witnessed return.
QURTUBI-FULL:4:6#12/r5.anchor: والصحيح أن اللفظ يعم هذا وسواه. والظاهر أن المراد إذا أنفقتم شيئا على المولى عليه فأشهدوا

QURTUBI-FULL:4:6#12/r6.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:4:6#12/r6.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:4:6#12/r6.claim: The guardian must also protect the orphan's body through discipline and care, just as he safeguards and develops the child's assets; al-Qurtubi discussed this in al-Baqara.
QURTUBI-FULL:4:6#12/r6.anchor: كما على الوصي والكفيل حفظ مال يتيمه والتثمير له، كذلك عليه حفظ الصبي في بدنه

QURTUBI-FULL:4:6#13/r1.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:4:6#13/r1.speaker: رجل قال للنبي
QURTUBI-FULL:4:6#13/r1.claim: A man asks whether he may consume an orphan's assets and discipline him; the Prophet allows modest use without accumulating wealth or shielding his own assets, and says to discipline the child as one would one's own.
QURTUBI-FULL:4:6#13/r1.anchor: وروي أن رجلا قال للنبي صلى الله عليه وسلم: إن في حجري يتيما

QURTUBI-FULL:4:6#13/r2.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:4:6#13/r2.speaker: ابن العربي
QURTUBI-FULL:4:6#13/r2.claim: Ibn al-Arabi says that although the report is not established with a connected chain, no one can find a way to avoid its ruling.
QURTUBI-FULL:4:6#13/r2.anchor: وإن لم يثبت مسندا فليس يجد أحد عنه ملتحدا

QURTUBI-FULL:4:6#13/r3.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:4:6#13/r3.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:4:6#13/r3.claim: God is sufficient as accountant of deeds and their recompense, a warning to everyone who denies a right; grammatically the b in billahi is additional and the subject is nominative.
QURTUBI-FULL:4:6#13/r3.anchor: أي كفى الله حاسبا لأعمالكم ومجازيا بها. ففي هذا وعيد لكل جاحد حق

RAZI-FULL:v9p152#2/r1.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v9p152#2/r1.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v9p152#2/r1.claim: Because 4:2 ordered guardians to hand over orphan property, this verse specifies when: both puberty and discerned sound judgment must be established before delivery.
RAZI-FULL:v9p152#2/r1.anchor: أمر من قبل بدفع مال اليتيم اليه بقوله

RAZI-FULL:v9p152#2/r2.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v9p152#2/r2.speaker: أبو حنيفة
RAZI-FULL:v9p152#2/r2.claim: Abū Ḥanīfa holds that a discerning child’s transactions with the guardian’s permission are valid; he reads the testing command as allowing supervised buying and selling before puberty.
RAZI-FULL:v9p152#2/r2.anchor: تصرفات الصبي العاقل المميز باذن الولي صحيحة

RAZI-FULL:v9p152#2/r3.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v9p152#2/r3.speaker: الشافعي
RAZI-FULL:v9p152#2/r3.claim: Al-Shāfiʿī holds such transactions invalid. Al-Rāzī sides with him: testing can mean observing transactions done by the guardian and asking the child to assess them, or letting the child handle an item while the guardian ratifies the sale.
RAZI-FULL:v9p152#2/r3.anchor: أجاب الشافعي رضي الله عنه بأن قال : ليس المراد

RAZI-FULL:v9p153/r1.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v9p153/r1.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v9p153/r1.claim: Reaching the age of marriage means puberty, identified by emission, as in 24:59; it is when legal accountability and penalties begin, and the label refers to the emission involved in intercourse.
RAZI-FULL:v9p153/r1.anchor: المراد من بلوغ النكاح هو الاحتلام

RAZI-FULL:v9p153/r2.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v9p153/r2.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v9p153/r2.claim: Puberty has five signs: wet dream, a specified age, and coarse pubic hair for both sexes; menstruation and pregnancy are further signs for women.
RAZI-FULL:v9p153/r2.anchor: للبلوغ علامات خمسة : منها ثلاثة مشتركة

RAZI-FULL:v9p153/r3.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v9p153/r3.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v9p153/r3.claim: Īnās means knowing or, according to another gloss, seeing; its linguistic root is vision, as in the reference to seeing a fire at 28:29.

RAZI-FULL:v9p153/r4.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v9p153/r4.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v9p153/r4.claim: The required judgment concerns financial competence: the ward can manage property, avoid waste, and resist being deceived.
RAZI-FULL:v9p153/r4.anchor: وهو أن يعلم أنه مصلح لما له حتى لا يقع منه إسراف

RAZI-FULL:v9p153/r5.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v9p153/r5.speaker: الشافعي
RAZI-FULL:v9p153/r5.claim: Al-Shāfiʿī requires religious uprightness as well as financial competence, whereas Abū Ḥanīfa does not; al-Rāzī prefers al-Shāfiʿī because rushd means attaining good, contrasts with error (2:256), and is denied of sinful Adam and Pharaoh (20:121; 11:97).
RAZI-FULL:v9p153/r5.anchor: فعند الشافعي رضي الله عنه لا بد منه ، وعند أبي حنيفة

RAZI-FULL:v9p154/r1.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v9p154/r1.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v9p154/r1.claim: The disagreement over religious uprightness matters because al-Shāfiʿī places a sinful person under legal restraint, while Abū Ḥanīfa does not.
RAZI-FULL:v9p154/r1.anchor: الشافعي رحمه الله يرى الحجر على الفاسق

RAZI-FULL:v9p154/r2.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v9p154/r2.speaker: أبو حنيفة
RAZI-FULL:v9p154/r2.claim: The jurists agree that an adolescent who is not financially sound does not receive the estate; Abū Ḥanīfa releases it at twenty-five regardless of demonstrated judgment, after puberty at eighteen plus seven years for changing maturity, invoking the prayer training age of seven.
RAZI-FULL:v9p154/r2.anchor: ثم عند أبي حنيفة لا يدفع اليه ماله حتى يبلغ خمسا وعشرين سنة

RAZI-FULL:v9p154/r3.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v9p154/r3.speaker: الشافعي وأبو يوسف ومحمد
RAZI-FULL:v9p154/r3.claim: Al-Shāfiʿī, Abū Yūsuf, and Muḥammad say the estate is withheld indefinitely until sound judgment is actually observed.
RAZI-FULL:v9p154/r3.anchor: وقال الشافعي رضي الله عنه : لا يدفع إليه أبدا إلا بايناس الرشد

RAZI-FULL:v9p154/r4.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v9p154/r4.speaker: أبو بكر الرازي
RAZI-FULL:v9p154/r4.claim: Abū Bakr al-Rāzī argues that an indefinite noun rushd requires only some rationality, so once age twenty-five arrives the verse’s condition is met.
RAZI-FULL:v9p154/r4.anchor: احتج أبو بكر الرازي لأبي حنيفة بهذه الآية فقال : لا شك أن اسم الرشد

RAZI-FULL:v9p154/r5.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v9p154/r5.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v9p154/r5.claim: Al-Rāzī rejects that argument: the context makes financial stewardship the required judgment; otherwise the syntax loses coherence, and anyone still unable to protect property at twenty-five remains like a child and must not receive it.
RAZI-FULL:v9p154/r5.anchor: المراد ابتلاؤهم فيما يتعلق بمصالح حفظ المال

RAZI-FULL:v9p154#2/r1.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v9p154#2/r1.speaker: الشافعي
RAZI-FULL:v9p154#2/r1.claim: If someone first reaches sound judgment and later becomes foolish, al-Shāfiʿī would restrain him, while Abū Ḥanīfa would not; al-Rāzī supports restraint by analogy with the still-unfit minor whose property is preserved for future need.
RAZI-FULL:v9p154#2/r1.anchor: إذا بلغ رشيدا ثم تغير وصار سفيها حجر عليه عند الشافعي ولا يحجر عليه عند أبي حنيفة

RAZI-FULL:v9p154#2/r2.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v9p154#2/r2.speaker: صاحب الكشاف
RAZI-FULL:v9p154#2/r2.claim: Al-Kashshāf says the indefinite rushd may mean financial and commercial sound judgment specifically, or may mean any discernible sign of it without awaiting complete maturity.
RAZI-FULL:v9p154#2/r2.anchor: الفائدة في تنكير الرشد التنبيه على ان المعتبر هو الرشد في التصرف والتجارة

RAZI-FULL:v9p154#2/r3.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v9p154#2/r3.speaker: ابن مسعود
RAZI-FULL:v9p154#2/r3.claim: Ibn Masʿūd reads fa-in aḥsastum, meaning fa-in aḥsastum/perceived; a cited line witnesses the form aḥsana bihi.
RAZI-FULL:v9p154#2/r3.anchor: قرأ ابن مسعود فان أحستم ، بمعنى أحسستم

RAZI-FULL:v9p154#2/r4.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v9p154#2/r4.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v9p154#2/r4.claim: The word rushd is also read with two fatḥas or with two ḍammas.

RAZI-FULL:v9p154#2/r5.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v9p154#2/r5.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v9p154#2/r5.claim: Once puberty and discerned judgment are both present, guardians must hand over the property; no separate complete-intellect condition is stated because judgment already entails more than basic reason.
RAZI-FULL:v9p154#2/r5.anchor: عند حصول الشرطين أعني البلوغ وإيناس الرشد يجب دفع المال اليهم

RAZI-FULL:v9p155/r1.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v9p155/r1.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v9p155/r1.claim: Guardians must not consume the property wastefully or hasten to spend it before the orphans grow up and reclaim it; the phrase describes their waste and haste.
RAZI-FULL:v9p155/r1.anchor: مسرفين ومبادرين كبرهم أو لاسرافكم ومبادرتكم كبرهم تفرطون في إنفاقها

RAZI-FULL:v9p155/r2.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v9p155/r2.speaker: الواحدي
RAZI-FULL:v9p155/r2.claim: Al-Wāḥidī explains istaʿaffa and ʿaffa as refraining and abstaining.
RAZI-FULL:v9p155/r2.anchor: قال الواحدي رحمه الله : استعف عن الشيء وعف اذا امتنع منه وتركه

RAZI-FULL:v9p155/r3.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v9p155/r3.speaker: صاحب الكشاف
RAZI-FULL:v9p155/r3.claim: Al-Kashshāf says istaʿaffa is more emphatic than ʿaffa, as if one actively seeks greater chastity.
RAZI-FULL:v9p155/r3.anchor: استعف أبلغ من عف كأنه طالب زيادة العفة

RAZI-FULL:v9p155/r4.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v9p155/r4.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v9p155/r4.claim: One legal view allows a needy guardian to use from the ward’s wealth what is needed and a fair amount for the work; the verse’s contrast and its distinction between unjust and non-unjust consumption support this allowance.
RAZI-FULL:v9p155/r4.anchor: أن له أن يأخذ بقدر ما يحتاج اليه من مال اليتيم وبقدر أجر عمله

RAZI-FULL:v9p155/r5.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v9p155/r5.speaker: النبي
RAZI-FULL:v9p155/r5.claim: A man asked the Prophet whether he could use an orphan’s wealth; the reply permits fair use without accumulating wealth or protecting one’s own property with it, and allows discipline as with one’s child.
RAZI-FULL:v9p155/r5.anchor: عن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم أن رجلا قال له : ان تحت حجري يتيما أآكل من ماله ؟ قال : بالمعروف

RAZI-FULL:v9p155/r6.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v9p155/r6.speaker: عمر بن الخطاب
RAZI-FULL:v9p155/r6.claim: In a letter to ʿAmmār, Ibn Masʿūd, and ʿUthmān ibn Ḥunayf, ʿUmar assigns shares from public funds and compares their role to a guardian of an orphan.
RAZI-FULL:v9p155/r6.anchor: عمر بن الخطاب رضي الله عنه كتب إلى عمار وابن مسعود وعثمان بن حنيف : سلام عليكم

RAZI-FULL:v9p155/r7.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v9p155/r7.speaker: ابن عباس
RAZI-FULL:v9p155/r7.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās permits a guardian to drink an orphan’s camel milk if he tends and waters the animal, while avoiding harm to its young or excessive milking.
RAZI-FULL:v9p155/r7.anchor: وعن ابن عباس أن ولي يتيم قال له : أفأشرب من لبن إبله ؟ قال : إن كنت تبغي

RAZI-FULL:v9p155/r8.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v9p155/r8.speaker: ابن عباس
RAZI-FULL:v9p155/r8.claim: Another report from Ibn ʿAbbās says the guardian may eat moderately by sharing in their work but should not wear even a turban beyond that allowance.
RAZI-FULL:v9p155/r8.anchor: يضرب بيده مع أيديهم فليأكل بالمعروف ولا يلبس عمامة فما فوقها

RAZI-FULL:v9p155/r9.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v9p155/r9.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v9p155/r9.claim: Guardianship work may merit compensation by analogy with collectors of charity, who receive a designated share.
RAZI-FULL:v9p155/r9.anchor: وجب أن يتمكن من أن يأكل من ماله بقدر عمله قياسا على الساعي في أخذ الصدقات

RAZI-FULL:v9p155#2/r1.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v9p155#2/r1.speaker: سعيد بن جبير ومجاهد وأبو العالية
RAZI-FULL:v9p155#2/r1.claim: A second view allows a poor guardian to borrow only what is needed and repay when able; if death comes before repayment despite inability, nothing is owed. This is attributed to Saʿīd ibn Jubayr, Mujāhid, Abū al-ʿĀliya, and most reports from Ibn ʿAbbās.
RAZI-FULL:v9p155#2/r1.anchor: وهذا قول سعيد بن جبير ومجاهد وأبي العالية ، وأكثر الروايات عن ابن عباس

RAZI-FULL:v9p155#2/r2.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v9p155#2/r2.speaker: أبو العالية وغيره
RAZI-FULL:v9p155#2/r2.claim: Some restrict borrowing to principal assets such as gold and silver, while allowing harmless use of livestock milk, servants, and riding animals.
RAZI-FULL:v9p155#2/r2.anchor: خص هذا الاقراض بأصول الأموال من الذهب والفضة

RAZI-FULL:v9p155#2/r3.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v9p155#2/r3.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v9p155#2/r3.claim: Those who allow this use reason from the command to return the orphan’s property, taking that to govern the assets themselves.
RAZI-FULL:v9p155#2/r3.anchor: واحتجوا بأن الله تعالى قال : { فإذا دفعتم إليهم أموالهم }

RAZI-FULL:v9p155#2/r4.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v9p155#2/r4.speaker: أبو بكر الرازي
RAZI-FULL:v9p155#2/r4.claim: Abū Bakr al-Rāzī reports his school’s view that guardians may take nothing from the orphan, whether as a loan or outright and whether rich or poor; he cites 4:2, 4:10, 4:127, and 2:188 as decisive texts against the possibly ambiguous permission here.
RAZI-FULL:v9p155#2/r4.anchor: قال أبو بكر الرازي : الذي نعرفه من مذهب أصحابنا أنه لا يأخذ على سبيل القرض

RAZI-FULL:v9p155#2/r5.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v9p155#2/r5.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v9p155#2/r5.claim: Al-Rāzī rejects the argument: 4:2 is general while this verse is specific, and the other prohibitions only apply if moderate guardian use is already proved unjust, which is the very issue disputed.
RAZI-FULL:v9p155#2/r5.anchor: أما قوله : { وءاتوا اليتامى أموالهم } فهو عام وهذه الآية التي نحن فيها خاصة

RAZI-FULL:v9p156/r1.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v9p156/r1.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v9p156/r1.claim: The community agrees that witnesses should preferably attest when a guardian hands over an adult orphan’s property: this deters a false claim by the recipient, lets the guardian defend against such a claim, and demonstrates the guardian’s integrity.
RAZI-FULL:v9p156/r1.anchor: الأمة مجمعة على أن الوصي إذا دفع المال إلى اليتيم بعد صيرورته بالغا

RAZI-FULL:v9p156/r2.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v9p156/r2.speaker: النبي
RAZI-FULL:v9p156/r2.claim: The Prophet instructed a person who found lost property to bring upright witnesses and neither hide nor lose it, so that the finder’s trustworthiness is evident.
RAZI-FULL:v9p156/r2.anchor: من وجد لقطة فليشهد ذوي عدل ولا يكتم ولا يغيب

RAZI-FULL:v9p156/r3.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v9p156/r3.speaker: مالك والشافعي
RAZI-FULL:v9p156/r3.claim: Mālik and al-Shāfiʿī do not accept the guardian’s bare claim that he delivered the property or spent it on the ward; Abū Ḥanīfa and his associates do accept it.
RAZI-FULL:v9p156/r3.anchor: قال مالك والشافعي : لا يصدق ، وقال أبو حنيفة وأصحابه : يصدق

RAZI-FULL:v9p156/r4.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v9p156/r4.speaker: الشافعي
RAZI-FULL:v9p156/r4.claim: Al-Shāfiʿī treats the command to call witnesses as obligatory and argues that the guardian is entrusted by religious law, not personally by the orphan.
RAZI-FULL:v9p156/r4.anchor: فإن قوله : { فأشهدوا عليهم } أمر ، وظاهر الأمر الوجوب ، وأيضا قال الشافعي : القيم غير مؤتمن من جهة اليتيم

RAZI-FULL:v9p156/r5.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v9p156/r5.speaker: أبو بكر الرازي
RAZI-FULL:v9p156/r5.claim: Abū Bakr al-Rāzī argues that if the guardian is not believed because the orphan did not entrust him, the same should apply to a judge or father, and even to property both parties admit was lost.
RAZI-FULL:v9p156/r5.anchor: لو كان ما ذكره علة لنفي التصديق لوجب أن لا يصدق القاضي إذا قال لليتيم

RAZI-FULL:v9p156/r6.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v9p156/r6.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v9p156/r6.claim: Al-Rāzī rejects the analogies: distrust of a judge would create endless appeals; a father has greater compassion than a stranger; a non-negligent accidental loss must be accepted or guardianship would fail, unlike witnessed delivery.
RAZI-FULL:v9p156/r6.anchor: القاضي حاكم فيجب إزالة التهمة عنه ليصير قضاؤه نافذا

RAZI-FULL:v9p156/r7.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v9p156/r7.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v9p156/r7.claim: The preceding warning against consuming wealth hastily before the orphan grows up shows why suspicion of guardians is well-founded and strengthens the case for witnessing delivery.
RAZI-FULL:v9p156/r7.anchor: وهذا يدل على جريان العادة بكثرة إقدام الولي على ظلم الايتام والصبيان

RAZI-FULL:v9p157/r1.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v9p157/r1.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v9p157/r1.claim: Witnessing protects the orphan from injustice and short delivery because the guardian cannot convincingly claim to have transferred the assets without witnesses; al-Rāzī says both the command’s wording and its purpose require it.
RAZI-FULL:v9p157/r1.anchor: إذا كان لا يتمكن من ادعاء دفع المال اليه إلا عند حضور الشاهد ، صار ذلك مانعا له من الظلم

RAZI-FULL:v9p157/r2.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v9p157/r2.speaker: أبو بكر الرازي
RAZI-FULL:v9p157/r2.claim: Abū Bakr al-Rāzī argues that since a guardian is entrusted with safekeeping, he should be believed when returning the property just as a deposit holder is.
