THALABI:v3p259/r1.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v3p259/r1.speaker: قتادة
THALABI:v3p259/r1.claim: Qatada permits a guardian maintaining an orphan's orchard and livestock to take some produce, but forbids consuming the principal assets.
THALABI:v3p259/r1.anchor: قال قتادة: كان اليتيم يكون له الحائط من النخل فيقوم وليه على صلاحه وسقيه فيصيب من ثمرته

THALABI:v3p259/r2.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v3p259/r2.speaker: الضحاك
THALABI:v3p259/r2.claim: Al-Dahhak says reasonable benefit means riding the orphan's animal or using a servant, not eating from the estate.
THALABI:v3p259/r2.anchor: المعروف ركوب الدابة وخدمة الخادم وليس له أن يأكل من ماله شيئا

THALABI:v3p259/r3.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v3p259/r3.speaker: ابن عباس
THALABI:v3p259/r3.claim: Ibn Abbas allows a livestock guardian to drink surplus milk after tending the herd, seeking strays, treating illness, and maintaining its watering place, provided he does not harm the young or overmilk.
THALABI:v3p259/r3.anchor: فاشرب من فضل ألبانها عنهم غير مضر بأولادها ولا تنهكها في الحلب

THALABI:v3p259/r4.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v3p259/r4.speaker: عائشة
THALABI:v3p259/r4.claim: Aisha and other scholars say a poor guardian may take compensation proportionate to his care and work, even if it consumes the property, without repayment.
THALABI:v3p259/r4.anchor: قال بعضهم: المعروف هو أن يأخذ من جميع ماله، إذا كان يلي ذلك بقدر قيامه [وخدمته] وعمله وأجرته،

THALABI:v3p259/r5.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v3p259/r5.speaker: محمد بن كعب القرظي
THALABI:v3p259/r5.claim: Muhammad ibn Kaʿb says the wealthy guardian should abstain, while the needy one may take only the bare minimum as an employee.
THALABI:v3p259/r5.anchor: قالت به عائشة وجماعة من العلماء، وقال محمد بن كعب القرظي من كان غنيا

THALABI:v3p259/r6.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v3p259/r6.speaker: author
THALABI:v3p259/r6.claim: Maʿruf is what is easy and willingly accepted; the author connects the expression with another Qurʾanic reference to fair provision.
THALABI:v3p259/r6.anchor: وأصل المعروف ما تيسر على الإنسان فطابت نفسه به، قال الله تعالى: متاع بالمعروف

THALABI:v3p259/r7.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v3p259/r7.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
THALABI:v3p259/r7.claim: Asked whether he may strike an orphan and eat from the estate, the Prophet says to treat him as one's own child and take reasonably without hoarding or using the orphan's property to protect one's own.
THALABI:v3p259/r7.anchor: بالمعروف غير متأثل من ماله ولا واقيا مالك بماله

THALABI:v3p259/r8.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v3p259/r8.speaker: author
THALABI:v3p259/r8.claim: Witnessing the handover is divine guidance, not a duty: it shows the guardian discharged the trust, ends suspicion, and prevents disputes; God is reckoner, judge, and witness.
THALABI:v3p259/r8.anchor: فإذا دفعتم إليهم أموالهم فأشهدوا عليهم هذا أدب من الله تعالى، ليعلم أن الولي

WAHIDI-BASIT:v6p328/r1.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v6p328/r1.speaker: المفسرون
WAHIDI-BASIT:v6p328/r1.claim: The verse was revealed after Thabit ibn Rifaʿa’s father died and his uncle asked the Prophet when he could use and return the orphan’s property.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v6p328/r1.anchor: قال المفسرون: نزلت في ثابت بن رفاعة

WAHIDI-BASIT:v6p328/r2.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v6p328/r2.speaker: الحسن، وقتادة، ومجاهد، والسدي، وابن زيد
WAHIDI-BASIT:v6p328/r2.claim: They interpret testing orphans as assessing their intellect and religious conduct.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v6p328/r2.anchor: قال الحسن، وقتادة، ومجاهد، والسدي، وابن زيد: اختبروهم في عقولهم وأديانهم

WAHIDI-BASIT:v6p328#2/r1.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v6p328#2/r1.speaker: الفقهاء
WAHIDI-BASIT:v6p328#2/r1.claim: Guardians test a near-pubescent boy by entrusting a little spending money; a girl is tested through household management and spinning cotton.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v6p328#2/r1.anchor: يرد إليه الأمر في نفقته عند مراهقة الحلم، ويعطى شيئا نزرا يتصرف فيه

WAHIDI-BASIT:v6p328#2/r2.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v6p328#2/r2.speaker: ابن عباس، ومجاهد، والسدي، وابن زيد
WAHIDI-BASIT:v6p328#2/r2.claim: They understand reaching marriage age as attaining puberty, specifically a wet dream.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v6p328#2/r2.anchor: قال ابن عباس ومجاهد والسدي وابن زيد: يريد الحلم

WAHIDI-BASIT:v6p328#2/r3.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v6p328#2/r3.speaker: author
WAHIDI-BASIT:v6p328#2/r3.claim: The phrase means reaching the condition for marriage through seminal emission.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v6p328#2/r3.anchor: حتى إذا بلغوا حال النكاح من الاحتلام

WAHIDI-BASIT:v6p328#2/r4.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v6p328#2/r4.speaker: آخرون؛ ابن قتيبة
WAHIDI-BASIT:v6p328#2/r4.claim: Another interpretation is reaching adult capacity for marriage; Ibn Qutayba says becoming able to marry women.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v6p328#2/r4.anchor: وقال آخرون: أي بلغوا مبلغ الرجال والنساء من القدرة على النكاح

WAHIDI-BASIT:v6p328#2/r5.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v6p328#2/r5.speaker: author
WAHIDI-BASIT:v6p328#2/r5.claim: A boy or girl reaches maturity upon ejaculation, whether through intercourse or a wet dream.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v6p328#2/r5.anchor: فإذا أنزل الغلام أو الجارية فقد بلغ، سواء كان عن جماع أو احتلام

WAHIDI-BASIT:v6p328#2/r6.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v6p328#2/r6.speaker: ابن عباس؛ عطاء عنه؛ الفراء؛ الزجاج
WAHIDI-BASIT:v6p328#2/r6.claim: The glosses for anastum are knowing, seeing, finding, and knowing, respectively.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v6p328#2/r6.anchor: قال الفراء: وجدتم (¬3). وقال الزجاج: علمتم

WAHIDI-BASIT:v6p328#2/r7.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v6p328#2/r7.speaker: author
WAHIDI-BASIT:v6p328#2/r7.claim: The root sense of īnās is seeing; the cited verse and Ibn Ḥalaza’s line use it for perceiving or finding something.

WAHIDI-BASIT:v6p332/r1.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v6p332/r1.speaker: ابن عباس
WAHIDI-BASIT:v6p332/r1.claim: Guardians must not hasten to consume orphans’ property extravagantly before they reach puberty and sound judgment.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v6p332/r1.anchor: يريد لا تبادروا في أموال اليتامى بالسرف قبل أن يبلغ الحلم والرشد

WAHIDI-BASIT:v6p332/r2.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v6p332/r2.speaker: المفسرون
WAHIDI-BASIT:v6p332/r2.claim: Guardians may rush to consume the estate out of fear that maturity will require them to hand it over.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v6p332/r2.anchor: لا تبادروا بأكل مالهم كبرهم ورشدهم حذرا أن يبلغوا فيلزمكم تسليم المال إليهم

WAHIDI-BASIT:v6p332/r3.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v6p332/r3.speaker: author
WAHIDI-BASIT:v6p332/r3.claim: An is accusative as the object of the verbal noun, meaning hastening their maturity.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v6p332/r3.anchor: و (أن) في محل النصب؛ لأنه مفعول المصدر

WAHIDI-BASIT:v6p332/r4.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v6p332/r4.speaker: ابن عباس
WAHIDI-BASIT:v6p332/r4.claim: A wealthy guardian must refrain entirely from the orphan’s property.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v6p332/r4.anchor: من كان غنيا من الأوصياء فليستعفف عن مال اليتيم ولا يأكل منه شيئا

WAHIDI-BASIT:v6p332/r5.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v6p332/r5.speaker: author
WAHIDI-BASIT:v6p332/r5.claim: Istiʿfāf means leaving the property and not eating from it.

WAHIDI-BASIT:v6p332/r6.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v6p332/r6.speaker: سعيد بن جبير، وعبيدة، ومجاهد، وأبو العالية، وأكثر الروايات عن ابن عباس
WAHIDI-BASIT:v6p332/r6.claim: A poor guardian may borrow only what he needs, repay upon becoming able, and owes nothing if he dies unable; verse 4:114 supports construing maʿrūf as a loan, as does ʿUmar’s practice.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v6p332/r6.anchor: هو أن يأخذ بقدر ما يحتاج إليه من

WAHIDI-BASIT:v6p332/r7.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v6p332/r7.speaker: عطاء، وعكرمة، والسدي
WAHIDI-BASIT:v6p332/r7.claim: A poor guardian may take a moderate amount without extravagance and need not repay it.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v6p332/r7.anchor: معنى الأكل بالمعروف هو أن يقتصد ولا يسرف، ثم لا قضاء عليه فيما يأكل

WAHIDI-BASIT:v6p332/r8.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v6p332/r8.speaker: إبراهيم
WAHIDI-BASIT:v6p332/r8.claim: A guardian may take only enough to relieve hunger and cover nakedness.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v6p332/r8.anchor: هو ما سد الجوعة ووارى العورة

WAHIDI-BASIT:v6p332/r9.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v6p332/r9.speaker: عائشة وجماعة من العلماء
WAHIDI-BASIT:v6p332/r9.claim: A guardian may take a fair wage proportionate to work, even from the whole estate, without repayment; a report from Ibn ʿAbbās permits eating without hoarding or protecting one’s own wealth with the orphan’s.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v6p332/r9.anchor: أن يأخذ من جميع المال إذا كان يلي ذلك بقدر قيامه وعمله وأجرته

WAHIDI-BASIT:v6p332/r10.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v6p332/r10.speaker: author
WAHIDI-BASIT:v6p332/r10.claim: The guardian may not be extravagant and is entitled only to the market-rate wage for his legally assigned work; the wealthy must abstain.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v6p332/r10.anchor: القيم ممنوع من الإسراف، وإنما له أجر مثل عمله؛ لأنه أجير بالشرع

WAHIDI-BASIT:v6p336/r1.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v6p336/r1.speaker: author
WAHIDI-BASIT:v6p336/r1.claim: Witnessing the transfer protects the guardian with evidence if a dispute arises; it is recommended, not obligatory, and the orphan’s word prevails because the guardian is a trustee.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v6p336/r1.anchor: وفي هذا دليل على أن القول قول اليتيم عند التنازع

WAHIDI-BASIT:v6p336/r2.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v6p336/r2.speaker: ابن الأنباري والأزهري
WAHIDI-BASIT:v6p336/r2.claim: Ḥasīban can mean an accountant or one who suffices.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v6p336/r2.anchor: يكون بمعنى محاسبا، ويكون بمعنى كافيا

WAHIDI-BASIT:v6p336/r3.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v6p336/r3.speaker: ابن الأنباري
WAHIDI-BASIT:v6p336/r3.claim: In a threat, ḥasībuhu Allāh means God will hold him accountable; Qays al-Majnūn’s poem uses ḥasīb in that sense.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v6p336/r3.anchor: فمعناه: ثم أنت محاسبها على ظلمها

WAHIDI-BASIT:v6p336/r4.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v6p336/r4.speaker: ابن الأنباري
WAHIDI-BASIT:v6p336/r4.claim: Mukhabbal al-Saʿdī’s verse likewise uses ḥasīb for the one who will account for a wrong.

WAHIDI-BASIT:v6p336/r5.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v6p336/r5.speaker: author
WAHIDI-BASIT:v6p336/r5.claim: When ḥasīb means sufficient, ḥasībuka Allāh means God is enough for you; compare the phrase in Āl ʿImrān.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v6p336/r5.anchor: ومن الكفاية قولهم: حسيبك الله. ومعناه: كافي إياك الله

WAHIDI-BASIT:v6p336/r6.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v6p336/r6.speaker: ابن عباس
WAHIDI-BASIT:v6p336/r6.claim: God is the requiter of both the good and the evildoer, returning to the sense of accounting.

WAHIDI-BASIT:v6p336/r7.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v6p336/r7.speaker: الزجاج
WAHIDI-BASIT:v6p336/r7.claim: The prefixed bāʾ in “God is sufficient” constructions is extra, so the meaning is simply that God or the Lord suffices.

WAHIDI-BASIT:v6p336/r8.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v6p336/r8.speaker: author
WAHIDI-BASIT:v6p336/r8.claim: Ḥasīban is accusative either as a circumstantial qualifier or as specification distinguishing God from those who suffice or account.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v6p336/r8.anchor: وحسيبا منصوب على وجهين: أحدهما الحال

WAHIDI-WAJIZ:4:5-6/r2.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:4:5-6/r2.speaker: author
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:4:5-6/r2.claim: Test orphans’ minds and religion until puberty; when they show sound judgment and can preserve property, hand it over.

WAHIDI-WAJIZ:4:5-6/r3.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:4:5-6/r3.speaker: author
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:4:5-6/r3.claim: Guardians must not waste the estate or rush to use it before the orphan grows up; a rich guardian takes nothing, while a poor one may take a customary wage for work.
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:4:5-6/r3.anchor: حذر أن يبلغوا، فيلزمكم تسليم المال إليهم

WAHIDI-WAJIZ:4:5-6/r4.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:4:5-6/r4.speaker: author
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:4:5-6/r4.claim: When the orphans receive their property, take witnesses so the guardian can prove delivery if a dispute arises; God sufficiently reckons and recompenses.
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:4:5-6/r4.anchor: لكي إن وقع اختلاف أمكن الولي

ELMALILI:4:6/r1.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:4:6/r1.speaker: author
ELMALILI:4:6/r1.claim: A poor guardian or trustee may take a fair amount for the work and service performed and necessary needs; a wealthy one should abstain.
ELMALILI:4:6/r1.anchor: fakir olan velî veya vasî de mâruf vechile ücret-i sa‘y ü hizmeti ve hâcet-i zarûriyesi kadar yesin.

ELMALILI:4:6/r2.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:4:6/r2.speaker: author
ELMALILI:4:6/r2.claim: The meaning of fair dealing is clarified by prohibitions on consuming wealth wrongfully or unjustly, including the orphan’s property, and by the command to uphold justice for orphans.
ELMALILI:4:6/r2.anchor: Bu mâruf لَا تَأْكُلُوٓا۟ أَمْوَٰلَكُم بَيْنَكُم بِٱلْبَٰطِلِ [el-Bakara 2/188; en-Nisâ 4/29], إِنَّ ٱلَّذِينَ يَأْكُلُونَ أَمْوَٰلَ ٱلْيَتَٰمَىٰ ظُلْمًا [en-Nisâ 4/10], وَأَن تَقُومُوا۟ لِلْيَتَٰمَىٰ بِٱلْقِسْطِ [en-Nisâ 4/127] âyetleriyle mâlum olur.

ELMALILI:4:6/r3.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:4:6/r3.speaker: author
ELMALILI:4:6/r3.claim: When handing orphans their property, the guardian should deliver it in the presence of witnesses.
ELMALILI:4:6/r3.anchor: O yetimlerin mallarını kendilerine teslim ettiğiniz zaman da onlara karşı şâhid tutunuz, şâhid huzurunda veriniz

ELMALILI:4:6/r4.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:4:6/r4.speaker: author
ELMALILI:4:6/r4.claim: God is sufficient as accountant: obedience means no other accountant need be feared, and disobedience cannot be rescued by another accountant.
ELMALILI:4:6/r4.anchor: Allah da bütün hesaplarınızı görmeye kâfidir.

ELMALILI:4:6/r5.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:4:6/r5.speaker: author
ELMALILI:4:6/r5.claim: The verse is reported to have been revealed after Rifaʿa died leaving his young son Sabit and the boy’s guardian asked the Prophet what share of the property he could lawfully use and when he should return it.
ELMALILI:4:6/r5.anchor: Rifâ‘a vefat etmiş ve oğlu Sâbit’i sağīr olarak bırakmış idi, velîsi “taht-ı hıcrimde biraderzâdem var, bunun malından bana ne kadar helâl olur ve malını ne zaman teslim edeyim?” diye Resûlullah’a sormuştu

ELMALILI:4:6/r6.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:4:6/r6.speaker: author
ELMALILI:4:6/r6.claim: The discussion now moves on to inheritance rulings.

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:4:6/r1.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:4:6/r1.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:4:6/r1.claim: Orphan property is delivered only after both marriageable age and actual financial maturity, since either can occur before the other; jurists differ on age from fifteen to nineteen and on separate ages by sex, and a state may select and legislate one view.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:4:6/r1.anchor: Âyet malın teslimini iki şarta bağlamıştır

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:4:6/r2.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:4:6/r2.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:4:6/r2.claim: Guardians test wards through suitable means, then when convinced of their ability to manage property, deliver it to its now mature owner in the presence of witnesses.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:4:6/r2.anchor: Veliler ve vasîler uygun vasıtalarla kısıtlıları deneyecekler, rüşdün oluştuğuna kanaat getirdiklerinde şahitler huzurunda mallarını

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:4:6/r3.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:4:6/r3.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:4:6/r3.claim: Guardians managing a ward's assets may take an appropriate customary or legal share or fee if they need it; if not, they are encouraged to serve freely for the ward and society, seeking God's pleasure.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:4:6/r3.anchor: Kısıtlıların malları üzerinde tasarrufta bulunan vasîlerin, ihtiyaçları bulunduğu takdirde, örfe veya kanuna göre bu maldan uygun bir pay yahut ücret almaları câizdir

WAHIDI-ASBAB:v1p143/r1.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-ASBAB:v1p143/r1.speaker: author
WAHIDI-ASBAB:v1p143/r1.claim: The verse was revealed about Thabit b. Rifa'a and his uncle: after Rifa'a died leaving a young son, the uncle asked the Prophet what he could use from the boy's property and when he should hand it over.
WAHIDI-ASBAB:v1p143/r1.anchor: نزلت في ثابت بن رفاعة وفي عمه، وذلك أن رفاعة توفي وترك ابنه ثابتا وهو صغير

QIRAAT-ER:4:6:15#1/r1.author: QIRAAT-ER
QIRAAT-ER:4:6:15#1/r1.speaker: author
QIRAAT-ER:4:6:15#1/r1.claim: The hāʾ of the plural pronoun may have kasra or ḍamma in ilayhum, a dialectal voweling difference with no semantic effect.
QIRAAT-ER:4:6:15#1/r1.anchor: Kasra vs. ḍamma on hāʾ al-jamʿ — dialectal variation in 3rd person plural pronoun voweling

QIRAAT-ER:4:6:44#1/r1.author: QIRAAT-ER
QIRAAT-ER:4:6:44#1/r1.speaker: author
QIRAAT-ER:4:6:44#1/r1.claim: This entry repeats the ilayhum hāʾ-vowel variant: kasra versus ḍamma is dialectal and does not change meaning.
QIRAAT-ER:4:6:44#1/r1.anchor: Kasra vs. ḍamma on hāʾ al-jamʿ — dialectal variation; identical to word 15 variant

QIRAAT-ER:4:6:48#1/r1.author: QIRAAT-ER
QIRAAT-ER:4:6:48#1/r1.speaker: author
QIRAAT-ER:4:6:48#1/r1.claim: The hāʾ in ʿalayhum likewise varies between kasra and ḍamma without changing meaning.
QIRAAT-ER:4:6:48#1/r1.anchor: Kasra vs. ḍamma on hāʾ al-jamʿ — dialectal variation; no semantic difference

ABDURRAZZAQ:v1p146#2/r1.author: ʿAbd al-Razzāq al-Ṣanʿānī
ABDURRAZZAQ:v1p146#2/r1.speaker: قتادة والحسن
ABDURRAZZAQ:v1p146#2/r1.claim: Qatada and al-Hasan say guardians should test orphans’ judgment before returning their property, and must not squander it or rush to consume it before the orphans grow up.
ABDURRAZZAQ:v1p146#2/r1.anchor: عن قتادة والحسن في قوله تعالى ﴿ وابتلوا اليتامى ﴾ قال يقول اختبروا اليتامى

ABDURRAZZAQ:v1p146#2/r2.author: ʿAbd al-Razzāq al-Ṣanʿānī
ABDURRAZZAQ:v1p146#2/r2.speaker: ابن عباس
ABDURRAZZAQ:v1p146#2/r2.claim: Ibn Abbas permits a guardian to take some milk from an orphan’s livestock in return for caring for it, including searching for strays and tending its sores and watering places.
ABDURRAZZAQ:v1p146#2/r2.anchor: قال ابن عباس ألست تبغي ضالتها قال بلى قال ألست تهنيء جرباها

ABDURRAZZAQ:v1p146#2/r3.author: ʿAbd al-Razzāq al-Ṣanʿānī
ABDURRAZZAQ:v1p146#2/r3.speaker: ابن عباس
ABDURRAZZAQ:v1p146#2/r3.claim: Ibn Abbas permits drinking the animals’ milk when the guardian tends and waters them, provided this does not harm their young or amount to excessive milking.
ABDURRAZZAQ:v1p146#2/r3.anchor: عن يحيى بن سعيد عن القاسم بن القاسم ابن محمد قال جاء أعرابي إلى ابن عباس

ABDURRAZZAQ:v1p146#2/r4.author: ʿAbd al-Razzāq al-Ṣanʿānī
ABDURRAZZAQ:v1p146#2/r4.speaker: إبراهيم
ABDURRAZZAQ:v1p146#2/r4.claim: Ibrahim defines reasonable consumption as enough to satisfy hunger and cover one’s nakedness, not fine linen or luxurious robes.
ABDURRAZZAQ:v1p146#2/r4.anchor: عن مغيرة عن إبراهيم في هذه الآية ﴿ ومن كان غنيا فليستعفف ومن كان فقيرا فليأكل بالمعروف ﴾ قال ما سد الجوع ووارى العورة

ABDURRAZZAQ:v1p146#2/r5.author: ʿAbd al-Razzāq al-Ṣanʿānī
ABDURRAZZAQ:v1p146#2/r5.speaker: مجاهد وسعيد بن جبير والحكم
ABDURRAZZAQ:v1p146#2/r5.claim: Mujahid, Sa‘id ibn Jubayr, and al-Hakam interpret a poor guardian’s reasonable consumption as a loan, citing the order to witness the return of the property.
ABDURRAZZAQ:v1p146#2/r5.anchor: عن مجاهد وعن حماد عن سعيد بن جبير في قوله تعالى ﴿ فليأكل بالمعروف ﴾ قال هو القرض قال الثوري وقاله الحكم أيضا

ABDURRAZZAQ:v1p146#2/r6.author: ʿAbd al-Razzāq al-Ṣanʿānī
ABDURRAZZAQ:v1p146#2/r6.speaker: عبيدة
ABDURRAZZAQ:v1p146#2/r6.claim: Ubayda also says the poor guardian’s use of the property is a loan.
ABDURRAZZAQ:v1p146#2/r6.anchor: عن محمد بن سيرين عن عبيدة في قوله تعالى ﴿ ومن كان فقيرا فليأكل بالمعروف ﴾ قال هو عليه قرض

ABDURRAZZAQ:v1p146#2/r7.author: ʿAbd al-Razzāq al-Ṣanʿānī
ABDURRAZZAQ:v1p146#2/r7.speaker: الحسن
ABDURRAZZAQ:v1p146#2/r7.claim: Al-Hasan says a poor guardian’s permitted consumption is not a loan.
ABDURRAZZAQ:v1p146#2/r7.anchor: سألت الحسن عن قوله تعالى ﴿ ومن كان غنيا فليستعفف ﴾ قال ليس بقرض

ABDURRAZZAQ:v1p148/r1.author: ʿAbd al-Razzāq al-Ṣanʿānī
ABDURRAZZAQ:v1p148/r1.speaker: عطاء وعكرمة
ABDURRAZZAQ:v1p148/r1.claim: Ata and Ikrima’s brief gloss on the guardian’s conduct is that he ‘lays his hand’ on the property.
ABDURRAZZAQ:v1p148/r1.anchor: عن عطاء وعكرمة قالا يضع يده

ABDURRAZZAQ:v1p148/r2.author: ʿAbd al-Razzāq al-Ṣanʿānī
ABDURRAZZAQ:v1p148/r2.speaker: عبد الله
ABDURRAZZAQ:v1p148/r2.claim: Abdullah ibn Masud tells a guardian not to buy an item from the orphans’ inheritance and not to borrow any of their property.
ABDURRAZZAQ:v1p148/r2.anchor: عبد الله رجل من همدان على فرس أبلق فقال إن عمي أوصى إلي بتركته وإن هذا من تركته أفأشتريه قال لا ولا تستقرض من أموالهم

ABDURRAZZAQ:v1p148/r3.author: ʿAbd al-Razzāq al-Ṣanʿānī
ABDURRAZZAQ:v1p148/r3.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
ABDURRAZZAQ:v1p148/r3.claim: The Prophet tells a guardian he may discipline an orphan as he would his own child and use the orphan’s wealth reasonably, without accumulating wealth or shielding his own assets with it.
ABDURRAZZAQ:v1p148/r3.anchor: قال رجل للنبي صلى الله عليه وسلم إن في حجري يتيما أفأضربه قال مما كنت منه ضاربا ولدك

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p491/r9.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p491/r9.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p491/r9.claim: Ānasa means to perceive or sense; al-Farra glosses it as finding, al-Zajjaj as knowing, Ata as seeing, and Ibn Abbas as recognizing, close in meaning.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p491/r9.anchor: وقال الفراء: وجد. وقال الزجاج: علم. وقال عطاء: أبصر

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p518/r4.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p518/r4.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p518/r4.claim: One occasion report says Rifa'a died leaving the young Thabit, whose guardian asked what use of the estate was lawful and when it should be handed over.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p518/r4.anchor: توفي رفاعة وترك ابنه ثابتا صغيرا فسأل: إن ابن أخي في حجري

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p518/r5.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p518/r5.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p518/r5.claim: Another account says Aws b. Thabit or Aws b. Suwayd died leaving Umm Kujja, three daughters, and two cousins, who seized the estate and excluded the women.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p518/r5.anchor: توفي أوس بن ثابت، ويقال: أوس بن سويد عن زوجته أم كجة وثلاث بنات

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p518/r6.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p518/r6.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p518/r6.claim: In pre-Islamic custom, women, daughters, and young boys did not inherit; Umm Kujja complained, and male relatives argued her sons could not fight or carry burdens, so the Prophet awaited revelation.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p518/r6.anchor: وكانوا في الجاهلية لا يورثون النساء ولا البنات ولا الابن الصغير الذكر

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p518/r7.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p518/r7.speaker: ابن عباس، السدي، مقاتل، سفيان
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p518/r7.claim: They define testing orphans as testing their judgment; al-Tha'labi adds judgment, religion, care of property, and sound management.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p518/r7.anchor: ابتلاء اليتامى اختبارهم في عقولهم قاله: ابن عباس والسدي، ومقاتل، وسفيان

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p518/r8.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p518/r8.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p518/r8.claim: A boy can be tested with a small amount of money under supervision; a girl can be entrusted with household work and managing wool production, payments, and receipt.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p518/r8.anchor: أن يدفع إليه نزر يسير من المال يتصرف فيه، والوصي يراعي حاله

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p518/r9.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p518/r9.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p518/r9.claim: Testing should suit each child's abilities and work; after puberty, if maturity appears, the estate is handed over and witnessed, with witnessing following delivery.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p518/r9.anchor: فإذا أنس منه الرشد بعد البلوغ والاختبار دفع إليه ماله

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p519/r1.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p519/r1.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p519/r1.claim: The maturity that must be observed is the maturity made a condition in the verse.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p519/r1.anchor: والإشهاد الإيناس المشروط. وقال ابن سيرين: لا يدفع إليه

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p519/r2.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p519/r2.speaker: ابن سيرين
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p519/r2.claim: Ibn Sirin would wait a year after maturity testing, so the child experiences all four seasons before transfer.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p519/r2.anchor: لا يدفع إليه بعد الإيناس والاختبار المذكورين حتى تمضي عليه سنة

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p519/r3.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p519/r3.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p519/r3.claim: The verse does not specify the legal age or the signs of puberty; juristic works discuss those questions.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p519/r3.anchor: ولم تتعرض الآية لسن البلوغ، ولا بماذا يكون

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p519/r4.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p519/r4.speaker: الجمهور
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p519/r4.claim: The apparent rule, adopted by the majority, keeps an immature person under restraint indefinitely and withholds the estate.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p519/r4.anchor: ولا يدفع إليه المال، وبه قال الجمهور. وقال النخعي وأبو حنيفة

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p519/r5.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p519/r5.speaker: النخعي، أبو حنيفة
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p519/r5.claim: Al-Nakha'i and Abu Hanifa wait until age twenty-five, then release the property whether discernment is evident or not.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p519/r5.anchor: وقال النخعي وأبو حنيفة: ينتظر به خمس وعشرون سنة

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p519/r6.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p519/r6.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p519/r6.claim: The apparent wording gives the guardian independent authority to hand over the estate.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p519/r6.anchor: وظاهر الآية يدل على استبداد الوصي بالدفع والاستقلال به

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p519/r7.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p519/r7.speaker: طائفة
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p519/r7.claim: Some require the guardian to present the case to a judge and establish maturity, or to be someone the judge trusts.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p519/r7.anchor: يفتقر إلى أن يدفعه إلى السلطان ويثبت عنده رشده

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p519/r8.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p519/r8.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p519/r8.claim: The general word orphans includes daughters, who therefore receive the same treatment as sons.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p519/r8.anchor: وظاهر عموم اليتامى اندراج البنات في هذا الحكم

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p519/r9.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p519/r9.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p519/r9.claim: Reported daughter-specific waiting rules include maturity without marriage, five years after consummation, a year, or seven years with a father versus one year for an orphan without a guardian.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p519/r9.anchor: فقيل: يعتبر رشدها، وإن لم تتزوج بالبلوغ

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p519/r10.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p519/r10.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p519/r10.claim: حتى marks the end of testing, introduces إذا, and the response to إذا is فإن آنستم, followed by the response to إن, فادفعوا; maturity is observed after puberty.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p519/r10.anchor: وحتى هنا غاية للابتلاء، ودخلت على الشرط وهو: إذا

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p519/r11.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p519/r11.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p519/r11.claim: Some grammarians say the clause after حتى is genitive; most say حتى governs nothing, as in poetic examples beginning وحتى.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p519/r11.anchor: ذهب الزجاج وابن درستويه إلى أن الجملة في موضع جر

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p519/r12.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p519/r12.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p519/r12.claim: بلغوا النكاح elliptically means reaching the age or time for marriage.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p519/r12.anchor: وفي قوله: بلغوا النكاح تقدير محذوف وهو: بلغوا حد النكاح أو وقته

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p519/r13.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p519/r13.speaker: ابن عباس، عطاء، الفراء، الزجاج
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p519/r13.claim: They gloss آنستم as knew, saw, found, and knew, respectively; these meanings are close.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p519/r13.anchor: وقال ابن عباس: معنى آنستم عرفتم. وقال عطاء: رأيتم

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p519/r14.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p519/r14.speaker: ابن مسعود
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p519/r14.claim: Ibn Masud reads فإن أحستم, deleting the medial radical from أحسستم; the deletion is rare, though others report it as the dialect of Sulaym and productive with some attached pronouns.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p519/r14.anchor: وقرأ ابن مسعود: فإن أحستم، يريد أحسستم

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p519/r15.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p519/r15.speaker: ابن مسعود، أبو عبد الرحمن، أبو السمال، عيسى الثقفي
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p519/r15.claim: They read رشدا with fatḥa on both letters; an anomalous reading has ḍamma on both.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p519/r15.anchor: وقرأ ابن مسعود وأبو عبد الرحمن وأبو السمال وعيسى الثقفي: رشدا بفتحتين

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p519/r16.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p519/r16.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p519/r16.claim: رشدا is indefinite because it means a kind or aspect of maturity; one need not wait for complete maturity.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p519/r16.anchor: وقرىء شاذا: رشدا بضمتين، ونكر رشدا لأن معناه نوع

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p520/r1.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p520/r1.speaker: ابن عطية، مالك
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p520/r1.claim: Ibn Atiyya and Malik require both puberty and discernment before property is handed over.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p520/r1.anchor: قال ابن عطية ومالك: يرى الشرطين: البلوغ والرشد

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p520/r2.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p520/r2.speaker: أبو حنيفة
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p520/r2.claim: Abu Hanifa considers either condition sufficient unless folly is known, comparing this to the rule for concubinage.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p520/r2.anchor: وأبو حنيفة: يرى أن يدفع المال بالشرط الواحد ما لم يحفظ له سفه

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p520/r3.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p520/r3.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p520/r3.claim: The analogy fails: puberty is not stated as a cause of transfer but marks the usual age when judgment matures; discernment is tested then, as shown by إذا for timing and إن for the condition.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p520/r3.anchor: وذلك أن البلوغ لم تسقه الآية سببا في الشرط

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p520/r4.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p520/r4.speaker: سيبويه
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p520/r4.claim: Sibawayh allows إذا to function as a conditional particle in poetry under necessity because it needs a response and is followed by a verb.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p520/r4.anchor: وأجاز سيبويه أن يجازى بها في الشعر

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p520/r5.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p520/r5.speaker: الخليل
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p520/r5.claim: Al-Khalil argues إذا is not itself conditional because what follows is expected to happen: one says one will come when dates redden, not if they redden.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p520/r5.anchor: واحتج الخليل على منع شرطيتها بحصول ما بعدها

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p520/r6.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p520/r6.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p520/r6.claim: Abu Hayyan rejects the claim that إذا lacks conditional sense: grammarians broadly treat it as a future adverb usually carrying conditional meaning, even though it does not govern jussive mood.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p520/r6.anchor: بل النحويون كالمجمعين على أن إذا ظرف لما يستقبل فيه معنى الشرط غالبا

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p520/r7.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p520/r7.speaker: مالك
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p520/r7.claim: If a person becomes mature and then returns to foolishness, Malik says the restriction is reinstated.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p520/r7.anchor: ثم عاد إلى السفه، أيعود الحجر عليه أم لا؟ وفيه قولان: قال مالك: يعود

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p520/r8.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p520/r8.speaker: أبو حنيفة
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p520/r8.claim: Abu Hanifa says a restriction is not reinstated after maturity; the two views are also reported from al-Shafi'i.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p520/r8.anchor: وقال أبو حنيفة: لا يعود، والقولان عن الشافعي

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p520/r9.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p520/r9.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p520/r9.claim: Eating here stands for taking property because consumption is the main use of what is taken.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p520/r9.anchor: تقدم أنه يعبر بالأكل عن الأخذ، لأن الأكل أعظم وجوه الانتفاع بالمأخوذ

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p520/r10.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p520/r10.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p520/r10.claim: The prohibition on consuming or wasting the estate is an independent sentence, not coordinated with the command to hand it over, which follows the puberty condition.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p520/r10.anchor: هذه الجملة مستقلة. نهاهم تعالى عن أكل أموال اليتامى وإتلافها

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p520/r11.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p520/r11.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p520/r11.claim: Reading the prohibition as coordinated with فادفعوا would create a hardship by conditioning it on puberty; neither the wording nor its opposite makes eating otherwise lawful.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p520/r11.anchor: وبهذا الذي قررناه يتضح خطأ من جعل ولا تأكلوها عطفا على فادفعوا

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p520/r12.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p520/r12.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p520/r12.claim: إسراف is excessive spending, and سرف is error in where one spends.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p520/r12.anchor: والإسراف: الإفراط في الإنفاق، والسرف الخطأ في مواضع الإنفاق

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p520#2/r1.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p520#2/r1.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p520#2/r1.claim: A poem about giving generously describes the gifts as containing no miserliness or waste, illustrating proper spending.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p520#2/r1.anchor: ما في عطائهم من ولا سرف

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p520#2/r2.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p520#2/r2.speaker: ابن عباس وغيره
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p520#2/r2.claim: They say rushing means the guardian hastens to exploit the ward's estate before the ward matures, claiming to act before the child can take it back.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p520#2/r2.anchor: قال ابن عباس وغيره: ومبادرة كبرهم أن الوصي

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p520#2/r3.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p520#2/r3.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p520#2/r3.claim: إسرافا and بدارا may be circumstantial verbal nouns or reasons; بدار can suggest a race between the child growing and guardian taking property, or the guardian alone, and أن يكبروا may be the object of the verbal noun or express fear.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p520#2/r3.anchor: وانتصب إسرافا وبدارا على أنهما مصدران في موضع الحال

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p520#2/r4.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p520#2/r4.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p520#2/r4.claim: The apparent division addresses the guardian: a rich guardian should refrain, while a poor guardian may take only modest food carefully assessed.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p520#2/r4.anchor: ظاهر هذه الجملة يدل على أنه تقسيم لحال الوصي على اليتيم

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p520#2/r5.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p520#2/r5.speaker: إبراهيم، عطاء، الحسن، قتادة
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p520#2/r5.claim: They say the reasonable amount is a modest allowance for necessities; no liability attaches and it need not be repaid if the guardian later becomes solvent, a view followed by jurists.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p520#2/r5.anchor: ولا يقضي إذا أيسر قاله: ابراهيم، وعطاء، والحسن، وقتادة

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p520#2/r6.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p520#2/r6.speaker: عمر، ابن عباس، عبيدة، الشعبي، أبو العالية، ابن جبير
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p520#2/r6.claim: They require repayment once solvent and forbid borrowing beyond need; al-Awzai also holds this view.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p520#2/r6.anchor: وقال عمر، وابن عباس، وعبيدة، والشعبي، ومجاهد، وأبو العالية، وابن جبير: يقضي إذا أيسر

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p520#2/r7.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p520#2/r7.speaker: ابن عباس، أبو العالية، الحسن، الشعبي
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p520#2/r7.claim: They limit reasonable use to small customary amounts of milk or dates and prohibit taking the principal assets.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p520#2/r7.anchor: وقال ابن عباس أيضا وأبو العالية، والحسن، والشعبي: إنما يأكل بالمعروف

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p520#2/r8.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p520#2/r8.speaker: طائفة، الإمام أحمد
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p520#2/r8.claim: Some say reasonable means compensation proportionate to the guardian's service; one report attributes this to Ahmad.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p520#2/r8.anchor: وقالت طائفة: المعروف أن يكون له أجر بقدر عمله

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p520#2/r9.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p520#2/r9.speaker: الحسن بن حي
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p520#2/r9.claim: Hasan b. Hayy distinguishes a father-appointed guardian, who may eat reasonably, from a judge-appointed guardian, who must seek wages from the public treasury.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p520#2/r9.anchor: فصل الحسن بن حي فقال: إن كان وصي أب فله الأكل بالمعروف

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p520#2/r10.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p520#2/r10.speaker: أبو حنيفة وصاحباه
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p520#2/r10.claim: Abu Hanifa and his two companions allow a guardian who is traveling to take what he needs but not to retain anything; a resident may take nothing.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p520#2/r10.anchor: وفصل أبو حنيفة وصاحباه فقالوا: إن كان وصي اليتيم مقيما

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p520#2/r11.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p520#2/r11.speaker: الشعبي
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p520#2/r11.claim: Al-Sha'bi permits taking only in dire need, like eating carrion, and requires repayment when able; travel or residence alone makes no difference.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p520#2/r11.anchor: وفصل الشعبي فقال: إن كان مضطرا بحال من

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p522/r1.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p522/r1.speaker: مجاهد
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p522/r1.claim: Mujahid says the permission to eat is abrogated by the warning against devouring orphan property in 4:10.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p522/r1.anchor: وقال مجاهد: هذه الإباحة منسوخة بقوله: إن الذين يأكلون أموال اليتامى ظلما

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p522/r2.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p522/r2.speaker: أبو يوسف
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p522/r2.claim: Abu Yusuf suggests the permission may be abrogated by the ban on consuming one another's property wrongfully in 2:188, so a guardian may take neither loan nor other payment.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p522/r2.anchor: وقال أبو يوسف: لعلها منسوخة بقوله: ولا تأكلوا أموالكم بينكم بالباطل

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p522/r3.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p522/r3.speaker: ابن عباس، النخعي
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p522/r3.claim: They say this is about the guardian's own wealth: the wealthy should be self-sufficient and the poor should manage their own assets rather than need the orphan's property; al-Kiya al-Tabari chooses this view among Shafi'is.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p522/r3.anchor: هذا الأمر ليس متعلقا بمال اليتيم

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p522/r4.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p522/r4.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p522/r4.claim: Some allow a wage from a large estate when managing it occupies the guardian's time; with little work, nothing is due, though modest customary food may be given without harm.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p522/r4.anchor: إن كان مال اليتيم كثيرا يحتاج إلى قيام كثير عليه

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p522/r5.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p522/r5.speaker: ربيعة، يحيى بن سعيد
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p522/r5.claim: They say the verse divides the orphans' circumstances rather than guardians': spend frugally from a wealthy ward's estate and according to a poor ward's means, with guardians addressed indirectly.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p522/r5.anchor: هذا تقسيم لحال اليتيم، لا لحال الوصي

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p522/r6.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p522/r6.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p522/r6.claim: The disagreements concern whether the division describes guardian or child; whether it concerns the guardian's or child's property; abrogation; the type of taking, eligible guardians, permissible items, wages, and repayment.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p522/r6.anchor: فهذه أقوال ملخصها: هل تقسيم في الولي أو الصبي قولان

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p522/r7.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p522/r7.speaker: الشعبي
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p522/r7.claim: The necessity-only view allows only enough as with carrion, requires repayment if possible, and applies whether the guardian is traveling or at home.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p522/r7.anchor: يجوز له أكل الميتة أكل بقدر حاجته ورد إذا وجد

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p522#2/r1.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p522#2/r1.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p522#2/r1.claim: If a guardian takes something that is not a wage, jurists further dispute whether it becomes a debt repayable upon solvency.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p522#2/r1.anchor: فهل يترتب دينا في ذمته يجب قضاؤه إذا أيسر أم لا؟

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p522#2/r2.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p522#2/r2.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p522#2/r2.claim: فليستعفف is more emphatic than فليعف because it asks for increased restraint.

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p522#2/r3.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p522#2/r3.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p522#2/r3.claim: Witnessing delivery prevents disputes and suspicion, protects the guardian from liability if the ward denies receipt, reassures the ward, and marks release from restraint for ordinary dealings.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p522#2/r3.anchor: أمر تعالى بالإشهاد لحسم مادة النزاع، وسوء الظن بهم

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p522#2/r4.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p522#2/r4.speaker: أبو حنيفة وأصحابه، مالك
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p522#2/r4.claim: If there are no witnesses and the ward accuses the guardian, these authorities accept the guardian's statement with an oath.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p522#2/r4.anchor: عند أبي حنيفة وأصحابه، وعند مالك

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p522#2/r5.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p522#2/r5.speaker: الشافعي
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p522#2/r5.claim: Al-Shafi'i requires the guardian to produce evidence if he did not witness the transfer.

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p522#2/r6.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p522#2/r6.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p522#2/r6.claim: The apparent wording makes witnessing obligatory, though some say it is recommended.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p522#2/r6.anchor: وظاهر الأمر أنه واجب. وقال قوم: هو ندب

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p522#2/r7.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p522#2/r7.speaker: عمرو بن جبير
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p522#2/r7.claim: Amr b. Jubayr limits witnessing to repayment by a guardian of money borrowed from an orphan while poor and repaid after becoming solvent.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p522#2/r7.anchor: هذا الإشهاد إنما هو على دفع الولي ما استقرضه من مال اليتيم

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p522#2/r8.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p522#2/r8.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p522#2/r8.claim: Other interpretations say the verse requires witnessing repayment of anything taken from the orphan, or documenting expenditures on the ward so a later dispute can be resolved; a trust received with witnesses is discharged only by witnessed return.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p522#2/r8.anchor: فإن مالا قبض على وجه الأمانة بإشهاد لا يبرأ منه إلا بإشهاد على دفعه

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p522#2/r9.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p522#2/r9.speaker: الأعمش، الطبري
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p522#2/r9.claim: They explain حسيبا as sufficient to testify, from a verb meaning to suffice; other senses are one who reckons or accounts for deeds and recompenses them, warning against lying.

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p522#2/r10.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p522#2/r10.speaker: ابن عباس، السدي، مقاتل
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p522#2/r10.claim: They gloss حسيبا as a witness.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p522#2/r10.anchor: وقال ابن عباس والسدي ومقاتل: معنى حسيبا شهيدا

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p522#2/r11.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p522#2/r11.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p522#2/r11.claim: حسيب may be a reciprocal intensive noun or a strengthened active participle; grammarians also disagree whether كفى is a verb or a noun of action and whether its subject is Allah or an implicit مصدر.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p522#2/r11.anchor: وفي كفى خلاف: أهي اسم فعل، أم فعل؟

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p522#2/r12.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p522#2/r12.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p522#2/r12.claim: The sound parse makes كفى a verb with Allah as subject and an extra ب; an alternative requires the Kufan allowance for an implicit verbal noun to govern its complement, which Basrans reject.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p522#2/r12.anchor: والصحيح أنها فعل، وفاعله اسم الله، والباء زائدة

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p523/r9.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p523/r9.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p523/r9.claim: حسيبا may be accusative as specification or circumstance; كفى can omit its object here, unlike uses where it takes two objects such as 5:48.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p523/r9.anchor: وانتصب حسيبا على التمييز لصلاحية دخول من عليه

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p531/r2.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p531/r2.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p531/r2.claim: It repeats key words and meanings: fear, creation, orphan, women, inheritance, and guarding against injustice.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p531/r2.anchor: والتكرار في: اتقوا، وفي: خلق، وفي: خفتم، وأن لا تقسطوا،

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p531/r7.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p531/r7.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p531/r7.claim: The matching forms in “hand over” and “when you hand over” create perfect paronomasia.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p531/r7.anchor: والتجنيس المماثل في: فادفعوا فإذا دفعتم، والمغاير في: وقولوا لهم قولا.

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p531/r9.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p531/r9.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p531/r9.claim: The added force in فليستعفف intensifies the meaning of seeking restraint.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p531/r9.anchor: والزيادة للزيادة في المعنى في: فليستعفف.

ALUSI-FULL:v4p203#2/r1.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v4p203#2/r1.speaker: شيخ الإسلام
ALUSI-FULL:v4p203#2/r1.claim: Shaykh al-Islam says the command begins specifying when and on what condition orphan wealth is returned, following the general order to give it and the ban on entrusting it to fools.
ALUSI-FULL:v4p203#2/r1.anchor: شروع في تعيين وقت تسليم أموال اليتامى إليهم وبيان شرطه بعد الأمر بإيتائها على الإطلاق

ALUSI-FULL:v4p203#2/r2.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v4p203#2/r2.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v4p203#2/r2.claim: This connection is clearer if the earlier fools are wasteful orphans; it is less clear if all orphans are called foolish based on their childhood, as another account has it.
ALUSI-FULL:v4p203#2/r2.anchor: على تقدير أن يراد من السفهاء المبذرين بالفعل من اليتامى

ALUSI-FULL:v4p203#2/r3.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v4p203#2/r3.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v4p203#2/r3.claim: Another view treats the verse as a return to orphan-property rulings rather than a new beginning, on the premise that the preceding material was a digression.
ALUSI-FULL:v4p203#2/r3.anchor: وقيل : إن هذا رجوع إلى بيان الأحكام المتعلقة بأموال اليتامى

ALUSI-FULL:v4p203#2/r4.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v4p203#2/r4.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v4p203#2/r4.claim: The guardians are addressed; test orphans by observing their ability to manage property and transact prudently.

ALUSI-FULL:v4p203#2/r5.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v4p203#2/r5.speaker: أبو حنيفة
ALUSI-FULL:v4p203#2/r5.claim: Abu Hanifa takes sound financial management as the test’s criterion.
ALUSI-FULL:v4p203#2/r5.anchor: والإقتصار على هذا الإهتداء رأي أب يحنيفة

ALUSI-FULL:v4p203#2/r6.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v4p203#2/r6.speaker: الشافعي
ALUSI-FULL:v4p203#2/r6.claim: Al-Shafiʿi additionally requires uprightness in religion, a view also attributed to Ibn Jubayr, Ibn Abbas, and al-Hasan.
ALUSI-FULL:v4p203#2/r6.anchor: والشافعي رحمه الله تعالى يعتبر مع هذا أيضا الصلاح في الدين

ALUSI-FULL:v4p203#2/r7.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v4p203#2/r7.speaker: أبو حنيفة والشافعي
ALUSI-FULL:v4p203#2/r7.claim: Abu Hanifa and al-Shafiʿi agree that the trial takes place before puberty, as the verse’s endpoint indicates; Malik places it after puberty.
ALUSI-FULL:v4p203#2/r7.anchor: وأتفق الإمامان رضي الله تعالى عنهما على أن هذا الإختبار قبل البلوغ

ALUSI-FULL:v4p203#2/r8.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v4p203#2/r8.speaker: أبو حنيفة
ALUSI-FULL:v4p203#2/r8.claim: Abu Hanifa reasons that testing before puberty requires permission for a discerning minor to buy and sell under the guardian’s supervision.
ALUSI-FULL:v4p203#2/r8.anchor: لأن ذلك الإختبار إنما يحصل إذا أذن له في البيع والشراء مثلا

ALUSI-FULL:v4p203#2/r9.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v4p203#2/r9.speaker: الشافعي
ALUSI-FULL:v4p203#2/r9.claim: Al-Shafiʿi says testing need not authorize transactions or hand over property: the guardian can make the contract after observing the minor’s ability.
ALUSI-FULL:v4p203#2/r9.anchor: الإختبار لا يقتضي الإذن في التصرف لأنه يتوقف على دفع المال إلى اليتيم

ALUSI-FULL:v4p203#2/r10.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v4p203#2/r10.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v4p203#2/r10.claim: Reaching marriageable age means puberty, through a wet dream or age; fifteen is the limit for al-Shafiʿi, Abu Yusuf, Muhammad, and a transmitted Hanafi position adopted in the school.
ALUSI-FULL:v4p203#2/r10.anchor: أي إذا بلغوا حد البلوغ وهو إما بالإحتلام أو بالسن

ALUSI-FULL:v4p203#2/r11.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v4p203#2/r11.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v4p203#2/r11.claim: The common arrival at marriageable fitness by fifteen supports that age; al-Bayhaqi himself calls weak the report from Anas that property records and legal penalties begin at fifteen.
ALUSI-FULL:v4p203#2/r11.anchor: لما أن العادة الفاشية أن الغلام والجارية يصلحان للنكاح وثمرته في هذه المدة

ALUSI-FULL:v4p203#2/r12.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v4p203#2/r12.speaker: أبو حنيفة
ALUSI-FULL:v4p203#2/r12.claim: The well-known Hanafi view sets puberty at eighteen for boys and seventeen for girls, based on reaching maturity; Ibn Abbas and al-Qutaybi are cited for eighteen.
ALUSI-FULL:v4p203#2/r12.anchor: وشاع عن الإمام الأعظم أن السن للغلام تمام ثماني عشرة سنة وولجارية

ALUSI-FULL:v4p203#2/r13.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v4p203#2/r13.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v4p203#2/r13.claim: One report from Abu Hanifa gives nineteen for a boy, meaning he enters his nineteenth year after completing eighteen; the transmissions vary.
ALUSI-FULL:v4p203#2/r13.anchor: وعنه في الغلام تسع عشرة سنة والمراد أن يطعن في التاسعة عشرة

ALUSI-FULL:v4p204/r1.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v4p204/r1.speaker: الشافعي
ALUSI-FULL:v4p204/r1.claim: Al-Shafiʿi is often said to use pubic hair growth as evidence of puberty among captured polytheists whose true age is unknown, deciding whether to apply adult or child treatment.
ALUSI-FULL:v4p204/r1.anchor: وشاع عن الإمام الشافعي أنه قد جعل الإنبات دليلا على البلوغ في المشركين خاصة

ALUSI-FULL:v4p204/r2.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v4p204/r2.speaker: ابن حزم
ALUSI-FULL:v4p204/r2.claim: Ibn Hazm denounces al-Shafiʿi over the pubic-hair ruling; al-Alusi says the denunciation is unwarranted because it is only a practical marker in a case where age cannot be known.

ALUSI-FULL:v4p204/r3.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v4p204/r3.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v4p204/r3.claim: The captured adolescent might lie to avoid death, unlike a Muslim; examination therefore supplies an indicator in this case, not a separate general puberty criterion for unbelievers.
ALUSI-FULL:v4p204/r3.anchor: ولا يخفى أن هذا لا يصلح محلا للتشنيع

ALUSI-FULL:v4p204/r4.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v4p204/r4.speaker: مجاهد
ALUSI-FULL:v4p204/r4.claim: Mujahid explains anastum as perceived or sensed.

ALUSI-FULL:v4p204/r5.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v4p204/r5.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v4p204/r5.claim: Anasa originally described looking toward an approaching person with a hand shielding the eye, then broadened to perception; the verse may use literal or figurative perception.
ALUSI-FULL:v4p204/r5.anchor: وأصل معنى الإستئناسكما قال الشهاب التظر من بعد

ALUSI-FULL:v4p204/r6.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v4p204/r6.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v4p204/r6.claim: A poet’s use of anastu for perceiving a sound as evening approaches supports the verb’s sense of noticing.

ALUSI-FULL:v4p205/r1.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v4p205/r1.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v4p205/r1.claim: Some derive anasa from the eye’s pupil and take its original meaning to be seeing generally; al-Alusi leaves both literal and figurative senses possible here.
ALUSI-FULL:v4p205/r1.anchor: وزعم بعضهم أن أصله الإبصار مطلقا وأنه أخذ من إنسان العين

ALUSI-FULL:v4p205/r2.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v4p205/r2.speaker: ابن مسعود
ALUSI-FULL:v4p205/r2.claim: Ibn Masud’s variant ahastum drops one doubled s after shifting its vowel; it may instead be a regular Sulaymi dialect pattern for doubled roots with attached pronouns.
ALUSI-FULL:v4p205/r2.anchor: وقرأ ابن مسعود أحستم بحاء مفتوحة وسين ساكنة وأصله أحسستم

ALUSI-FULL:v4p205/r3.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v4p205/r3.speaker: أبو زيد الطائي
ALUSI-FULL:v4p205/r3.claim: Abu Zayd al-Taʾi’s verse supplies evidence for the dialectal treatment of a doubled verb with a pronoun.
ALUSI-FULL:v4p205/r3.anchor: وقيل : إنها لغة سليم وإنها مطردة في عين كل فعل مضاعف

ALUSI-FULL:v4p205/r4.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v4p205/r4.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v4p205/r4.claim: Rushd means financial discernment and prudent management, or, in another view, religious rectitude as well as sound financial judgment.
ALUSI-FULL:v4p205/r4.anchor: أي إهتداءا إلى ضبط الأموال وحسن التصرف فيها وقيل : صلاحا

ALUSI-FULL:v4p205/r5.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v4p205/r5.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v4p205/r5.claim: Readers pronounce rushd with either fatha or damma, both meaning maturity; another distinction assigns worldly and afterlife maturity to the damma and only afterlife maturity to the fatha.
ALUSI-FULL:v4p205/r5.anchor: وقريء رشدا بفتحتين ورشدا بضمتين وهما بمعنى رشدا

ALUSI-FULL:v4p205/r6.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v4p205/r6.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v4p205/r6.claim: The fa in give them their property signals prompt delivery at the point of entitlement; some also see a semantic distinction between paying it over here and the earlier verb give.
ALUSI-FULL:v4p205/r6.anchor: من غير تأخير عن حد البلوغ كما تدل عليه الفاء

ALUSI-FULL:v4p205/r7.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v4p205/r7.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v4p205/r7.claim: Hatta can introduce a full clause without losing its endpoint sense; here the conditional clause sets the end of testing and its fulfillment governs delivery.
ALUSI-FULL:v4p205/r7.anchor: وتسمى ابتدائية في ذلك ولا يذهب منها معنى الغاية

ALUSI-FULL:v4p205/r8.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v4p205/r8.speaker: ابن مالك
ALUSI-FULL:v4p205/r8.claim: Ibn Malik treats a later condition as modifying the first like a circumstantial clause; a competing analysis makes the first condition’s answer serve as the answer to subsequent ones.
ALUSI-FULL:v4p205/r8.anchor: وزعم ابن مالك أن الشرط الثاني مقيد للأول بمنزلة الحال

ALUSI-FULL:v4p205/r9.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v4p205/r9.speaker: الشافعي
ALUSI-FULL:v4p205/r9.claim: The preferred grammatical analysis makes each later condition’s answer implicit from the preceding answer, requiring the conditions to occur in reverse nesting order; al-Jassas says Muhammad and Abu Yusuf also dispute the issue.
ALUSI-FULL:v4p205/r9.anchor: والصحيح في هذه المسألة أن الجواب للأول وجواب الثاني محذوف

ALUSI-FULL:v4p205/r10.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v4p205/r10.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v4p205/r10.claim: Other jurists make the final condition and its answer govern the preceding ones; some require all conditions in any order, while conjunctions alter which conditions the answer covers.
ALUSI-FULL:v4p205/r10.anchor: وقال بعض الفقهاء : الجواب للأخير والشرط الأخير وجوابه جواب الثاني

ALUSI-FULL:v4p205/r11.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v4p205/r11.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v4p205/r11.claim: Al-Alusi endorses the lower-complexity analysis associated with al-Zamakhshari and al-Zajjaj: hatta governs the whole temporal clause, idha remains temporal, and delivery follows puberty plus financial maturity.
ALUSI-FULL:v4p205/r11.anchor: وما نحن فيه من المقرون بالفاء وهي رابطة للجواب كالفاء الثانية

ALUSI-FULL:v4p205/r12.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v4p205/r12.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v4p205/r12.claim: The contrast between idha for puberty and in for maturity reflects certainty of the former and uncertainty of the latter.
ALUSI-FULL:v4p205/r12.anchor: وعبر في البلوغ بإذا وفي الإيناس بإن للفرق بينهما ظهورا وخفاءا

ALUSI-FULL:v4p205/r13.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v4p205/r13.speaker: مجاهد
ALUSI-FULL:v4p205/r13.claim: Mujahid says property is not returned even if an orphan’s hair turns gray unless financial maturity is perceived.
ALUSI-FULL:v4p205/r13.anchor: به قال مجاهد فقد أخرج إبن المنذر وغيره عنه أنه قال : لا يدفع إلى اليتيم ماله

ALUSI-FULL:v4p205/r14.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v4p205/r14.speaker: الشافعي
ALUSI-FULL:v4p205/r14.claim: Al-Shafiʿi and the two Hanafi disciples follow the verse’s apparent requirement that property is withheld if puberty arrives without financial maturity.
ALUSI-FULL:v4p205/r14.anchor: وهو مذهب الشافعي وقول الإمامين وبه قال مجاهد

ALUSI-FULL:v4p205/r15.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v4p205/r15.speaker: أبو حنيفة
ALUSI-FULL:v4p205/r15.claim: Abu Hanifa requires delivery seven years after puberty even without perceived maturity, because the period permits change and education; he reads the earlier general command to give orphans their property as applying after puberty.
ALUSI-FULL:v4p205/r15.anchor: إذا زادت عل ى سن البلوغ سبع سنين وهي مدة معتبرة فى تغير الأحوال

ALUSI-FULL:v4p205/r16.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v4p205/r16.speaker: عمر
ALUSI-FULL:v4p205/r16.claim: Umar is cited as saying a man’s intellect reaches completion at twenty-five.
ALUSI-FULL:v4p205/r16.anchor: فقد ورد عن عمر رضي الله تعالى عنه أنه قال : ينتهي لب الرجل

ALUSI-FULL:v4p205/r17.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v4p205/r17.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v4p205/r17.claim: Al-Alusi reasons that time and experience eventually remove childhood traces and produce some maturity because this is the mind’s age of completion.
ALUSI-FULL:v4p205/r17.anchor: وإذا أمتد الزمان وظهرت الخبرة والتجربة لم يبق أثر الصبا

ALUSI-FULL:v4p206/r1.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v4p206/r1.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v4p206/r1.claim: The philosophers’ biological argument doubles the earliest period in which a boy could father a child and that child could in turn reproduce.
ALUSI-FULL:v4p206/r1.anchor: ففي هذه المدة يمكن أن يولد له ابن ثم ضعف هذا المبلغ يولد لابنه ابن

ALUSI-FULL:v4p206/r2.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v4p206/r2.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v4p206/r2.claim: Al-Alusi notes that the Hanafi argument from give the orphans their property depends on reading it as delivery after puberty, an interpretation already debated.
ALUSI-FULL:v4p206/r2.anchor: على أن المراد بالإيتاء فيها الدفع وقد مر الكلام في ذلك

ALUSI-FULL:v4p206/r3.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v4p206/r3.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v4p206/r3.claim: Critics argue that if any maturity inevitably appears by twenty-five, Abu Hanifa’s position collapses into the other imams’ rule; al-Alusi says financial competence need not arise by that age, while generic maturity would not satisfy the verse.
ALUSI-FULL:v4p206/r3.anchor: إذا كان ضرب من الرشد كافيا كما يشعر به التنكير وكان ذلك حاصلا لا محالة في ذلك السن

ALUSI-FULL:v4p206/r4.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v4p206/r4.speaker: الفخر
ALUSI-FULL:v4p206/r4.claim: Al-Fakhr says the test concerns protecting property, so the required maturity is competence in managing its interests; otherwise the verse’s clauses would be disconnected.
ALUSI-FULL:v4p206/r4.anchor: لا شك أن المراد من ابتلاء اليتامى المأمور به ابتلاؤهم فيما يتعلق بمصالح حفظ المال

ALUSI-FULL:v4p206/r5.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v4p206/r5.speaker: الفخر
ALUSI-FULL:v4p206/r5.claim: Al-Fakhr’s clear analogy says an adult or elder without the reason needed to preserve and use property should remain barred from it just as a child is.
ALUSI-FULL:v4p206/r5.anchor: فإذا كان هذا المعنى حاصلا في الشاب والشيخ كانا في حكم الصبي

ALUSI-FULL:v4p206/r6.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v4p206/r6.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v4p206/r6.claim: Al-Alusi condemns Ibn Hazm and his Shiʿi followers for vilifying Abu Hanifa over this subsidiary disagreement while often relying on weaker evidence elsewhere.
ALUSI-FULL:v4p206/r6.anchor: ولقوة كلام المخالف في هذه المسألة شنع الضال ابن حزم كعادته

ALUSI-FULL:v4p207/r1.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v4p207/r1.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v4p207/r1.claim: Al-Alusi defends Abu Hanifa: once an orphan reaches adulthood, he is accountable for belief, worship, choice, reward, and punishment, so keeping his property under another’s control resembles oppression.
ALUSI-FULL:v4p207/r1.anchor: كان منع ماله عنه وتصرف الغير به أشبه الأشياء بالظلم

ALUSI-FULL:v4p207/r2.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v4p207/r2.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v4p207/r2.claim: Although this reasoning might warrant immediate payment at puberty even without competence, payment is delayed until twenty-five to allow education, maturity, and restraint from waste.
ALUSI-FULL:v4p207/r2.anchor: إلا أنا أخرنا الدفع إلى هذه المدة للتأديب ورجاء الرشد والكف عن السفه

ALUSI-FULL:v4p207/r3.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v4p207/r3.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v4p207/r3.claim: The delay resembles, in one respect, holding the property of rebels until they return to obedience.
ALUSI-FULL:v4p207/r3.anchor: ونظير ذلك من وجه أخذ أموال البغاة وحبسها عنهم ليفيئوا

ALUSI-FULL:v4p207/r4.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v4p207/r4.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v4p207/r4.claim: Seven years was chosen because it commonly changes a child’s capacities; ten also marks change in the prayer hadith, but the lower sufficient period is adopted.
ALUSI-FULL:v4p207/r4.anchor: واعتبرت الزيادة سبع سنين لأنهاكما تقدممدة معتبرة في تغير الأحوال

ALUSI-FULL:v4p207/r5.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v4p207/r5.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v4p207/r5.claim: Al-Alusi denies that the restriction turns on every kind of foolishness or remains in force indefinitely; the relevant condition is childish incapacity and the legal school does not infer absence of consequence automatically from absence of a condition.
ALUSI-FULL:v4p207/r5.anchor: بل مع سفه الصبا ولا نسلم بقاءه بعد تلك المدة على أن التعليق بالشرط لا يوجب العدم

ALUSI-FULL:v4p207/r6.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v4p207/r6.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v4p207/r6.claim: The warning against consuming orphan property wastefully and before they grow supports Abu Hanifa’s view that property should not be withheld once they have grown, with the special delay for an immature adult explained earlier.
ALUSI-FULL:v4p207/r6.anchor: فإنه مشير إلى أنه لا يمنع مال اليتيم عنه إذا كبر

ALUSI-FULL:v4p207#2/r1.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v4p207#2/r1.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v4p207#2/r1.claim: Israf is exceeding what is permitted, by excess or shortfall; asrafa usually names excess and sarafa deficiency, while heedlessness or error is not intended here.
ALUSI-FULL:v4p207#2/r1.anchor: والإسراف في الأصل تجاوز الحد المباح إلى مالم يبح وربما كانذلك في الإفراط

ALUSI-FULL:v4p207#2/r2.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v4p207#2/r2.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v4p207#2/r2.claim: Mubadara means haste: the guardian may rush to consume the property before the orphan grows, while the orphan may hasten to reclaim it; the word is linked to fullness.
ALUSI-FULL:v4p207#2/r2.anchor: والمبادرة المسارعة وهي لأصل الفعل هنا وتصح المفاعلة فيه بأن يبادر الولي أخذ مال اليتيم

ALUSI-FULL:v4p207#2/r3.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v4p207#2/r3.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v4p207#2/r3.claim: The etymological examples are the full moon, a money bag filled with money, and a grain heap filled with food.
ALUSI-FULL:v4p207#2/r3.anchor: ومنه البدر لامتلائه نورا والبدرة لامتلائها بالمال والبيدر لامتلائه بالطعام

ALUSI-FULL:v4p207#2/r4.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v4p207#2/r4.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v4p207#2/r4.claim: The two coordinated accusatives are parsed as circumstantial accusatives, though some parse them as purpose clauses; this warning connects with the preceding prohibition, not the post-puberty conditional.
ALUSI-FULL:v4p207#2/r4.anchor: والأسمان المتعاطفان منصوبان على الحال كما أشرنا إليه وقيل : إنهما مفعول لهما

ALUSI-FULL:v4p207#2/r5.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v4p207#2/r5.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v4p207#2/r5.claim: With fatha, kabura concerns age; with damma it denotes capacity or eminence, and with ala it describes something burdensome.
ALUSI-FULL:v4p207#2/r5.anchor: بفتح الباء الموحدة من باب علم يستعمل في السن وأما بالضم فهو في القدرة والشرف

ALUSI-FULL:v4p207#2/r6.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v4p207#2/r6.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v4p207#2/r6.claim: The prohibition singles out eating, the basic and common use of wealth, so other forms of consuming it are prohibited all the more.
ALUSI-FULL:v4p207#2/r6.anchor: وتخصيص الأكل الذي هو أساس الانتفاع وتكثر الحاجة إليه بالنهي يدل على النهي عن غيره

ALUSI-FULL:v4p207#2/r7.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v4p207#2/r7.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v4p207#2/r7.claim: This warning reinforces the order to hand over the property and prepares for the rule distinguishing a wealthy guardian from a poor one.
ALUSI-FULL:v4p207#2/r7.anchor: وفي الجملة تأكيد للأمر بالدفع وتقرير لها وتمهيد لما بعدها

ALUSI-FULL:v4p207#2/r8.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v4p207#2/r8.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v4p207#2/r8.claim: A wealthy guardian or trustee must refrain from using the orphan’s property and live on the wealth God gave him.
ALUSI-FULL:v4p207#2/r8.anchor: ومن كان من الأولياء والأوصياء ذا مال فليكف نفسه عن أكل مال اليتيم

ALUSI-FULL:v4p207#2/r9.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v4p207#2/r9.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v4p207#2/r9.claim: Istiafaf means to restrain oneself and is stronger than afaf; taking it as dignified avoidance explains the practical sense.
ALUSI-FULL:v4p207#2/r9.anchor: فالإستعفاف الكف وهو أبلغ من العف

ALUSI-FULL:v4p207#2/r10.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v4p207#2/r10.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v4p207#2/r10.claim: The poor guardian may eat from the property only according to recognized custom and to the necessary amount for food and clothing, as ʿAtaʾ and Qatada say.
ALUSI-FULL:v4p207#2/r10.anchor: بقدر حاجته الضرورية من سد الجوعة وستر العورة قاله عطاء وقتادة

ALUSI-FULL:v4p208/r1.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v4p208/r1.speaker: ابن عباس
ALUSI-FULL:v4p208/r1.claim: A poor guardian may take from an orphan's assets in proportion to the work and benefit he provides, without extravagance or waste.
ALUSI-FULL:v4p208/r1.anchor: يأكل الفقير إذا ولى مال اليتيم بقدر قيامه على ماله ومنفعته له مالم يسرف أو يبذر

ALUSI-FULL:v4p208/r2.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v4p208/r2.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
ALUSI-FULL:v4p208/r2.claim: In answer to Ibn Umar, the Prophet permitted eating from an orphan's wealth without extravagance, accumulating wealth, or using it to shield one's own assets.
ALUSI-FULL:v4p208/r2.anchor: سأل النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم فقال : ليس لي مال وإني ولي يتيم فقال : كل من مال يتيمك غير مسرف

ALUSI-FULL:v4p208/r3.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v4p208/r3.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v4p208/r3.claim: Whether the guardian's permitted consumption counts as wages has two opinions; the author's school takes the second, as al-Jassas states in al-Ahkam.
ALUSI-FULL:v4p208/r3.anchor: وهل يعد ذلك أجرة أم لا قولان ومذهبنا الثاني كما صرح به الجصاص في الأحكام

ALUSI-FULL:v4p208/r4.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v4p208/r4.speaker: سعيد بن جبير ومجاهد وأبي العالية والزهري وعبيدة السلماني والباقر
ALUSI-FULL:v4p208/r4.claim: A poor guardian may borrow enough from the orphan's property for his needs and repay it once able; this is the recognized manner of eating.
ALUSI-FULL:v4p208/r4.anchor: أن للولي الفقير أن يأكل من مال اليتيم بقدر الكفاية على جهة القرض فإذا وجد ميسرة أعطى ما أستقرض

ALUSI-FULL:v4p208/r5.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v4p208/r5.speaker: عمر بن الخطاب
ALUSI-FULL:v4p208/r5.claim: Umar treated the public treasury like an orphan's property: he abstained when wealthy, took a reasonable amount when needy, and repaid it when able.
ALUSI-FULL:v4p208/r5.anchor: إن أستغنيت أستعففت وإن أحتجت أخذت منه بالمعروف فإذا أيسرت قضيت

ALUSI-FULL:v4p208/r6.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v4p208/r6.speaker: ابن عباس
ALUSI-FULL:v4p208/r6.claim: Ibn Abbas, on the authority of Ata, says the permission was abrogated by the warning against consuming orphan property wrongfully.
ALUSI-FULL:v4p208/r6.anchor: عن ابن عباس رضي الله تعالى عنهما أنه قال : ( ومن كان فقيرا ) الآية نسختها ( إن الذين يأكلون أموال اليتامى ظلما )

ALUSI-FULL:v4p208/r7.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v4p208/r7.speaker: عكرمة عن ابن عباس
ALUSI-FULL:v4p208/r7.claim: One reported view permits a poor guardian to take food from the orphan's wealth but not clothing.
ALUSI-FULL:v4p208/r7.anchor: ذهب قوم إلى إباحة الأكل دون الكسوة ورواه عكرمة عنإبن عباس

ALUSI-FULL:v4p208/r8.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v4p208/r8.speaker: يحيى بن سعيد
ALUSI-FULL:v4p208/r8.claim: The view that the verse authorizes spending the orphan's own wealth on the orphan according to his circumstances is rejected: it does not explain the command to abstain, and disrupts the syntax.
ALUSI-FULL:v4p208/r8.anchor: وحكى ذلك عن يحيى بن سعيد وهو مردودلأن قوله سبحانه : ( فليستعفف ) لا يعطي معنى ذلك

ALUSI-FULL:v4p208/r9.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v4p208/r9.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v4p208/r9.claim: The handover clause addresses guardians and trustees: after observing the preceding requirements, they deliver the assets under their care to the orphans; fronting the recipient emphasizes them.
ALUSI-FULL:v4p208/r9.anchor: أيها الأولياء والأوصياء إليهم أي اليتامى بع رعاية ماذكر لكم أموالهم

ALUSI-FULL:v4p208/r10.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v4p208/r10.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v4p208/r10.claim: Witnessing the handover establishes receipt and discharges the guardian, reducing suspicion and disputes and better preserving trust; the author's school treats it as recommended.
ALUSI-FULL:v4p208/r10.anchor: بأن قبضوها وبرئت عنها ذممكم لما أن ذلك أبعد عن التهمة وأنفى للخصومة وأدخل في الأمانة وهو أمر ندب عندنا

ALUSI-FULL:v4p208/r11.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v4p208/r11.speaker: الشافعية والمالكية
ALUSI-FULL:v4p208/r11.claim: The Shafi'i and Maliki schools regard witnessing the transfer as obligatory and infer that a guardian cannot prove delivery merely by his assertion.
ALUSI-FULL:v4p208/r11.anchor: وذهب الشافعية والمالكية إلى أنه أمر وجوب وأستدلوا بذلك على أن القيم لا يصدق بقوله في الدفع بدون بينة

ALUSI-FULL:v4p208/r12.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v4p208/r12.speaker: السدي
ALUSI-FULL:v4p208/r12.claim: Al-Suddi interprets God's sufficiency as witness for the parties.
ALUSI-FULL:v4p208/r12.anchor: وكفى بالله حسيبا 6 ( أي شهيدا قاله السدي

ALUSI-FULL:v4p208/r13.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v4p208/r13.speaker: سعيد بن جبير
ALUSI-FULL:v4p208/r13.claim: Sa'id ibn Jubayr says that no witness is better than God between guardians and orphans, matching the author's view that formal proof is not required.
ALUSI-FULL:v4p208/r13.anchor: عن سعيد بن جبير أن معنى ( وكفى بالله حسيبا ) أنه لا شاهد أفضل من الله تعالى فيما بينكم وبينهم

ALUSI-FULL:v4p208/r14.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v4p208/r14.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v4p208/r14.claim: Alternatively, God suffices as your reckoner, so do not disobey the command or exceed its limits; this is apt because trustees are accountable for what they hold.
ALUSI-FULL:v4p208/r14.anchor: فلا تخالفوا ما أمرتم به ولا تجاوزوا ما حد لكم ولا يخفى موقع المحاسب هنا لأن الوصي يحاسب على ما في يده

ALUSI-FULL:v4p208/r15.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v4p208/r15.speaker: أبو البقاء
ALUSI-FULL:v4p208/r15.claim: Abu al-Baqa analyzes 'God suffices' either with God as subject and an extra ba conveying command, or with an implicit subject and God as object; hasiban is circumstantial or specification.
ALUSI-FULL:v4p208/r15.anchor: وفي فاعل ( كفى ) كما قال أبو البقاء : وجهان أحدهما أنه الاسم الجليل والباء زائدة

ALUSI-FULL:v4p208/r16.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v4p208/r16.speaker: السمين
ALUSI-FULL:v4p208/r16.claim: Al-Samin treats kafa as taking one object, while Abu al-Baqa allows two, with the implied sense of God sparing you harm or the like.
ALUSI-FULL:v4p208/r16.anchor: وكفى ) متعدية إلى مفعول واحد عند السمين والتقدير وكفاكم الله حسيبا وإلى مفعولين عند أبي البقاء

ALUSI-FULL:v4p209/r15.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v4p209/r15.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v4p209/r15.claim: Testing the orphans signifies testing deficient wayfarers; reaching marriage means becoming ready for guidance, and sound judgment means steadiness on the path without fickleness.
ALUSI-FULL:v4p209/r15.anchor: ولعله إشارة إلى إختبار الناقصين من السائرين ( حتى إذا بلغوا النكاح ) وصلحوا للأرشاد والتربية

ALUSI-FULL:v4p209/r16.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v4p209/r16.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v4p209/r16.claim: Handing over the wealth means entrusting spiritual secrets only to free and worthy people.
ALUSI-FULL:v4p209/r16.anchor: فأدفعوا إليهم أموالهم ) التي يستحقونها من الأسرار التي لا تودع إلا عند الأحرار

ALUSI-FULL:v4p209#2/r1.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v4p209#2/r1.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v4p209#2/r1.claim: Perfect shaykhs are charged to appoint successors and authorize disciples who are fit to guide others.
ALUSI-FULL:v4p209#2/r1.anchor: والمراد إيصاء الكمل من الشيوخ أن يخلفوا ويأذنوا بالإرشاد من يصلح لذلك من المريدين السالكين

ALUSI-FULL:v4p209#2/r2.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v4p209#2/r2.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v4p209#2/r2.claim: Not consuming the disciples' wealth means not benefiting from their spiritual gifts to their exclusion or rushing before they mature into guidance; this is a grave disease of the ego.
ALUSI-FULL:v4p209#2/r2.anchor: أي تنتفعوا بتلك الأموال دونهم ( إسرافا وبدارا أن يكبروا ) بالتصدي للأرشاد فإن ذلك من أعظم أدواء النفس

ALUSI-FULL:v4p209#2/r3.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v4p209#2/r3.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v4p209#2/r3.claim: A spiritually rich guardian should abstain from a disciple's resources; one unable to bear need may benefit only to necessity's measure.
ALUSI-FULL:v4p209#2/r3.anchor: ومن كان منكم غنيا ) بالله لا يلتفت إلى ضرورات الحياة أصلا ( فليستعفف ) عما للمريد ( ومن كان فقيرا ) لا يتحمل الضرورة

ALUSI-FULL:v4p209#2/r4.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v4p209#2/r4.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v4p209#2/r4.claim: A spiritual handover calls for witnessing God and the spirits of the divine presence and taking a covenant that the disciple honor rights owed to God and creation.
ALUSI-FULL:v4p209#2/r4.anchor: فإذا دفعتم إليهم أموالهم فأشهدوا عليهم ) الله تعالى وأرواح أهل الحضرة وخذوا العهد عليهم برعاية الحقوق

ALUSI-FULL:v4p209#2/r5.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v4p209#2/r5.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v4p209#2/r5.claim: God is true existence and sees hidden betrayals and inward secrets; He is the sufficient protector.
ALUSI-FULL:v4p209#2/r5.anchor: لأنه الموجود الحقيقي والمطلع الذي يعلم خائنة الأعين وما تخفي الصدور وهو حسبنا ونعم الوكيل

BAGHAWI-FULL:v2p165/r1.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v2p165/r1.speaker: author
BAGHAWI-FULL:v2p165/r1.claim: The verse was revealed about Thabit b. Rifaʿa, whose father died while he was young; his uncle asked the Prophet what he could use of the boy's wealth and when to return it.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v2p165/r1.anchor: قوله تعالى: {وابتلوا اليتامى} الآية نزلت في ثابت بن رفاعة وفي عمه، وذلك أن رفاعة توفي

BAGHAWI-FULL:v2p165/r2.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v2p165/r2.speaker: author
BAGHAWI-FULL:v2p165/r2.claim: Testing orphans means examining their reason, religion, and ability to preserve their property; reaching marriage means attaining adulthood.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v2p165/r2.anchor: {وابتلوا اليتامى} اختبروهم في عقولهم وأديانهم وحفظهم أموالهم، {حتى إذا بلغوا النكاح} أي: مبلغ الرجال والنساء،

BAGHAWI-FULL:v2p165/r3.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v2p165/r3.speaker: author
BAGHAWI-FULL:v2p165/r3.claim: Ānastum means you perceive; sound judgment includes reason, religious integrity, protecting wealth, and knowing what will improve it.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v2p165/r3.anchor: {فإن آنستم} أبصرتم، {منهم رشدا} فقال المفسرون يعني: عقلا وصلاحا في الدين وحفظا للمال

BAGHAWI-FULL:v2p165/r4.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v2p165/r4.speaker: سعيد بن جبير ومجاهد والشعبي
BAGHAWI-FULL:v2p165/r4.claim: They say wealth must not be given to a ward, even an elderly one, until sound judgment is evident.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v2p165/r4.anchor: وقال سعيد بن جبير ومجاهد والشعبي: لا يدفع إليه ماله وإن كان شيخا حتى يؤنس منه رشده.

BAGHAWI-FULL:v2p165/r5.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v2p165/r5.speaker: author
BAGHAWI-FULL:v2p165/r5.claim: Test according to the ward's circumstances: give a market-going child a little to manage; test others through household spending, servants, employees, or a woman's management and preservation of her home and belongings. Repeated good conduct establishes sound judgment.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v2p165/r5.anchor: فإن كان ممن يتصرف في السوق فيدفع الولي إليه شيئا يسيرا من المال وينظر في تصرفه

BAGHAWI-FULL:v2p165/r6.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v2p165/r6.speaker: author
BAGHAWI-FULL:v2p165/r6.claim: Removing guardianship and delivering property requires both puberty and sound judgment; puberty has four indicators, two shared by men and women: age and wet dream.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v2p165/r6.anchor: واعلم أن الله تعالى علق زوال الحجر عن الصغير وجواز دفع المال إليه بشيئين: بالبلوغ والرشد

BAGHAWI-FULL:v2p165/r7.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v2p165/r7.speaker: عبد الله بن عمر
BAGHAWI-FULL:v2p165/r7.claim: Ibn ʿUmar reports that the Prophet declined him at age fourteen at Uhud but accepted him at age fifteen at the Trench, supporting fifteen as the age of majority.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v2p165/r7.anchor: عن ابن عمر رضي الله عنهما قال: عرضت على رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم عام أحد وأنا ابن أربع عشرة سنة، فردني

BAGHAWI-FULL:v2p166#2/r1.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v2p166#2/r1.speaker: أبو حنيفة
BAGHAWI-FULL:v2p166#2/r1.claim: Abu Hanifa removes guardianship from one who manages property well even if religiously corrupt; if financially wasteful he withholds property until age twenty-five, though transactions before then are effective.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v2p166#2/r1.anchor: وعند أبي حنيفة رضي الله عنه إذا كان مصلحا لماله زال الحجر عنه وإن كان مفسدا في دنيه،

BAGHAWI-FULL:v2p166#2/r2.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v2p166#2/r2.speaker: author
BAGHAWI-FULL:v2p166#2/r2.claim: The author argues that scripture requires both puberty and sound judgment; a sinner is not sound in judgment, and one still wasting wealth at twenty-five is not sound by agreement, so property should remain withheld.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v2p166#2/r2.anchor: والقرآن حجة لمن استدام الحجر عليه، لأن الله تعالى قال: {حتى إذا بلغوا النكاح فإن آنستم منهم رشدا فادفعوا إليهم أموالهم}

BAGHAWI-FULL:v2p166#2/r3.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v2p166#2/r3.speaker: author
BAGHAWI-FULL:v2p166#2/r3.claim: Once a person reaches adulthood and is sound in judgment, guardianship ends and property is delivered, whether male or female and whether married or not.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v2p166#2/r3.anchor: وإذا بلغ وأونس منه الرشد، زال الحجر عنه، ودفع إليه المال رجلا كان أو امرأة تزوج أو لم يتزوج.

BAGHAWI-FULL:v2p166#2/r4.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v2p166#2/r4.speaker: مالك
BAGHAWI-FULL:v2p166#2/r4.claim: Malik says a woman receives her property only after marriage, and her spending still requires her husband's permission until she matures through experience.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v2p166#2/r4.anchor: وعند مالك رحمه الله تعالى: إن كانت امرأة لا يدفع المال إليها ما لم تتزوج

BAGHAWI-FULL:v2p166#2/r5.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v2p166#2/r5.speaker: author
BAGHAWI-FULL:v2p166#2/r5.claim: If someone later becomes spendthrift, guardianship returns; if only religiously corrupt, one view restores it as in a person who first reached adulthood in that state, while another says an established ruling is stronger than a new one.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v2p166#2/r5.anchor: فإذا بلغ الصبي رشيدا وزال الحجر عنه ثم عاد سفيها، نظر: فإن عاد مبذرا لماله حجر عليه، وإن عاد مفسدا في دينه فعلى وجهين: أحدهما: يعاد الحجر عليه

BAGHAWI-FULL:v2p166#2/r6.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v2p166#2/r6.speaker: أبو حنيفة
