BAGHAWI-FULL:v2p166#2/r6.claim: Abu Hanifa holds that no free, sane adult can be legally interdicted; the author cites the Companions' agreement allowing interdiction, based on Ali seeking Uthman's order against ʿAbd Allah b. Jaʿfar's extravagant land purchase, which Zubayr joined as partner.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v2p166#2/r6.anchor: وعند أبي حنيفة رحمه الله تعالى: لا حجر على الحر العاقل البالغ بحال، والدليل على إثبات الحجر

BAGHAWI-FULL:v2p167/r1.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v2p167/r1.speaker: author
BAGHAWI-FULL:v2p167/r1.claim: Guardians must not consume an orphan's property wrongfully or hastily, racing the ward's maturity to avoid having to hand it over; an is accusative in this construction.

BAGHAWI-FULL:v2p167/r2.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v2p167/r2.speaker: author
BAGHAWI-FULL:v2p167/r2.claim: A wealthy guardian must abstain entirely; a poor guardian who maintains the property may take a reasonable amount.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v2p167/r2.anchor: {ومن كان غنيا فليستعفف} أي ليمتنع من مال اليتيم فلا يرزأه قليلا ولا كثيرا

BAGHAWI-FULL:v2p167/r3.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v2p167/r3.speaker: عمرو بن شعيب
BAGHAWI-FULL:v2p167/r3.claim: A poor man with an orphan asks about using the orphan's wealth; the Prophet permits eating without excess, haste, or hoarding.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v2p167/r3.anchor: عن عمرو بن شعيب عن أبيه عن جده رضي الله عنه أن رجلا أتى رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم فقال: إني فقير وليس لي شيء ولي يتيم؟

BAGHAWI-FULL:v2p167/r4.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v2p167/r4.speaker: مجاهد وسعيد بن جبير
BAGHAWI-FULL:v2p167/r4.claim: They say reasonable consumption is a loan that the guardian must repay when financially able; ʿUmar says he would similarly eat from the public treasury only if needy and repay when solvent.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v2p167/r4.anchor: وهو قول مجاهد وسعيد بن جبير، قال عمر بن الخطاب رضي الله عنه: إني أنزلت نفسي

BAGHAWI-FULL:v2p167/r5.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v2p167/r5.speaker: الشعبي
BAGHAWI-FULL:v2p167/r5.claim: Al-Shaʿbi permits eating only under dire necessity, as with carrion.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v2p167/r5.anchor: وقال الشعبي: لا يأكله إلا أن يضطر إليه كما يضطر إلى الميتة.

BAGHAWI-FULL:v2p167/r6.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v2p167/r6.speaker: author
BAGHAWI-FULL:v2p167/r6.claim: Some say no repayment is due.

BAGHAWI-FULL:v2p167/r7.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v2p167/r7.speaker: عطاء وعكرمة
BAGHAWI-FULL:v2p167/r7.claim: They limit customary consumption to food enough to end hunger and clothing to cover the body, forbidding excess or clothing bought from the orphan's property.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v2p167/r7.anchor: فقال عطاء وعكرمة: يأكل بأطراف أصابعه

BAGHAWI-FULL:v2p167/r8.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v2p167/r8.speaker: الحسن وجماعة
BAGHAWI-FULL:v2p167/r8.claim: They permit a guardian to consume orchard fruit and livestock milk in moderation without repayment, but require returning any gold or silver taken.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v2p167/r8.anchor: وقال الحسن وجماعة: يأكل من ثمر نخيله ولبن مواشيه بالمعروف ولا قضاء عليه،

BAGHAWI-FULL:v2p168/r1.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v2p168/r1.speaker: الكلبي
BAGHAWI-FULL:v2p168/r1.claim: Al-Kalbi says customary compensation is use of the animal for riding or a servant's labor; the guardian may not eat any of the orphan's wealth.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v2p168/r1.anchor: وقال الكلبي: المعروف ركوب الدابة وخدمة الخادم، وليس له أن يأكل من ماله شيئا.

BAGHAWI-FULL:v2p168/r2.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v2p168/r2.speaker: ابن عباس
BAGHAWI-FULL:v2p168/r2.claim: Ibn ʿAbbas tells a camel caretaker he may drink milk only if he searches for strays, treats mange, repairs the water trough, waters the herd, and does not harm offspring or overmilk.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v2p168/r2.anchor: سمعت القاسم بن محمد يقول: جاء رجل إلى ابن عباس رضي الله عنهما قال: إن لي يتيما وإن له إبلا أفأشرب من لبن إبله؟

BAGHAWI-FULL:v2p168/r3.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v2p168/r3.speaker: عائشة
BAGHAWI-FULL:v2p168/r3.claim: Aisha and other scholars say a guardian may take from all the ward's property in proportion to living costs and labor, without repayment.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v2p168/r3.anchor: وقال بعضهم: والمعروف أن يأخذ من جميع ماله بقدر قيامه وأجرة عمله، ولا قضاء عليه، وهو قول عائشة

BAGHAWI-FULL:v2p168/r4.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v2p168/r4.speaker: author
BAGHAWI-FULL:v2p168/r4.claim: Witnessing the handover of the ward's property is guidance, not an obligation; it protects the guardian from suspicion and future dispute. God is an accountant, requiter, and witness.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v2p168/r4.anchor: قوله تعالى: {فإذا دفعتم إليهم أموالهم فأشهدوا عليهم} هذا أمر إرشاد، ليس بواجب

BAYDAWI-FULL:4:6/r1.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:4:6/r1.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:4:6/r1.claim: Test orphans before puberty by observing religious soundness and money management, letting them handle preliminary contract steps; Abu Hanifa instead tests by giving them something to manage.
BAYDAWI-FULL:4:6/r1.anchor: اختبروهم قبل البلوغ بتتبع أحوالهم في صلاح الدين، والتهدي إلى ضبط المال وحسن التصرف

BAYDAWI-FULL:4:6/r2.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:4:6/r2.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:4:6/r2.claim: Puberty occurs by wet dream or at fifteen years according to this school, supported by a prophetic report on recording liability and applying penalties; Abu Hanifa sets eighteen.
BAYDAWI-FULL:4:6/r2.anchor: بأن يحتلم، أو يستكمل خمس عشرة سنة عندنا لقوله عليه الصلاة والسلام:

BAYDAWI-FULL:4:6/r3.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:4:6/r3.speaker: أبو حنيفة
BAYDAWI-FULL:4:6/r3.claim: Abu Hanifa sets puberty at eighteen; bulūgh al-nikāḥ euphemistically means maturity and suitability for marriage in his view.
BAYDAWI-FULL:4:6/r3.anchor: وثماني عشرة عند أبي حنيفة رحمه الله تعالى. وبلوغ النكاح كناية عن البلوغ

BAYDAWI-FULL:4:6/r4.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:4:6/r4.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:4:6/r4.claim: Ānastum means perceiving maturity; a reading aḥsastum has the sense of perceiving.
BAYDAWI-FULL:4:6/r4.anchor: فإن أبصرتم منهم رشدا. وقرىء أحستم بمعنى أحسستم.

BAYDAWI-FULL:4:6/r5.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:4:6/r5.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:4:6/r5.claim: Deliver property promptly at puberty only if maturity is observed; the conditional grammar makes maturity a prerequisite.
BAYDAWI-FULL:4:6/r5.anchor: من غير تأخير عن حد البلوغ، ونظم الآية أن إن الشرطية جواب إذا المتضمنة معنى الشرط

BAYDAWI-FULL:4:6/r6.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:4:6/r6.speaker: أبو حنيفة
BAYDAWI-FULL:4:6/r6.claim: Abu Hanifa gives property after seven years beyond puberty even without observed maturity, since it is a period of change when a child begins to discern and is ordered to worship.
BAYDAWI-FULL:4:6/r6.anchor: وقال أبو حنيفة رحمه الله تعالى: إذا زادت على سن البلوغ سبع سنين وهي مدة معتبرة في تغير الأحوال

BAYDAWI-FULL:4:6/r7.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:4:6/r7.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:4:6/r7.claim: Guardians must not consume orphan wealth wastefully or hastily before the children grow; this may describe the guardian's own extravagance and haste.
BAYDAWI-FULL:4:6/r7.anchor: مسرفين ومبادرين كبرهم، أو لإسرافكم ومبادرتكم كبرهم.

BAYDAWI-FULL:4:6/r8.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:4:6/r8.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:4:6/r8.claim: A wealthy guardian abstains; a poor guardian may take a customary amount proportionate to need and work, since the language implies a limited right in the child's property.
BAYDAWI-FULL:4:6/r8.anchor: من أكلها. { ومن كان فقيرا فليأكل بالمعروف } بقدر حاجته وأجرة سعيه

BAYDAWI-FULL:4:6/r9.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:4:6/r9.speaker: النبي
BAYDAWI-FULL:4:6/r9.claim: The Prophet told an orphan's guardian to take fairly without accumulating wealth or shielding his own property with the orphan's.
BAYDAWI-FULL:4:6/r9.anchor: أن رجلا قال له إن في حجري يتيما أفآكل من ماله؟ قال: كل بالمعروف غير متأثل مالا

BAYDAWI-FULL:4:6/r10.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:4:6/r10.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:4:6/r10.claim: Witness the transfer to prove receipt and prevent suspicion, dispute, and liability; the chosen position and Malik require proof from the guardian, unlike Abu Hanifa.
BAYDAWI-FULL:4:6/r10.anchor: وهو المختار عندنا وهو مذهب مالك خلافا لأبي حنيفة.

BAYDAWI-FULL:4:6/r11.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:4:6/r11.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:4:6/r11.claim: God suffices as accountant; guardians must not violate the command or exceed its limits.
BAYDAWI-FULL:4:6/r11.anchor: محاسبا فلا تخالفوا ما أمرتم به ولا تتجاوزوا ما حد لكم.

BIQAI-FULL:v2p215/r8.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v2p215/r8.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v2p215/r8.claim: Guardians should regularly test orphans' religious and financial judgment during adolescence until they reach marriageable age, by puberty or age.
BIQAI-FULL:v2p215/r8.anchor: أي اختبروهم في أمر الرشد في الدين والمال في مدة مراهقتهم

BIQAI-FULL:v2p215/r9.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v2p215/r9.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v2p215/r9.claim: If they show sound financial judgment upon maturity, their assets must be handed over; the indefinite wording reflects how rare complete maturity is.
BIQAI-FULL:v2p215/r9.anchor: ونكره لأن وجود كمال الرشد في أحد يعز وقوعه

BIQAI-FULL:v2p215/r10.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v2p215/r10.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v2p215/r10.claim: The pronoun shift from guardians' assets to the orphans' assets signals that property belongs to those who can manage it responsibly, ending the need for protective restriction.
BIQAI-FULL:v2p215/r10.anchor: وأضافها إليهم بعد إضافتها أولا إلى المعطين إشارة إلى أنه لا يستحقها إلا من يحسن التصرف فيها

BIQAI-FULL:v2p215/r11.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v2p215/r11.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v2p215/r11.claim: Guardians must not consume orphans' wealth wastefully or hastily before they grow up, fearing they will lose access; extravagance means spending beyond due moderation.
BIQAI-FULL:v2p215/r11.anchor: أي مسرفين بالخروج عن القصد في التصرف

BIQAI-FULL:v2p216/r1.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v2p216/r1.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v2p216/r1.claim: A wealthy guardian should abstain entirely from the orphan’s property; a poor guardian who manages it may take only customary compensation for his work.
BIQAI-FULL:v2p216/r1.anchor: أي يطلب العفة ويوجدها ويظهرها عن الأكل منها جملة

BIQAI-FULL:v2p216/r2.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v2p216/r2.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v2p216/r2.claim: The poor guardian’s customary allowance is proportionate to the wage earned through his effort.
BIQAI-FULL:v2p216/r2.anchor: فقال معبرا بالأكل لأنه معظم المقصود : { فليأكل بالمعروف } أي بقدر أجرة سعيه

BIQAI-FULL:v2p216/r3.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v2p216/r3.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v2p216/r3.claim: Guardians must document the return of an orphan’s property because maturity and sound judgment vary, and witnesses prevent disputes and protect both sides.
BIQAI-FULL:v2p216/r3.anchor: لأن الأحوال تتبدل , والرشد يتفاوت , فالإشهاد أقطع للشر

BIQAI-FULL:v2p216/r4.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v2p216/r4.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v2p216/r4.claim: Requiring witnesses deters a guardian from betrayal, since he knows a later claim will require evidence.
BIQAI-FULL:v2p216/r4.anchor: والأمر بالإشهاد أزجر للولي عن الخيانة , لأن من عرف أنه لا يقبل عند الخصام إلا ببينة

BIQAI-FULL:v2p216/r5.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v2p216/r5.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v2p216/r5.claim: God is a meticulous accountant; the closing warning cautions guardians and orphans against betrayal, transgression, and coveting another’s rights.
BIQAI-FULL:v2p216/r5.anchor: أي محاسبا بليغا في الحساب , فهو أبلغ تحذيرا لهم وللأيتام من الخيانة والتعدي

DURR-FULL:v2p433/r13.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v2p433/r13.speaker: ابن عباس
DURR-FULL:v2p433/r13.claim: Test orphans when they reach puberty; if their judgment and handling of property are sound, hand over their wealth, and do not consume it wastefully or hastily before they mature.
DURR-FULL:v2p433/r13.anchor: عن ابن عباس {وابتلوا اليتامى} يعني اختبروا اليتامى عند الحلم {فإن آنستم} عرفتم {منهم رشدا

DURR-FULL:v2p435/r1.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v2p435/r1.speaker: مجاهد
DURR-FULL:v2p435/r1.claim: Test the orphans' minds; reaching marriage means puberty, discernment means perceiving, and sound judgment means intellect.
DURR-FULL:v2p435/r1.anchor: عن مجاهد {وابتلوا اليتامى} قال: عقولهم {حتى إذا بلغوا النكاح} يقول: الحلم {فإن آنستم} قال: أحسستم {منهم رشدا

DURR-FULL:v2p435/r2.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v2p435/r2.speaker: السدي
DURR-FULL:v2p435/r2.claim: Al-Suddi says to test their minds and discern both intelligence and soundness.
DURR-FULL:v2p435/r2.anchor: عن السدي {وابتلوا اليتامى} قال: جربوا عقولهم {فإن آنستم منهم رشدا} قال: عقولا وصلاحا

DURR-FULL:v2p435/r3.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v2p435/r3.speaker: مقاتل
DURR-FULL:v2p435/r3.claim: The people addressed to test the orphans are their guardians and trustees.
DURR-FULL:v2p435/r3.anchor: عن مقاتل {وابتلوا اليتامى} يعني الأولياء والأوصياء

DURR-FULL:v2p435/r4.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v2p435/r4.speaker: محمد بن قيس
DURR-FULL:v2p435/r4.claim: Muhammad ibn Qays says puberty is at fifteen years.
DURR-FULL:v2p435/r4.anchor: عن محمد بن قيس {حتى إذا بلغوا النكاح} قال: خمس عشرة

DURR-FULL:v2p435/r5.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v2p435/r5.speaker: الحسن
DURR-FULL:v2p435/r5.claim: Sound judgment means religious integrity and safeguarding property.
DURR-FULL:v2p435/r5.anchor: عن الحسن {فإن آنستم منهم رشدا} قال: صلاحا في دينه وحفظا لماله

DURR-FULL:v2p435/r6.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v2p435/r6.speaker: سعيد بن جبير
DURR-FULL:v2p435/r6.claim: Sound judgment means religious integrity and protecting one's wealth.
DURR-FULL:v2p435/r6.anchor: عن سعيد بن جبير {فإن آنستم منهم رشدا} قال: صلاحا في دينهم وحفظا لأموالهم

DURR-FULL:v2p435/r7.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v2p435/r7.speaker: ابن عباس
DURR-FULL:v2p435/r7.claim: When an orphan reaches puberty with intelligence and dignity, his property is handed to him.
DURR-FULL:v2p435/r7.anchor: عن ابن عباس قال: إذا أدرك اليتيم بحلم وعقل ووقار دفع إليه ماله

DURR-FULL:v2p435/r8.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v2p435/r8.speaker: مجاهد
DURR-FULL:v2p435/r8.claim: Do not hand an orphan his property, even if his hair has turned gray, until sound judgment is evident.
DURR-FULL:v2p435/r8.anchor: عن مجاهد قال: لا تدفع إلى اليتيم ماله وإن شمط ما لم يؤنس منه رشد

DURR-FULL:v2p435/r9.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v2p435/r9.speaker: الحسن
DURR-FULL:v2p435/r9.claim: Do not consume the orphan's property extravagantly or in haste.
DURR-FULL:v2p435/r9.anchor: عن الحسن {ولا تأكلوها إسرافا وبدارا} ويقول: لا تسرف فيها ولا تبادر

DURR-FULL:v2p435/r10.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v2p435/r10.speaker: سعيد بن جبير
DURR-FULL:v2p435/r10.claim: Do not consume the property without right or hastily before the orphan reaches puberty, fearing he will reclaim it.
DURR-FULL:v2p435/r10.anchor: عن سعيد بن جبير {ولا تأكلوها إسرافا} يعني في غير حق {وبدارا أن يكبروا} قال: خشية أن يبلغ الحلم

DURR-FULL:v2p435/r11.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v2p435/r11.speaker: عائشة
DURR-FULL:v2p435/r11.claim: The verse concerns an orphan's guardian: a wealthy guardian abstains, while a poor guardian may take a customary amount proportionate to his care.
DURR-FULL:v2p435/r11.anchor: عن عائشة قالت: أنزلت هذه الآية في ولي اليتيم {ومن كان غنيا فليستعفف ومن كان فقيرا فليأكل بالمعروف

DURR-FULL:v2p435/r12.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v2p435/r12.speaker: ابن عباس
DURR-FULL:v2p435/r12.claim: A wealthy guardian should rely on his own means and take nothing; a poor guardian may take subsistence from the orphan's property to meet his needs.
DURR-FULL:v2p435/r12.anchor: عن ابن عباس {ومن كان غنيا فليستعفف} قال: بغناه من ماله حتى يستغني عن مال اليتيم

DURR-FULL:v2p436/r1.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v2p436/r1.speaker: ابن عباس
DURR-FULL:v2p436/r1.claim: A wealthy guardian should support himself from his own property and avoid the orphan's assets.
DURR-FULL:v2p436/r1.anchor: عن ابن عباس {ومن كان غنيا فليستعفف} قال: يستعف بماله حتى لا يفضي إلى مال اليتيم

DURR-FULL:v2p436/r2.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v2p436/r2.speaker: ابن عباس
DURR-FULL:v2p436/r2.claim: A poor guardian may borrow from the orphan's property.
DURR-FULL:v2p436/r2.anchor: عن ابن عباس {ومن كان فقيرا فليأكل بالمعروف} قال: هو القرض

DURR-FULL:v2p436/r3.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v2p436/r3.speaker: ابن عباس
DURR-FULL:v2p436/r3.claim: A poor guardian may borrow from the orphan's property.
DURR-FULL:v2p436/r3.anchor: عن ابن عباس {ومن كان فقيرا فليأكل بالمعروف} يعني القرض

DURR-FULL:v2p436/r4.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v2p436/r4.speaker: ابن عباس
DURR-FULL:v2p436/r4.claim: A poor guardian may take surplus milk, basic food, and clothing that covers him, but should not exceed need; he repays if able and is excused if unable.
DURR-FULL:v2p436/r4.anchor: عن ابن عباس في الآية قال: ولي اليتيم إن كان غنيا فليستعفف وإن كان فقيرا أخذ من فضل اللبن وأخذ بالقوت

DURR-FULL:v2p436/r5.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v2p436/r5.speaker: ابن عباس
DURR-FULL:v2p436/r5.claim: A wealthy guardian may take nothing; a poor one may borrow from the orphan and repay when able.
DURR-FULL:v2p436/r5.anchor: عن ابن عباس في الآية يقول: إن كان غنيا فلا يحل له أن يأكل من مال اليتيم شيئا وإن كان فقيرا فليستقرض

DURR-FULL:v2p436/r6.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v2p436/r6.speaker: عمر بن الخطاب
DURR-FULL:v2p436/r6.claim: Umar treated himself as a guardian over public funds: when self-sufficient he abstained, and when needy he took a customary amount and repaid when able.
DURR-FULL:v2p436/r6.anchor: عن عمر بن الخطاب قال: إني أنزلت نفسي من مال الله بمنزلة ولي اليتيم إن استغنيت استعففت

DURR-FULL:v2p436/r7.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v2p436/r7.speaker: ابن عباس
DURR-FULL:v2p436/r7.claim: A needy guardian may eat their food but should not take clothing or a turban.
DURR-FULL:v2p436/r7.anchor: عن ابن عباس في قوله {ومن كان فقيرا فليأكل بالمعروف} قال: إذا احتاج ولي اليتيم وضع يده فأكل من طعامهم

DURR-FULL:v2p436/r8.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v2p436/r8.speaker: ابن عباس
DURR-FULL:v2p436/r8.claim: A poor guardian should eat only by using three fingertips.
DURR-FULL:v2p436/r8.anchor:
عن ابن عباس {فليأكل بالمعروف} قال:
بأطراف أصابعه الثلاث

DURR-FULL:v2p436/r9.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v2p436/r9.speaker: ابن عباس
DURR-FULL:v2p436/r9.claim: A poor guardian may take in proportion to his care and benefit to the property, without waste or extravagance.
DURR-FULL:v2p436/r9.anchor: عن ابن عباس في الآية قال: يأكل الفقير إذا ولي مال اليتيم بقدر قيامه على ماله ومنفعته له

DURR-FULL:v2p436/r10.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v2p436/r10.speaker: ابن عباس
DURR-FULL:v2p436/r10.claim: A caretaker of orphan camels may drink their milk if he searches for strays, treats mange, and maintains the water trough, provided he does not harm the herd or overmilk it.
DURR-FULL:v2p436/r10.anchor: ابن عباس فقال: إن في حجري أيتاما وإن لهم إبلا فماذا يحل لي من ألبانها

DURR-FULL:v2p437/r1.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v2p437/r1.speaker: النبي
DURR-FULL:v2p437/r1.claim: The Prophet permits a guardian with no property to consume from an orphan's assets without extravagance, waste, accumulating wealth, or shielding his own assets with theirs.
DURR-FULL:v2p437/r1.anchor: رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم فقال: ليس لي مال ولي يتيم فقال كل من مال يتيمك غير مسرف ولا مبذر

DURR-FULL:v2p437/r2.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v2p437/r2.speaker: النبي
DURR-FULL:v2p437/r2.claim: The Prophet says a guardian may discipline an orphan as he would his own child, but must not protect his own wealth with the orphan's or accumulate the orphan's property.
DURR-FULL:v2p437/r2.anchor: رسول الله مم أضرب يتيمي قال: مما كنت ضاربا منه ولدك

DURR-FULL:v2p437/r3.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v2p437/r3.speaker: النبي
DURR-FULL:v2p437/r3.claim: Another report allows disciplining an orphan as one's own child and customary consumption without accumulating property or using the orphan's wealth to protect one's own.
DURR-FULL:v2p437/r3.anchor: رسول الله مم أضرب يتيمي قال: مما كنت ضاربا منه ولدك

DURR-FULL:v2p437/r4.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v2p437/r4.speaker: قتادة
DURR-FULL:v2p437/r4.claim: The Prophet allowed Thabit ibn Wadaʿa's guardian customary benefit from an orphan's orchard produce, livestock milk, and labor, but not consumption of the principal assets.
DURR-FULL:v2p437/r4.anchor: عن قتادة في الآية قال: ذكر لنا أن عم ثابت بن وداعة - وثابت يومئذ يتيم في حجره

DURR-FULL:v2p437/r5.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v2p437/r5.speaker: عطاء
DURR-FULL:v2p437/r5.claim: ʿAtaʾ calls the poor guardian's consumption an optional Qur'anic concession rather than an obligation.
DURR-FULL:v2p437/r5.anchor: عن عطاء قال: خمس في كتاب الله رخصة وليست بعزيمة قوله {ومن كان فقيرا فليأكل بالمعروف

DURR-FULL:v2p437/r6.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v2p437/r6.speaker: ابن عباس
DURR-FULL:v2p437/r6.claim: Ibn Abbas says the permission for a poor guardian to eat is abrogated by the prohibition on consuming orphans' property unjustly.
DURR-FULL:v2p437/r6.anchor:
عن ابن
عباس {ومن كان فقيرا فليأكل بالمعروف} قال: نسختها (إن الذين يأكلون أموال اليتامى ظلما

DURR-FULL:v2p437/r7.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v2p437/r7.speaker: الضحاك
DURR-FULL:v2p437/r7.claim: Al-Dahhak likewise says the permission was abrogated by the warning against unjustly consuming orphans' property.
DURR-FULL:v2p437/r7.anchor:
في ناسخه عن الضحاك
مثله
وأخرج ابن أبي حاتم عن

DURR-FULL:v2p437/r8.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v2p437/r8.speaker: ابن أبي الزناد
DURR-FULL:v2p437/r8.claim: Abu al-Zinad says this permission applied only to Bedouins and people like them.
DURR-FULL:v2p437/r8.anchor: عن ابن أبي الزناد في الآية قال: كان أبو الزناد يقول: إنما كان ذلك في أهل البدو وأشباههم

DURR-FULL:v2p438/r1.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v2p438/r1.speaker: يحيى بن سعيد وربيعة
DURR-FULL:v2p438/r1.claim: Yahya ibn Saʿid and Rabiʿa say a poor orphan's needs should be met according to his poverty, while the guardian may take nothing for himself.
DURR-FULL:v2p438/r1.anchor: يحيى بن سعيد وربيعة عن قوله {فليأكل بالمعروف

DURR-FULL:v2p438/r2.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v2p438/r2.speaker: ابن عباس
DURR-FULL:v2p438/r2.claim: When handing an orphan his property, the guardian should transfer it in front of witnesses as God commanded.
DURR-FULL:v2p438/r2.anchor: عن ابن عباس {فإذا دفعتم إليهم أموالهم فأشهدوا عليهم} يقول: إذا دفع إلى اليتيم ماله

DURR-FULL:v2p438/r3.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v2p438/r3.speaker: سعيد بن جبير
DURR-FULL:v2p438/r3.claim: Trustees should witness the handover of property to orphans after puberty; God is the best witness over the parties.
DURR-FULL:v2p438/r3.anchor: عن سعيد بن جبير في الآية يقول للأوصياء: إذا دفعتم إلى اليتامى أموالهم إذا بلغوا الحلم فأشهدوا عليهم

DURR-FULL:v2p438/r4.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v2p438/r4.speaker: السدي
DURR-FULL:v2p438/r4.claim: God is sufficient as a witness.
DURR-FULL:v2p438/r4.anchor: عن السدي {وكفى بالله حسيبا} يقول: شهيدا

RAZI-FULL:v1p55/r1.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v1p55/r1.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v1p55/r1.claim: The ordinary analysis makes the pronoun in ربه refer to an earlier mention; Ibn Jinnī allows it to refer to ʿAdī, contrary to the majority, but Razi says the argument should be framed differently.
RAZI-FULL:v1p55/r1.anchor: أن الهاء عائدة إلى مذكور متقدم

RAZI-FULL:v1p55/r2.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v1p55/r2.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v1p55/r2.claim: A transitive act needs both an agent as influencer and an object as recipient; neither precedes the other in the act itself, so just as the agent may precede, the object may precede in wording.
RAZI-FULL:v1p55/r2.anchor: الفعل المتعدي لا يستغني عن المفعول وذلك لأن الفاعل هو المؤثر والمفعول هو القابل والفعل مفتقر إليهما

RAZI-FULL:v1p55/r3.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v1p55/r3.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v1p55/r3.claim: In ضرب غلامه زيد the object appears before the subject in wording, although it remains later in meaning.

RAZI-FULL:v1p55/r4.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v1p55/r4.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v1p55/r4.claim: In the verse about Abraham being tested by his Lord, the subject is later in wording but earlier in meaning; making that semantic order explicit would yield an antecedent before its pronoun.
RAZI-FULL:v1p55/r4.anchor: الإضمار قبل الذكر غير حاصل في الصورة لكنه حاصل في المعنى

RAZI-FULL:v1p55/r5.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v1p55/r5.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v1p55/r5.claim: A subject may be explicit, an overt attached pronoun, or an unexpressed implicit pronoun, as in ضرب زيد, ضربت, ضربنا, and زيد ضرب.
RAZI-FULL:v1p55/r5.anchor: الفاعل قد يكون مظهرا كقولك : ضرب زيد

RAZI-FULL:v1p55/r6.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v1p55/r6.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v1p55/r6.claim: The subject can be omitted in إذا كان غدا, understood as “what we are on” when tomorrow comes.
RAZI-FULL:v1p55/r6.anchor: إذا كان ما نحن عليه غدا

RAZI-FULL:v1p55/r7.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v1p55/r7.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v1p55/r7.claim: A verb may also be omitted: replying زيد to “Who did it?” means “Zayd did it”; the verse about a polytheist seeking protection is analyzed with an implied verb before أحد.

BURHAN:v2p120/r1.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v2p120/r1.speaker: author
BURHAN:v2p120/r1.claim: The people under discussion were already believers, as the occasion of revelation shows; the wording's possessive attribution treats them this way to intensify encouragement.
BURHAN:v2p120/r1.anchor: قلت كانوا مؤمنين قبله بدليل سبب نزولها وعوملوا هذه المعاملة من الإضافة مبالغة في الترغيب

BURHAN:v2p120/r3.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v2p120/r3.speaker: author
BURHAN:v2p120/r3.claim: Expressions can differ in eloquence through the force and dignity of individual meanings and through smoothness of wording.
BURHAN:v2p120/r3.anchor: أحدها المعانى الإفرادية بأن يكون بعضها أقوى دلالة وأفخم مسمى وأسلس لفظا

BURHAN:v2p120/r4.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v2p120/r4.speaker: author
BURHAN:v2p120/r4.claim: Inflection can make an expression more eloquent: wa-shtaʿala al-raʾsu shayban uses a specification construction that is stronger than shaybatan or shayba al-raʾs.
BURHAN:v2p120/r4.anchor: الثانى المعانى الإعرابية بأن يكون مسماها أبلغ معنى كالتمييز مع البدل

BURHAN:v2p120/r5.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v2p120/r5.speaker: author
BURHAN:v2p120/r5.claim: Syntactic arrangement can improve meaning: in lā tattakhidhū ilāhayni ithnayn, ithnayn is the object and ilāhayni a fronted adjective, with the broader term ithnayn emphasized.
BURHAN:v2p120/r5.anchor: الثالث مواقع التركيب كعوله تعالى ﴿ وقال الله لا تتخذوا إلهين اثنين ﴾

BURHAN:v2p120/r6.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v2p120/r6.speaker: author
BURHAN:v2p120/r6.claim: The Qurʾān's highest form of inimitability lies in a composition whose arrangement cannot be made more fitting or balanced for conveying its meaning.
BURHAN:v2p120/r6.anchor: فصل فى اشتمال القرآن على أعلى أنواع الإعجاز وهو أن يقع التركيب بحيث لا يمتنع

BURHAN:v2p120/r7.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v2p120/r7.speaker: القاضي أبو بكر ابن الطيب
BURHAN:v2p120/r7.claim: Al-Qāḍī Abū Bakr ibn al-Ṭayyib denies degrees of eloquence in the Qurʾān: every word is at the highest level, though people differ in how well they perceive it.
BURHAN:v2p120/r7.anchor: واختار القاضى أبو بكر ابن الطيب فى كتاب ( الإعجاز ) المنع وأن كل كلمة موصوفة بالذروة العليا

BURHAN:v2p120/r8.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v2p120/r8.speaker: أبو بصر بن القشيري
BURHAN:v2p120/r8.claim: Abū Baṣr ibn al-Qushayrī accepts that Qurʾānic eloquence has degrees and rebukes grammarians for weakening Hamza's genitive al-arḥām.
BURHAN:v2p120/r8.anchor: واختار أبو بصر بن القشيرى فى تفسيره التفاوت

BURHAN:v1p108/r11.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v1p108/r11.speaker: author
BURHAN:v1p108/r11.claim: Nikāḥ generally means marriage, but in this verse it denotes puberty.
BURHAN:v1p108/r11.anchor: النكاح فى القرآن التزوج إلا قوله جل ثناؤه ﴿ حتى إذا بلغوا النكاح ﴾ فإنه يعنى الحلم

ITQAN:v3p82/r2.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v3p82/r2.speaker: author
ITQAN:v3p82/r2.claim: When a qualified ruling has no other basis, it constrains an unqualified one; witness fairness is therefore required in sales and handing orphans their property as well as in divorce and wills.
ITQAN:v3p82/r2.anchor: اشتراط العدالة في الشهود على الرجعة والفرق والوصية في قوله

ITQAN:v2p307#2/r1.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v2p307#2/r1.speaker: author
ITQAN:v2p307#2/r1.claim: In the command to test the orphans, ibtalū means 'examine' or 'test.'

ITQAN:v2p307#2/r2.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v2p307#2/r2.speaker: author
ITQAN:v2p307#2/r2.claim: Ānastum means 'you have recognized' or 'found out.'

ITQAN:v2p307#2/r3.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v2p307#2/r3.speaker: author
ITQAN:v2p307#2/r3.claim: Rushdan means sound judgment or competence.

ITQAN:v2p418/r13.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v2p418/r13.speaker: ابن فارس
ITQAN:v2p418/r13.claim: Nikāḥ usually means marriage, but in 4:6 it means puberty.
ITQAN:v2p418/r13.anchor: وكل نكاح فيه تزوج إلا ﴿ حتى إذا بلغوا النكاح ﴾ فهو الحلم

DAMGHANI:v1p462/r24.author: al-Dāmghānī
DAMGHANI:v1p462/r24.speaker: author
DAMGHANI:v1p462/r24.claim: Nikāḥ can mean puberty or sexual maturity.
DAMGHANI:v1p462/r24.anchor: النكاح الحلم قوله تعالى في سورة النساء

DAMGHANI:v1p235/r5.author: al-Dāmghānī
DAMGHANI:v1p235/r5.speaker: author
DAMGHANI:v1p235/r5.claim: Isrāf can mean unlawfully taking the property of orphans.
DAMGHANI:v1p235/r5.anchor: الإسراف بمعنى الحرام قوله تعالى في سورة النساء

DAMGHANI:v1p322/r3.author: al-Dāmghānī
DAMGHANI:v1p322/r3.speaker: author
DAMGHANI:v1p322/r3.claim: Al-maʿrūf here means a loan or allowance; the same sense occurs in the passage about charitable confidential counsel.
DAMGHANI:v1p322/r3.anchor: ومن كان فقيرا فليأكل بالمعروف يعني بالقرض نظيرها فيها لا خير في كثير من نجواهم

IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p590/r1.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p590/r1.speaker: المفضل
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p590/r1.claim: Nikah originally meant sexual intercourse; the term later expanded to include the marriage contract.
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p590/r1.anchor: قال المفضل : أصل النكاح : الجماع . ثم كثر ذلك حتى قيل للعقد : النكاح

IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p590/r2.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p590/r2.speaker: أبو عمر غلام ثعلب
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p590/r2.claim: Reporting Thaʿlab from the Kufans and al-Mubarrad from the Basrans, he says the root means joining two things and can also mean intercourse without a contract.
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p590/r2.anchor: وقال أبو عمر غلام ثعلب : الذي حصلناه عن ثعلب عن الكوفيين والمبرد عن البصريين

IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p590/r3.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p590/r3.speaker: الأعشى
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p590/r3.claim: Al-Aʿsha's line uses nikah for a captive woman who had been sexually possessed without dowry or contract.
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p590/r3.anchor: قال الأعشى : - ومنكوحة غير ممهورة … وأخرى يقال له فادها

IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p590/r4.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p590/r4.speaker: القاضي أبو يعلى
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p590/r4.claim: Nikah may denote a contract in 33:49, but intercourse is literal and contract figurative because it leads to intercourse.
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p590/r4.anchor: وقال القاضي أبو يعلى : وقد يطلق اسم النكاح على العقد قال الله تعالى

IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p590/r5.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p590/r5.speaker: القاضي أبو يعلى
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p590/r5.claim: A thing can take the name of something adjacent or causally related, as with ʿaqiqa for the sacrificed animal, rawiya for a water carrier, and ghait for human waste.
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p590/r5.anchor: وإنما سمي العقد نكاحا لأنه سبب يتوصل به إلى الوطء . وقد يسمى الشيء باسم غيره

IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p590/r6.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p590/r6.speaker: بعض المفسرين
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p590/r6.claim: Nikah means the contract in 2:221, 4:3, 4:25, and 33:49.
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p590/r6.anchor: وذكر بعض ا لمفسرين أن النكاح في القرآن على خمسة أوجه : - أحدها : العقد

IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p590/r7.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p590/r7.speaker: بعض المفسرين
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p590/r7.anchor: وذكر بعض ا لمفسرين أن النكاح في القرآن على خمسة أوجه

IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p590/r8.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p590/r8.speaker: بعض المفسرين
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p590/r8.claim: Nikah denotes both contract and intercourse in 4:22.
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p590/r8.anchor: وذكر بعض ا لمفسرين أن النكاح في القرآن على خمسة أوجه

IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p590/r9.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p590/r9.speaker: بعض المفسرين
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p590/r9.claim: In this verse, nikah means puberty or reaching sexual maturity.
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p590/r9.anchor: وذكر بعض ا لمفسرين أن النكاح في القرآن على خمسة أوجه

IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p590/r10.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p590/r10.speaker: بعض المفسرين
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p590/r10.anchor: وذكر بعض ا لمفسرين أن النكاح في القرآن على خمسة أوجه

IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p590/r11.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p590/r11.speaker: بعضهم
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p590/r11.claim: Some add a sixth sense: acceptance, as in the Prophet's marriage case in 33:50.
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p590/r11.anchor: وقد ألحق بعضهم وجها سادسا . فقال : والنكاح : القبول

IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p363/r1.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p363/r1.speaker: ابن فارس
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p363/r1.claim: Sarf means exceeding the proper limit.
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p363/r1.anchor: قال ابن فارس : السرف مجاوزة الحد

IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p363/r3.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p363/r3.speaker: ابن فارس
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p363/r3.claim: Sarif can describe an ignorant person.

IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p363/r4.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p363/r4.speaker: ابن فارس
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p363/r4.claim: Sarf can mean excessive appetite or eagerness; a hadith compares meat's sarf to wine's.
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p363/r4.anchor: والسرف الضراوة وفي الحديث : ' إن للحم سرفا كسرف الخمر '

IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p363/r5.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p363/r5.speaker: ابن فارس
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p363/r5.claim: Saraf is also the name of a place.

IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p363/r6.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p363/r6.speaker: بعض المفسرين
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p363/r6.claim: Here saraf means acting beyond what is required, specifically killing someone not legally liable to be killed; compare 17:33.
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p363/r6.anchor: وذكر بعض المفسرين أن السرف في القرآن على ستة أوجه : - أحدها : الخروج عما يجب

IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p363/r7.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p363/r7.speaker: بعض المفسرين
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p363/r7.claim: In this verse, saraf means unlawful consumption of orphan property.
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p363/r7.anchor: وذكر بعض المفسرين أن السرف في القرآن على ستة أوجه

IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p363/r8.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p363/r8.speaker: بعض المفسرين
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p363/r8.claim: Saraf means spending in sin in 25:67.
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p363/r8.anchor: وذكر بعض المفسرين أن السرف في القرآن على ستة أوجه

IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p363/r9.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p363/r9.speaker: بعض المفسرين
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p363/r9.claim: Saraf means declaring lawful things forbidden in 7:31.
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p363/r9.anchor: وذكر بعض المفسرين أن السرف في القرآن على ستة أوجه

IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p363/r10.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p363/r10.speaker: بعض المفسرين
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p363/r10.claim: Saraf means associating partners with God in 40:43.
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p363/r10.anchor: وذكر بعض المفسرين أن السرف في القرآن على ستة أوجه

IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p363/r11.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p363/r11.speaker: بعض المفسرين
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p363/r11.claim: Saraf means excess in sins in 39:53.
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p363/r11.anchor: وذكر بعض المفسرين أن السرف في القرآن على ستة أوجه

IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p574/r1.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p574/r1.speaker: author
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p574/r1.claim: Maʿruf derives from knowledge and, in law, denotes what the revealed law makes obligatory or recommended; its opposite is munkar.
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p574/r1.anchor: المعروف : اسم مشتق من المعرفة و [ هو ] في الشريعة عبارة عما كان عليه أمر الشرع من وجوب أو ندب

IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p574/r2.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p574/r2.speaker: author
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p574/r2.claim: ʿUrf can also mean a pleasant scent that identifies the thing from which it comes.
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p574/r2.anchor: والعرف : الرائحة الطيبة المعرفة لعنصر ما صدرت عنه

IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p574/r5.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p574/r5.speaker: أهل التفسير
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p574/r5.claim: Maʿruf means a loan or customary allowance in 4:6 and 4:114.
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p574/r5.anchor: وذكر أهل التفسير أن المعروف في القرآن على ثمانية أوجه

IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p258#2/r1.author: Ibn Qutayba
IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p258#2/r1.speaker: author
IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p258#2/r1.claim: Balāʾ basically means a test: the orphans are tested, and Abraham's command to sacrifice his son was a manifest test.
IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p258#2/r1.anchor: الاختبار، قال الله جل وعلا: وابتلوا اليتامى حتى إذا بلغوا النكاح

BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p218/r1.author: ʿĀʾisha ʿAbd al-Raḥmān (Bint al-Shāṭiʾ)
BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p218/r1.speaker: author
BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p218/r1.claim: Testing the orphans should produce reassuring confidence that they truly have sound judgment; the phrase means more than seeing outward, material signs of maturity at puberty.
BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p218/r1.anchor: ليس الإيناس هنا مجرد إبصار لظواهر الرشد المادية الحسية في سن البلوغ ولكنه الطمأنينة المؤنسة بالابتلاء والامتحان

BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p218/r3.author: ʿĀʾisha ʿAbd al-Raḥmān (Bint al-Shāṭiʾ)
BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p218/r3.speaker: author
BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p218/r3.claim: The Arabic sense of īnās is not a bare formal permission, and ānasa is unsuitable for seeing an enemy or fire or hearing thunder or a beast's roar.
BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p218/r3.anchor: ولا يسوغ في ذوق العربية أن يقال مثلاً: استأنس الرشطي، أو جابى الضرائب، أو الجائن

NASHR:v1p327/r1.author: Ibn al-Jazarī
NASHR:v1p327/r1.speaker: author
NASHR:v1p327/r1.claim: Length distinctions form a gradual scale from the shortest to the longest; the measurable element is the increment itself, learned through oral practice, imitation, and testing.
NASHR:v1p327/r1.anchor: وهذه الزيادة بعينها إن قدرت بألف أو بنصف ألف هي واحدة

NASHR:v1p327/r2.author: Ibn al-Jazarī
NASHR:v1p327/r2.speaker: أبو عمرو الداني
NASHR:v1p327/r2.claim: Al-Dani says reciters' differences follow their habits in articulation and reading speed; none exceeds ordinary Arabic or accepted recitation, and direct teaching clarifies the practice.
NASHR:v1p327/r2.anchor: ليس لواحد منهم مذهب يسرف فيه على غيره إسرافا يخرج عن المتعارف في اللغة والمتعالم في القراءة

NASHR:v1p327/r3.author: Ibn al-Jazarī
NASHR:v1p327/r3.speaker: author
NASHR:v1p327/r3.claim: Teachers may deliberately overtrain a student in precision, length, and articulation so the student lands on the permitted amount.
NASHR:v1p327/r3.anchor: ربما بالغ الأستاذ على المتعلم في التحقيق والتجويد والمد والتفكيك

NASHR:v1p327/r4.author: Ibn al-Jazarī
NASHR:v1p327/r4.speaker: حمزة
NASHR:v1p327/r4.claim: Hamza says he lengthens for a young student so the student reaches the intended meaning; the author explains this as correcting underperformance.
NASHR:v1p327/r4.anchor: سمعت حمزة يقول: إنما أزيد على الغلام في المد ليأتي بالمعنى

NASHR:v1p327/r5.author: Ibn al-Jazarī
NASHR:v1p327/r5.speaker: حمزة
NASHR:v1p327/r5.claim: Hamza warns against excess: beyond the natural limit is not recitation. The author says this second case corrects overperformance; Hamza also calls emphatic practice training for students.
NASHR:v1p327/r5.anchor: وما كان فوق القراءة فليس بقراءة

NASHR:v1p327/r6.author: Ibn al-Jazarī
NASHR:v1p327/r6.speaker: حمزة
NASHR:v1p327/r6.claim: When al-Thawri asked about Hamza's hamza, separation, and emphasis, Hamza answered that it was practice for the learner.
NASHR:v1p327/r6.anchor: قال الثوري لحمزة، وهو يقرئ: يا أبا عمارة

QURTUBI-FULL:20:11-12/r1.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:20:11-12/r1.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:20:11-12/r1.claim: In the cited 4:6 phrase, آنستم means you knew; آنست الصوت means I heard the sound.
QURTUBI-FULL:20:11-12/r1.anchor: أي علمتم. وآنست الصوت سمعته، والقبس شعلة من نار،
